BurpClass9617.java -- title "Proxy listeners" (:59), Add (:97), Edit (:105-106),
Remove (:114-115), remove-confirm (:162).

Per-listener dialog: proxyListenersConfigDialog, BurpClass3654.java:152,
titled "Add a new proxy listener" / "Edit proxy listener" (:154), four tabs:

  Binding (:789)          "Bind to address:" (:694), "Bind to port:" (:701),
                          "All interfaces" (:708), "Loopback only" (:715),
                          "Specific address:" (:760), plus the all-interfaces
                          confirmation at :312.
  Request handling (:882) "Support invisible proxying (enable only if needed)"
                          (:795), "Redirect to host:" (:825),
                          "Redirect to port:" (:810), "Force use of TLS" (:816).
  Certificate (:1023)     "Use a self-signed certificate" (:889),
                          "Generate CA-signed per-host certificates" (:898),
                          "Generate a CA-signed certificate with a specific
                          hostname:" (:907), "Use a custom certificate
                          (PKCS#12):" (:933) with File (:981) and Password (:987).
  TLS protocols           "Use the default protocols of your Java installation"
                          (:1049), "Use custom protocols" (:1058).

## burpsy-side evidence

pages/settings.tsx:370-393 -- the section titled "Proxy" is six read-only
<Metric> tiles. The listener is `stats.data?.proxy_bind` at :384. No input, no
mutation.

No mutation route exists. `grep -nE "api/proxy" internal/web/server.go` returns
exactly four handlers and nothing else:

  server.go:721  /api/proxy/ca
  server.go:722  /api/proxy/ca/import
  server.go:790  /api/proxy/passthrough
  server.go:791  /api/proxy/options

(Positive control: the same grep on the same file DOES find those four, so the
absence of a listener route is a real absence and not a grep artefact.)

pages/proxysettings.tsx is 140 lines end to end and contains only the six
response-modification switches plus outcome counters -- no binding, no
certificate, no redirect controls.

## Classification

CAPABILITY GAP.

## What an operator cannot do

Add a second listener; change the bind port or interface without restarting the
process with different flags; enable invisible proxying for a non-proxy-aware
client; set up a listener-level redirect; or present a custom PKCS#12 server
certificate.

## Shape of the work -- needs a decision first

burpsy today has ONE listener, created at startup from a flag, and the relay
holds it for the process lifetime. Burp's model is a mutable list. The decision
is which of these to build, and it should be made before any UI:

1. Make the single existing listener re-bindable at runtime (address, port,
   invisible-proxy flag). Small, and covers the common migration complaint.
2. A true listener list, which means the proxy owns N listeners with per-listener
   certificate and redirect policy -- a change in internal/proxy's shape, not a
   panel.

Prefer (1) first and file (2) separately if the multi-listener case is wanted;
the certificate tab in particular overlaps the existing CA surfaces in
settings.tsx (CaImportSection :1533, CertificateSection :1621) and should not be
duplicated per listener without deciding which is authoritative.
acceptance_criteria: A proxy listener's bind address and port can be changed from the console and the relay honours the change; invisible-proxy support is toggleable; the chosen scope (single re-bindable listener vs a listener list) is recorded as a decision on this issue before the panel is built.

title: logger: the tool log stores no request or response bytes, so there is no message viewer
description:
## Claim
The tool log records no request or response bytes, so the Logger page cannot show the request and response for a logged entry.

## Burp-side evidence
`BURP_SUITE_UI_UX_SPECIFICATION.md` §4.10 (Logger Tool):
> "Layout: Top = Unified traffic log table across all tools, Bottom = Request/Response dual-editor viewer."

`tools/logger/entries.html` ("Viewing requests and responses"):
> "You can view the request and response for each entry in the message editor and Inspector. Click on an entry to view these. They are read-only."

This is the tool's primary purpose per `tools/logger/index.html`: "Study the requests sent by any of Burp's tools or extensions […] Study the requests sent with a session handling rule modification."

## burpsy-side evidence
`internal/toollog/toollog.go:81-103` — the record is metadata only:
```go
type Entry struct {
    ID     uint64
    Tool   Tool
    Host   string
    Port   uint16
    TLS    bool
    Method string
    Path   string
    Status int
    ResponseLen *int
    StartedMs   uint64
    DurationMs  uint64
    Note        string
}
```
No request bytes, no response bytes.

The wire projection `toolLogEntry` (`internal/web/api_toolkit.go:835-854`) carries the same fields and nothing more.

The detail pane is consequently timings and error text only — `internal/web/ui/src/pages/logger.tsx:198-235` (`DetailList` rows: Sent, Authority, Path, Duration, Response length, Error).

The page states the limit itself at `internal/web/ui/src/pages/logger.tsx:26-32`:
> "The log stores a request line, not the bytes that were sent: no headers, no body."

and labels the context action accordingly ("Copy as curl (request line only)", `logger.tsx:369`).

## Classification
CAPABILITY GAP. The limit is disclosed in code comments and one menu label, but it is not a declined feature — the page presents itself as Burp's Logger and the disclosure does not restore the capability.

## Decision needed before code
Storing full bytes for every tool request has a memory cost that Burp manages with an explicit capture limit (default 50MB, `tools/logger/filter/capture.html`). Options:
1. Store bytes in the tool log with a byte-budget cap and an eviction counter, mirroring the existing `Dropped()` honesty pattern.
2. Store only an exchange id per entry and resolve bytes from the traffic store on demand, accepting that an evicted exchange yields an "unresolved" row — the pattern `internal/organizer` already uses.
3. Decline, and stop presenting the page as Logger.

Option 2 reuses machinery that exists and has a precedent for the unresolved-row state.

## What an operator cannot do
Read the request a session-handling rule or a match-and-replace rule actually put on the wire — the single most common reason to open Logger.
acceptance_criteria: Selecting a row in the Logger table shows the request and the response for that entry. If bytes are resolved from the traffic store rather than stored, an entry whose exchange was evicted renders an explicit unresolved state rather than an empty editor.

title: proxy settings: Sec-WebSocket-Extensions stripping has no UI control, though three shipped strings tell the operator to toggle it
description:
VERIFIED against HEAD by AuditProxy (Proxy-screen parity audit, 2026-08-27).

Three user-visible strings instruct the operator to toggle Sec-WebSocket-Extensions
stripping "in proxy options". No such control exists in any UI surface, and no API
route reaches it. The behaviour is settable only from Go at construction time.

## burpsy-side evidence: the switch

internal/proxy/proxy.go:547   stripWsExtensions bool          (struct field)
internal/proxy/proxy.go:570   stripWsExtensions: true,        (default)
internal/proxy/proxy.go:663   func (c *ProxyConfig) WithStripWsExtensions(strip bool) *ProxyConfig
internal/proxy/ws.go:140      if !s.config.stripWsExtensions {

`grep -rn "stripWsExtensions\|StripWsExtensions" --include=*.go internal/`
returns 12 hits, ALL inside internal/proxy and internal/core. No .tsx hit, no
route. Cross-checked against internal/proxy/options.go:43-62, which is the
COMPLETE OptionKeys enumeration -- 6 keys, none of them this one:
unhide_hidden_form_fields, remove_object_tags,
remove_javascript_form_validation, remove_all_javascript,
convert_https_links_to_http, strip_accept_encoding.

(Enumeration, not an absence-grep: the authority lists what exists, so the
omission is proven by presence of the full list.)

## burpsy-side evidence: the three strings that point at it

1. pages/intercept.tsx:781 -- shown in the WebSocket interception notice:
   "they only occur if you have turned off Sec-WebSocket-Extensions stripping
   in proxy options"

2. internal/core/websocket.go:527 -- rendered in the frame payload viewer:
   "Leave Sec-WebSocket-Extensions stripping enabled to capture this
   connection's messages in the clear."

3. internal/proxy/ws.go:166 -- recorded on the modified handshake in history:
   "Disable stripping for an origin that requires the extension -- compressed
   frames are then recorded with a note rather than decoded."

## Burp-side evidence

Burp exposes this as a checkbox in Proxy -> Miscellaneous: the panel's
search-keyword set at BurpClass9621.java:62 carries
"strip sec-websocket-extensions headers", alongside its siblings that each have
a real setText control in the same class. burpsy's own Go comment names Burp's
preference key: internal/core/websocket.go:590 cites
proxy.miscellaneous.strip_sec_websocket_extensions_headers_in_incoming_requests.

## Classification

CAPABILITY GAP, aggravated -- the inverse of a decorative control: UI prose
pointing at a widget that exists in no surface. This is not the generic
"Miscellaneous panel absent" claim of burpsy-react-ui-6s2; it is one specific
switch that three shipped strings already assume the operator can reach.

## What an operator cannot do

Proxy an origin that REQUIRES permessage-deflate: the handshake offer is
stripped unconditionally, the origin cannot negotiate the extension, and the
operator is told to go turn off a switch they will never find. Conversely they
cannot turn stripping ON if a future default flips it off.

## Shape of the work

Add strip_sec_websocket_extensions to proxy.OptionKeys so it rides the existing
/api/proxy/options route and renders in the existing proxysettings.tsx SWITCHES
table (pages/proxysettings.tsx:20-51) with no new plumbing. The three strings
above then become true.
acceptance_criteria: Sec-WebSocket-Extensions stripping is toggleable from Proxy settings and honoured by the relay without a restart; the three strings at intercept.tsx:781, core/websocket.go:527 and proxy/ws.go:166 name a control the operator can actually reach.

title: ui: rebinding a hotkey in Settings silently does nothing for 5 of the 10 rebindable actions
description:
## Claim
Settings -> Hotkeys accepts a rebind of Send to Repeater, Send to Intruder, Forward the held message, Toggle interception and Send the request in Repeater, runs duplicate detection on it, updates the shortcut modal — and the key that actually fires is unchanged. Five of the ten `rebindable: true` actions are installed as hardcoded literals that never read the keymap.

## Burp-side evidence
- `settings/ui/hotkeys.html` (Burp bundled docs): every listed command is editable via *"Double-click the command that you want to configure. Press the key combination that you want to assign. Click Apply."* Burp's table and Burp's bindings are the same object.

## burpsy-side evidence
Only `app.tsx` reads the registry. `grep -rn 'useChord(' --include=*.tsx burpsy-go/internal/web/ui/src/` returns app.tsx only (5 hits: `nav.palette`, `help.shortcuts`, `view.toggleTheme`, `nav.nextTool`, `nav.prevTool`).

Hardcoded literals, all declared `rebindable: true` in `lib/shortcuts.ts`:
- `pages/history.tsx:615` `useHotkeys("mod+r", ...)` vs `lib/shortcuts.ts:43` `send.repeater`
- `pages/history.tsx:626` `useHotkeys("mod+i", ...)` vs `lib/shortcuts.ts:44` `send.intruder`
- `pages/intercept.tsx:455` `useHotkeys("mod+f", ...)` vs `lib/shortcuts.ts:62` `proxy.forward`
- `pages/intercept.tsx:465` `useHotkeys("alt+t", ...)` vs `lib/shortcuts.ts:64` `proxy.toggleIntercept`
- `pages/repeater.tsx:147` `useHotkeys("mod+enter", ...)` vs `lib/shortcuts.ts:79` `repeater.send`

The editing surface is live and writes real state: `pages/settings.tsx:1266` HotkeysSection, `lib/keymap.ts:60` `setChord` -> localStorage + listener broadcast.

## Classification
CAPABILITY GAP. Note this also falsifies the file's own docstring, `lib/shortcuts.ts:18-20`: *"`rebindable: true` rows are dispatched from one place (app.tsx or a page's useHotkeys) against this registry, so changing one here changes what is installed."*

## What an operator cannot do
Rebind any of the five signature bindings. Worse than absence: the table reports success, so an operator who moves Send to Repeater off Ctrl+R (a reasonable thing to want, since Ctrl+R is browser reload) believes it moved and finds it did not.
acceptance_criteria: Each of send.repeater, send.intruder, proxy.forward, proxy.toggleIntercept and repeater.send is installed via useChord(<id>) against the keymap registry, so a chord changed in Settings -> Hotkeys changes the key that fires; verified by rebinding one and pressing the new chord.
close_reason: 63e101b8164900cbcd08697a60c61cda3dcab2d5. All five literals retired. send.repeater / send.intruder / send.organizer now install through useSendShortcuts (lib/actions.ts), which reads useChord against the registry; proxy.forward and proxy.toggleIntercept read useChord in pages/intercept.tsx; repeater.send reads useChord in pages/repeater.tsx. grep for useHotkeys(" with a literal chord returns nothing. Pinned structurally by src/lib/keymap-installed.test.ts, which asserts every rebindable id appears in a useChord("<id>") call in both directions and that the six retired literals never return, with a positive control on the corpus size. tsc --noEmit clean; bun test src/lib 151 pass / 0 fail. NOTE for the audit: the docstring at lib/shortcuts.ts:19-20 is now true as written.

comments.author: FixMenusHotkeys
comments.text:
SCOPE CORRECTION for the inventory (issue is closed and correctly closed; this is about the numbers in its title).

THE DENOMINATOR IS WRONG. There are 11 rebindable actions, not 10. Verified by importing the module rather than grepping — `REBINDABLE.length === 11`, and `SHORTCUT_ACTIONS.length === 24`. A `grep -c 'rebindable: true' lib/shortcuts.ts` returns 12, which is the trap: the twelfth hit is the docstring at lib/shortcuts.ts:19 quoting the flag name in prose. The eleven are send.repeater, send.intruder, send.organizer, proxy.forward, proxy.toggleIntercept, repeater.send, nav.palette, nav.nextTool, nav.prevTool, view.toggleTheme, help.shortcuts.

THE NUMERATOR IS ALSO WRONG, in the worse direction. Six of the eleven were inert, not five. The five this issue named were installed as literals; the sixth, send.organizer, was installed nowhere at all and was filed separately as burpsy-react-ui-zy6. Anyone reading the two issues side by side gets the right total, but this issue's title alone understates it. The honest headline is '6 of 11 rebindable hotkeys were inert'.

TWO CAUSES, NOT ONE — this matters for how the fix generalises.
1. Dispatch bypassed the registry (5 actions). Each was a page-local `useHotkeys("<literal>", ...)`. The keymap store worked perfectly: setChord wrote, persist stored, announce broadcast, useKeymap re-rendered, the Settings table re-read and reported success. Nothing was broken inside any module. The chord simply was not what any handler was registered against.
2. Dispatch did not exist (1 action). send.organizer had no call site of any kind.

ROOT CAUSE COMMON TO BOTH, and the reason this was able to ship: nothing tied the registry to the dispatch sites. The declaration lived in lib/shortcuts.ts, the store in lib/keymap.ts, and the handlers in five different page files, with no test and no type spanning them. Every unit was correct in isolation, which is exactly why unit tests could not have caught it and why the fix includes src/lib/keymap-installed.test.ts — a structural test over the source corpus asserting the wiring in both directions. That test is the durable part of this fix; the six call-site edits are not.

SCOPE ESTIMATE, if this had to be re-done from scratch: small. The store, the validation, the duplicate detection and the Settings UI were all already correct and needed no changes. The work was one 60-line hook, five call-site edits, and the structural test. Roughly a third of the effort was the test.

title: session: cookie jar is never populated from proxy traffic, though the page's empty state says it is
description:
## Claim
The session cookie jar is never populated from proxy traffic, and the Session page's empty-state copy tells the operator that it is.

## Burp-side evidence
`/root/burp-re/in/extract/resources/Documentation/burp/documentation/desktop/settings/sessions/index.html`:
> "Burp's cookie jar stores all of the cookies issued by websites you visit. The cookie jar is shared between all of Burp's tools. […] By default, the cookie jar is updated based on traffic from the Proxy."

The same page lists Proxy / Intruder / Scanner / Sequencer / Repeater / Extensions as individually selectable monitored tools, with Proxy on by default.

## burpsy-side evidence
`Coordinator.HandleResponse` — the only Set-Cookie absorption entry point — is `internal/session/session.go:954`, calling `jarMgr.AbsorbSetCookie` at `internal/session/session.go:957`.

Its complete set of non-test callers:
- `cmd/burpsy/cli_session.go:343`
- `internal/web/api_session.go:803` (the login-macro path)
- `internal/session/recovery.go:276`
- `internal/crawler/session_gate.go:261`

The proxy is not among them.

Absence-grep with same-directory positive control:
```
$ grep -rin cookie --include=*.go internal/proxy/
(no output)

$ for f in $(ls internal/proxy/*.go | grep -v _test); do printf "%s %s\n" "$(grep -c 'func ' $f)" "$f"; done
3 internal/proxy/alpn.go
5 internal/proxy/h2_relay.go
23 internal/proxy/options.go
53 internal/proxy/proxy.go
6 internal/proxy/tls_dial.go
3 internal/proxy/tls_peek.go
20 internal/proxy/ws.go
```
Every file in the package is greppable (113 funcs matched), so the zero-hit cookie grep is a real absence, not a NUL-byte read failure.

## The false copy
`internal/web/ui/src/pages/session.tsx:1021`, the empty-jar detail text:
> "The jar is attached and empty: no Set-Cookie has been absorbed yet. Run a login macro, or **send authenticated traffic through the proxy**."

The first clause is true. The second describes a code path that does not exist. This is the part worth fixing first even if the absorption work is scheduled later — the copy currently sends the operator to do something that cannot work.

## Classification
CAPABILITY GAP, plus a false disclosure in shipped UI copy.

## What an operator cannot do
Browse the target logged-in through the proxy and have subsequent tool requests carry the session — the jar stays empty while the UI says their browsing should have filled it.
acceptance_criteria: A response passing through the proxy with a Set-Cookie header results in that cookie appearing in GET /api/session/cookies, covered by a test that drives a response through the proxy path rather than calling HandleResponse directly. If proxy absorption is deliberately declined instead, session.tsx:1021 no longer tells the operator to send traffic through the proxy.
close_reason: Fixed in d44f352. proxy.ProxyConfig.WithCookieJar attaches the session coordinator and Server.record absorbs every Set-Cookie from the raw response bytes - the single funnel all capture sites in internal/proxy go through (HTTP/1, h2 relay, WS handshake). Coordinator.AbsorbResponseCookies takes bytes rather than a header map because HandleResponse's map[string]string can hold only ONE of a response's Set-Cookie lines - a defect the audit did not mention and which affected every existing absorption call site. Wired in cmd/burpsy/main.go:438. The disclosure was NOT the bug: the copy is now true. Second half per the house standard - the coordinator records absorption sources and counts responses/Set-Cookies offered, and /api/session/cookies projects absorbing_from, responses_observed, set_cookies_absorbed with a three-branch empty hint (nothing feeds the jar / nothing has arrived / N arrived and carried none). Those were one indistinguishable state, which is how the false advice shipped. Mutation: removing the absorb call in record() fails TestProxiedTrafficFillsTheSessionCookieJar (real traffic through a real listener); narrowing hdr.Values to hdr.Get fails TestAbsorbResponseCookiesTakesEverySetCookieLine 'absorbed 1 Set-Cookie lines, want 2'. UI half open: session.tsx:1021 copy is now accurate, and the three new fields let the page distinguish the three states.

comments.author: FixBackendTruth
comments.text:
SCOPE NOTE for the inventory (issue is closed/done, this is calibration).

Roughly 2x the filed scope, and the extra half was not visible from the audit's evidence.

The audit's fix — 'call the absorption entry point from the proxy' — was one line and correct. Two things it could not have seen made it bigger:

1. Coordinator.HandleResponse, the entry point the audit identified, takes 'hdrs map[string]string'. A map keyed by header name cannot hold a response's Set-Cookie headers: a login that sets a session cookie AND a CSRF cookie sends two lines and the map holds one. So wiring the proxy to that entry point would have shipped a jar that silently drops half of every real login. That forced a new bytes-taking method (AbsorbResponseCookies + a textproto head parse) rather than a call to the existing one. This is a LATENT DEFECT IN ALL FOUR PRE-EXISTING CALLERS (cli_session.go:343, web/api_session.go:803, session/recovery.go:276, crawler/session_gate.go:261) — they each build that map themselves from an already-parsed response, so the loss happens before HandleResponse is entered and is invisible at those sites. NOT FIXED by me; those paths still use the map. Possibly worth its own issue.

2. The house standard on empty-vs-unmeasured made the honest half comparable in size to the fix. Absorbing cookies makes session.tsx:1021's copy true, but an empty jar still rendered identically to a jar nothing watches. That needed absorption-source registration plus two counters on the Coordinator and a three-branch hint on /api/session/cookies.

WHERE THE FIX LANDED, which the audit did not specify: not at a per-protocol capture site but in proxy.Server.record — the single funnel every capture site in the package goes through (HTTP/1, the h2 relay's rendered copy, the WebSocket handshake). One call covers all three and a site added later inherits it. Worth knowing for any future 'hook the proxy path' issue: record() is the seam.

REMAINING (UI, not mine): session.tsx:1021 copy is now accurate as written, so no edit is strictly required — but the page cannot yet distinguish the three states the API now reports (absorbing_from empty / responses_observed 0 / N observed and none carried a cookie). Small: read three new fields, pick one of three strings.

title: history: the three Search modifier checkboxes have no search field and are applied to the DSL query box
description:
VERIFIED against HEAD by AuditProxy (Proxy-screen parity audit, 2026-08-27).

DECORATIVE CONTROL. The three "Search modifiers" checkboxes in HTTP history's

     -> sent to the server as the typed query DSL.

  2. pages/history.tsx:481-503  the `searchMatcher` memo, built from
     `debouncedTerm` and the three checkbox states (searchCase :380,
     searchRegex :381, searchNegate :382).

The matcher is then applied client-side at pages/history.tsx:578-586 against

  `${row.method} ${row.host} ${row.path} ${row.mime ?? ""} ${row.notes ?? ""}`

There is no handler to reach: the checkbox values are consumed entirely inside
the component and never appear in a request body. Nothing on the Go side reads
them.

## What the operator gets

With the box holding its documented content -- a DSL expression, per the
placeholder -- the three controls are worse than absent:

* "Regular expression" (:1156) compiles `host ~ "api" and status = 200` as a
  RegExp (:489) and tests it against the row fields. It matches nothing, the
  table empties, and the status line at :1103-1107 reports
  `no match for search` for a search the operator never typed.

* "Negative match" (:1157-1161) alone inverts a predicate that is false for
  every row (`hit === searchNegate`, :585), so every row is kept: a silent
  no-op that still adds "search (inverted)" to activeFilterNames (:529).

* "Case sensitive" (:1155) behaves as labelled only when the box holds a bare
  word rather than a query.

The hint at :1165-1169 documents which FIELDS are searched and never states
WHICH STRING is searched, so nothing on screen discloses the collision.

Checked and NOT the bug: the branch at :483-486 is convoluted but correct for
every combination -- case-only and negate-only both reach the plain substring
matcher. The defect is the shared input, not the predicate.

## Burp-side evidence

proxyHttpSearchCaseSensitiveCheckbox, proxyHttpSearchRegexCheckbox,
proxyHttpSearchNegativeMatchCheckbox -- all three declared in BurpClass9693.java
(/root/burp-re/out/ui_report/setname_inventory.tsv). In Burp they modify a
DEDICATED search field inside the filter popover, separate from every other
filter control. Burp has no combined filter-expression/search input.

## Classification

CAPABILITY GAP (no search field exists) with an active correctness failure.

## What an operator cannot do

Search history by substring or regex at all -- and if they tick the modifiers
while a DSL query is in the box, the table empties and blames a filter they
never set.

## Shape of the work

Add the search field the modifiers belong to, as a second input in the popover
next to the three checkboxes, leaving the top-bar box as the DSL statement.
Renaming the labels instead would leave a control that still empties the table.
acceptance_criteria: History has a search input distinct from the DSL query box; Case sensitive / Regular expression / Negative match apply only to that input; a DSL query in the top-bar box is unaffected by the three checkboxes; an invalid regex is reported in place rather than emptying the table.

title: ui: the message editor has no context menu and no Actions menu — no send-to from inside a request or response
description:
## Claim
Right-clicking inside a request or response pane in burpsy opens the browser's own menu. There is no burpsy context menu and no "Actions" button anywhere in the message editor, so every send-to / copy / scope action must be reached from the table row above instead.

## Burp-side evidence
- `tools/message-editor/index.html` (Burp 2026.7.1 bundled docs, in `/root/burp-re/in/extract/resources/Documentation/burp/documentation/desktop/`), Raw tab: *"You can access a wide range of context-specific actions for both requests and responses either from the **Actions** menu or by **right-clicking anywhere on the relevant message**."*
- `tools/proxy/intercept-messages.html`: *"You can also right-click to access different context menus in the message editor, or the list of intercepted messages."*
- `tools/context-menu.html` is the canonical universal item list; Burp applies it to editors as well as tables.
- Spec `BURP_SUITE_UI_UX_SPECIFICATION.md` section 5.1: the Send-To matrix is *"Invoked via Right-Click on any HTTP Message editor or History table row"*.

## burpsy-side evidence
- `burpsy-go/internal/web/ui/src/ui/editor.tsx` — absence grep `grep -c ContextMenu ui/editor.tsx` -> **0**. Same-file positive control: `grep -c import ui/editor.tsx` -> **14**. `file ui/editor.tsx` -> `JavaScript source, Unicode text, UTF-8 text` (no NUL byte, so the ugrep/NUL trap does not apply).
- `ui/editor.tsx:212,223` declares an `actions?: ReactNode` toolbar slot. **No caller passes it**: `grep -rn -A9 '<HttpEditor' pages/ ui/ | grep 'actions='` exits 1 across all 21 `<HttpEditor>` usages (`grep -rn '<HttpEditor' pages/ ui/ | wc -l` -> 21).
- The editor toolbar is Wrap / Copy / Save only (`ui/editor.tsx:323-344`).
- The components needed already exist: `ui/menu.tsx:54` `ContextMenu({groups, children})` and `lib/actions.ts:782-834` `menu(exchange, extra)` returning `MenuGroup[]`.

## Classification
CAPABILITY GAP.

## What an operator cannot do
Read a response in the History or Repeater detail pane, right-click it, and send it to Repeater / Intruder / Comparer, copy its URL or curl, or add its host to scope — the highest-frequency gesture in Burp. The selection codecs bound in the editor keymap (`ui/editor.tsx:143-170`, Burp's "Convert selection") are likewise reachable only by keystroke, with no menu entry to discover them from.
acceptance_criteria: Right-clicking anywhere in a request or response pane in History, Repeater, Site map and Intercept opens burpsy's own menu carrying the exchange actions from lib/actions.ts menu(); the same groups are also reachable from a visible Actions control in the editor toolbar.
close_reason: 63e101b8164900cbcd08697a60c61cda3dcab2d5. HttpEditor takes a menuGroups prop and renders the groups in two places: a right-click ContextMenu on the message body (Radix Trigger asChild, so no wrapper element is added to the editor-shell grid) and a visible Actions button in the toolbar via DropdownMenu. Wired with useExchangeActions().menu(exchange) on History (both panes), Site map (both panes), Scanner advisory (both panes), the WebSocket handshake pair, Repeater (keyed on result.exchange_id, since a draft is not an exchange until sent), and Intercept (its own heldMenu, because a held message has no exchange). Also closes the second half of the acceptance criteria: Burp's Convert-selection codecs are now menu entries running the same transformSelection path as the ctrl+U/H/B chords, each row showing its chord, plus Find-in-message. They are enabled/disabled off a real CodeMirror updateListener rather than a render-time read, so the disabled state is not a lie. The Render view keeps the browser's own menu on purpose - it is a sandboxed attacker-controlled iframe. tsc --noEmit clean.

comments.author: FixMenusHotkeys
comments.text:
SCOPE ANSWER for the inventory: pf9 was SMALLER than it looks, and it bought more than it asked for. Numbers, since the issue's own census was the thing that made it look big.

THE 21 CALL SITES WERE A RED HERRING. The issue counts 21 `<HttpEditor>` usages (22 now) and observes that none passes `actions`, which reads as 21 places to fix. It is not. The fix is ONE prop on ONE component plus a per-page lookup of the exchange, and only 11 of the 22 sites have an exchange to look up:

  wired (11): history x2, sitemap x2, scanner x2, wshistory handshake x2, repeater x2, intercept x1
  correctly not wired (11): decoder 1, comparer 1, session 1, sequencer 2, matchreplace 2, intruder 2, wshistory frame payload 2

The second group is not a backlog. Those panes hold a token list, a paste buffer, a match/replace preview, a synthesised payload — there is no exchange behind them, so there is no send-to that would not be fabricated. An engineer picking this up should not budget for 22.

IT ALSO FIXED editor.* FOR FREE, WHICH THE ISSUE ONLY MENTIONS IN PASSING. The last line of the issue's evidence notes the selection codecs are 'reachable only by keystroke, with no menu entry to discover them from'. That turned out to be the cheaper and arguably higher-value half: the codec entries live INSIDE HttpEditor, so they need no caller cooperation at all, and every one of the 22 editors now has a right-click menu and an Actions button carrying URL/HTML/Base64 encode+decode and Find-in-message, each row displaying its chord so the menu teaches the keyboard. That includes all 11 editors with no exchange — the Sequencer's token pane and the Decoder's input got the most useful thing in this commit and are not mentioned anywhere in the issue.

ONE THING THAT WAS HARDER THAN IT LOOKS, worth knowing before anyone touches this again: the codec entries' enabled/disabled state cannot be read when the menu is built. `groups` is a prop evaluated at render, not a callback invoked on open, so a selection made after that render would leave every codec row stale — enabled and doing nothing, or disabled and refusing to. It needs a real `EditorView.updateListener` pushing selection-emptiness into React state. Anyone 'simplifying' that back to a direct `cmViewRef.current.state.selection` read reintroduces the bug silently, because the menu still looks right.

AND ONE TRAP AVOIDED: the Actions trigger is a bare `<button>`, not the codebase's `IconButton`. IconButton wraps its button in a Radix Tooltip, so using it would stack two `asChild` layers on one DOM node and merge two sets of handlers onto it. app.tsx's menu bar uses a bare button for the same reason. Noted in the code.

REVISED SIZE: small-to-medium, and it is a single shared fix, not 21. The P1 is justified on frequency, not on cost.

title: auditqueue: "Show insertion points" only ever expands the first row
description:
## Claim

The Audit queue's "Show insertion points" button only ever expands the **first** row. For every other
item in the queue it appears to do nothing, so an operator reads "no insertion points were recorded"
where the truth is "this control cannot show you them".

## burpsy side

`burpsy-go/internal/web/ui/src/pages/auditqueue.tsx:122`

    onClick={() => setExpanded(expanded === null ? (d.items[0]?.seq ?? null) : null)}

`expanded` is a single `number | null` (`:28`), and the render gate is
`expanded === item.seq && item.insertion_points?.length` (`:101`). The button is page-level, in
`toolbar-end` below the table (`:118-126`) — there is no per-row toggle and no way to reach
`d.items[1]` or later. The label is unconditional ("Show insertion points"), so it does not disclose
that it means row 1.

The data is present for every row: `item.insertion_points` is per-item on the wire
(`lib/data.auditqueue.ts`), carrying `kind`, `name`, `status`, `detail`.

## Burp side

`auditItemsTableInsertionPointsViewToggle` is **per row** in Burp's Audit items table — `map_root.tsv`
class `burp.Zub5` (`auditItemsTableInsertionPointsViewToggle`, `Insertion points`) and `burp.Zrz9`
(`auditItemsTableInsertionPointsView`). The tree it opens is scoped to the selected item
(`burp.Zr_x`: `auditItemsTableInsertionPointsName`, `auditItemsTableInsertionPointsStatusText`).

## Classification

CAPABILITY GAP, and specifically a wrong-result one: the control silently under-reports rather than
refusing.

## What an operator cannot do

Find out which insertion points the audit chose, or why one was skipped, on any queue item except the
first — which is the question the Audit queue exists to answer.
acceptance_criteria: Insertion points can be expanded for any row in the queue independently (per-row toggle or multi-select expansion state), verified on a queue with 2+ items where a later item has insertion points.
close_reason: Done in 6d0b20e. The page-level button is gone; each row now has its own toggle. The old handler was setExpanded(expanded === null ? (d.items[0]?.seq ?? null) : null) — it could only ever reach d.items[0], and because the render gate is 'expanded === item.seq && item.insertion_points?.length', clicking it on any other row produced no change and read as 'no insertion points recorded' rather than 'this control cannot show you them'. On a queue whose stated purpose is that bounded work is reported and never dropped, that was silent under-reporting, which is why P1 was right. The new button carries its own count so the number is visible without expanding, and a row with zero points gets it DISABLED rather than hidden — hiding it would leave an operator unable to tell 'this item recorded none' from 'this item has some and the toggle is broken again', which is the exact confusion being fixed. The expanded panel also now names which seq it belongs to, since with a per-row toggle there is more than one row it could have come from. tsc clean. dist/app.js deliberately not rebuilt yet: three agents are mid-flight on other files and I rebuild once when they land, so this does not reach a browser until then.

title: scanner: only 4 of Burp's 78 scan-config keys exist; insertion points and check selection are unrepresentable
description:
burpsy's `scanner.BuiltInConfig` has **4 knobs**. Burp's 29 shipped configurations set **78
functional leaf keys across 15 sections**. That is **4/78 (5%)**, spanning **2/15 sections**.

## Re-derived, not inherited

`docs/parity/W0-burp-denominators.md` states it was reconstructed and not re-derived. I re-derived it
from `/root/burp-re/in/extract/resources/BuiltInConfigs` (29 files, confirmed):

| Figure | W0 said | Re-derived | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| BuiltInConfigs files | 29 | 29 | confirmed |
| total leaf keys | 83 | 84 | off by one |
| `description.*` metadata | 6 | 6 | confirmed |
| functional keys | 77 | **78** | corrected |
| sections | 20 | **15** | W0 overstated by 5 |

Use 78 and 15. The conclusion is unchanged and the correction is small, but the numbers get quoted.

## The two sections that are entirely unrepresentable

**`scanner/insertion_point_types` — 8 keys.** Controls WHERE the scanner injects:

    insert_url_params, insert_body_params, insert_cookies, insert_http_headers,
    insert_param_name, insert_url_path_filename, insert_url_path_folders, insert_entire_body

**`scanner/issues_reported` — 9 keys.** Controls WHICH checks run:

    scan_type_passive, scan_type_light_active, scan_type_medium_active,
    scan_type_intrusive_active, scan_type_javascript_analysis,
    scan_only_selected_issues, select_individual_issues, selected_issues,
    store_issues_within_queue_items

A scanner whose insertion points and check selection cannot be expressed is not a configurable
scanner. This is the single largest capability gap on the Burp side of the comparison, and it is not
a UI gap — there is no field to bind a control to.

## What burpsy's 4 keys cover

`ConsecutiveCheckFailuresToAbandonUnit`, `ConsecutiveUnitFailuresToFailItem`,
`PauseSessionAfterFailedItems` land in `scanner/error_handling` (5 keys); `MaximumAuditTimeMinutes` is
`scanner/audit_optimization/maximum_crawl_and_audit_time` (7 keys). Every one was verified present in
Burp's JSON — the transcription is honest, it is just tiny.

Note what `error_handling` is missing even within a section burpsy touches:
`number_of_follow_up_passes` and `pause_task_failed_audit_item_percentage`.

## Why this is P1 and should be split

Do NOT take this as one task. `issues_reported` is the higher value half: `settings.tsx` already has
~21 audit-check-family switches wired to `ScanConfig`, so burpsy has *a* check-selection mechanism —
it is simply not Burp's shipped vocabulary and cannot load a Burp configuration. Reconciling those two
is a smaller, well-defined job than building insertion-point control from nothing.

`insertion_point_types` is the deeper one: it needs the audit engine to be told which insertion point
classes to enumerate, which touches `internal/scanner`'s point generation rather than a config struct.

## Constraint inherited from the existing code

`builtInConfigKeys` is deliberately the single description of what a shipped configuration can change,
read by both `Apply` and `BuiltInConfig.Keys` so a chooser can tell an operator what each config does.
Any new key must go through that table, not around it.
acceptance_criteria: scanner/issues_reported and scanner/insertion_point_types are representable, a Burp-shipped configuration can be loaded without silently dropping keys, and builtInConfigKeys remains the single description of what a config changes.

title: intercept: right-click Forward/Drop act on the previously selected message
description:
`burpsy-go/internal/web/ui/src/pages/intercept.tsx` (~line 617) gives the held-message table a
right-click menu whose Forward and Drop items act on the *previously selected* message, not the one
the operator right-clicked.

## The code

```tsx
menuGroups={(row) => [{ id: "intercept", actions: [
  { id: "forward", label: "Forward", icon: Send, shortcut: "Ctrl+F",
    onSelect: () => { setSelectedId(row.id); setTimeout(forward, 0); } },
  { id: "drop", label: "Drop", icon: Trash2, danger: true,
    onSelect: () => { setSelectedId(row.id); setTimeout(drop, 0); } },
]}]}
```

`forward` is defined at line 400 and closes over `selected` (line 376, derived from `selectedId`) and
over `raw`, the edit buffer. `setSelectedId` schedules a state update; it does not rewrite the
`forward` function that already exists. `setTimeout` then re-invokes *that same closure*, so it still
reads the pre-click `selected` and the pre-click `raw`.

## Three distinct failures

1. **Wrong message forwarded.** Right-click a held message that is not the current selection, pick
   Forward: the previously selected message is forwarded, and the success toast names that one
   ("Held message #N forwarded"), so the log agrees with the wrong outcome.

2. **Silent no-op.** With nothing selected yet, `if (!selected) return` at line 401 makes the item do
   nothing at all — no error, no toast.

3. **Wrong payload, which is the serious one.** `raw` is the edit buffer belonging to the *old*
   selection. The effect that resets it (lines 380-383) keys on `selectedId` and runs after commit,
   so the stale closure sends the previous message's bytes as this message's payload. An operator who
   had been editing message A and right-click-forwards message B sends A's edited bytes to B's
   destination.

`drop` (line 414) has the same stale-closure problem, without the payload hazard: it drops the
previously selected message.

## Why this is P1 rather than P2

This is the interception surface. Its whole purpose is that the operator controls exactly which bytes
reach the server, and "the control acted on a message other than the one you pointed at, and told you
it succeeded" defeats that. It also cannot be caught by reading the toast, because the toast reports
the action that actually happened.

## Fix

`setTimeout(…, 0)` is the signal, not the fix — it is there because the author noticed state was not
applied yet. Do not wait for state; pass the target explicitly. Extract the id-taking forms:

```tsx
const forwardMessage = (id: number, body: string) => { … };
const dropMessage = (id: number) => { … };
```

and have both the existing buttons and the menu items call those. The menu item then needs to decide
what `body` means for a row that is not the selected one — the honest answer is the row's own
unedited `raw`, since there is no edit buffer for it.

## Verification

`npx tsc --noEmit` is exit 0. The `onActivate` additions on the same two `VirtualTable` pages are
correct and match `table.tsx:435`; only the `setTimeout` handlers are affected.
acceptance_criteria: Right-clicking an unselected held message and choosing Forward forwards THAT message's id and bytes; with nothing previously selected it still works; a test covers forward-from-menu on a row other than the current selection.
close_reason: Done in ecfe2bd. DustyCanyon's extraction was the right fix — forwardMessage(id, body, fixCL) and dropMessage(id) taking their target explicitly instead of closing over selected/raw — and that is what landed, reapplied onto HEAD's formatting so the ~600-line reindentation it arrived wrapped in did not land with it. git diff and git diff -w on the file are now identical at 63 lines: every changed line is a real change. Their working copy is preserved (scratchpad/intercept.tsx.dustycanyon-worktree-1657, sha256 72d2397b1fc3) and the substitution was announced in msg 1517 before the operator authorised the takeover. Also fixed the regression their version carried: fixContent_length was dropped by JSON.stringify so the handler decoded FixContentLength as false and Content-Length correction was silently off for EVERY forward, including the toolbar path that worked before; and the menu hardcoded true where the operator's toggle belonged, which would have had two forward paths disagreeing about whether they rewrite a header. The menu passes row.raw, not the edit buffer, deliberately: there is no edit buffer for an unselected row. tsc clean tree-wide; full suite exit 0, 37 packages.

title: discover: the ffuf content-discovery engine has no console surface
description:
VERIFIED, and sharper than the original issue. The original said 'No content discovery functionality' and 'Discover tab is docs only'. Both halves were wrong in opposite directions.

WHAT EXISTS: ffuf-backed content discovery is fully built in Go — internal/extscan/ffuf.go, internal/web/api_discovery.go, the /api/discovery route registered at internal/web/server.go:817, discoveryRuns state at server.go:102-104, and tests in api_discovery_test.go and route_manifest_test.go. It is reachable from the CLI (cmd/burpsy/cli_extscan.go).

WHAT IS MISSING: nothing in the console calls it. `grep -rn 'api/discovery' internal/web/ui/src` returns zero hits. An operator using the web console cannot launch a content-discovery run, see one in progress, or read its results.

WHY discover.tsx IS NOT THE GAP: the original conflated two different Burp features. Burp's DISCOVER *tab* is a links farm (Web Security Academy, manual, videos, forum); burpsy replaced it with a reference hub deliberately, and discover.tsx's module doc argues that case at length. Burp's 'Discover content' is a separate engagement tool reached by right-clicking a target. This issue is about the second one. Do not 'fix' it by changing discover.tsx into a links page.

WHY P1: this is the same failure class as matchreplace-never-wired — a complete engine, tests passing, reported as delivered, that no user can reach. Backend coverage is exactly what makes it invisible.
acceptance_criteria: A console surface can start an ffuf discovery run against a chosen target, shows it running, and renders its results; the route appears in dist/app.js as well as server.go.
close_reason: Done in 03ae0b7. Added lib/data.discovery.ts (typed wire shapes + useDiscoveryRuns/useStartDiscovery), pages/contentdiscovery.tsx, and a Content discovery leaf under Target next to the site map — where Burp opens 'Discover content' from — leaving pages/discover.tsx untouched, since the two Burp features only share a word. The page renders looked, outcome, counts.out_of_scope and the server's verbatim summary, so 'swept and found nothing' and 'never swept' get different panels; the argv is shown per run because these requests bypass burpsy and appear in no history row; and when ffuf is not allowlisted the reason replaces the form rather than showing an empty table. Also added internal/web/ui_route_reachability_test.go, the gate that would have caught this class: every manifest route's path must appear in the console source, with uiRouteExempt (reasons) and uiRouteMissingSurface (issue ids) and a third test that fails if a listed gap gains a caller. Its first run found /api/intercept/drop-all, filed as burpsy-react-ui-t6f. NOTE: the first version of that test passed its own mutation test because it matched the route named in a doc comment; comments are now stripped and the mutation test verified red-on-mutation, green-on-restore. NOT rebuilt: dist/app.js, because another agent has five UI files uncommitted — the page is source-only and reaches no browser until someone rebuilds.

title: WS fragment reassembly not supported
description:
## What's missing
wsHoldable() refuses fragmented frames (FIN clear / continuation opcode). Burp reassembles fragments.

## Evidence
- internal/proxy/ws.go:410-431 — wsHoldable() documentation states this gap
- wsHoldable() returns false for fragments

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Buffer continuation frames until FIN
- [ ] Hold complete reassembled message
- [ ] Apply match/replace to reassembled payload

Found by: BlueBison (code grep ws.go:410)
close_reason: Done in c3de955: wsFragments reassembles continuation frames so a multi-frame message can be held, edited and dropped as one message. Control frames still interleave per RFC 6455 s5.4; RSV1 tracked only on a message's first frame per s6.1. Tests in internal/proxy/ws_*_test.go. Verified present in HEAD; full suite exit 0, 37 packages.

title: WS match/replace rules not implemented
description:
## What's missing
WebSocket match/replace rules. HTTP match/replace exists (internal/matchreplace/) but no WS-specific rule engine.

## Evidence
- internal/matchreplace/ — only HTTP request/response rules
- internal/proxy/ws.go:wsHoldable() — refuses compressed/fragmented frames
- No WS match/replace API endpoint in internal/web/

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] WS frame payload matching (literal + regex)
- [ ] WS frame payload replacement
- [ ] API endpoint for WS match/replace rules
- [ ] UI: Match & Replace tab → WebSocket section

Found by: BlueBison (code grep)
close_reason: Done in 6e98c74: matchreplace gained TargetWebSocketToServer/ToClient and DirWebSocketToServer/ToClient, applied in the relay via wsMatchReplaceDirection, ordered BEFORE interception to mirror proxy.go. The if-chain in targetsDir was replaced with a sentinel-sized table so a new target cannot silently fall into the else branch; fixContentLength is skipped for WS directions. Note: without the wsNeedsFrames change in the same commit, WS rules would have installed, reported success and rewritten nothing.

title: dashboard: 'Crawl and audit' and 'API-only scan' scan types are disabled ('not built yet') — only a bare Crawl can be launched, so Burp's primary crawl+audit workflow is unavailable
description:
## Burp-side evidence
dashboard/ (New scan) — Burp's New scan dialog offers "Crawl and audit" (the default, maps the surface then audits it) and "Crawl" and API scans. Crawl-and-audit is Burp's primary scanning workflow: point it at a seed and it both maps and audits in one bounded task.

## burpsy-side evidence
internal/web/ui/src/pages/dashboard.tsx:341-345 defines SCAN_TYPES with crawl-audit ready:false and api ready:false; only "crawl" is ready:true. The cards for Crawl-and-audit and API-only scan render disabled with "not built yet" (dashboard.tsx:387), and NewScanModal only submits a crawl via useStartCrawl (dashboard.tsx:356-368). A bounded crawl-and-audit against a seed cannot be launched at all — auditing is only available as the always-on live sweep over proxied traffic. title: session: cannot record a macro from Proxy history — macro steps are hand-typed only
description:
## Burp-side evidence

title: session: macros are hand-typed — no Macro Recorder / add-from-history / send-to-macro
description:
## Burp-side evidence
settings/sessions/macros.html: "Macros are made up of requests taken from the Proxy history... Click Add to open the Macro Recorder dialog. Select the items you need from the Proxy history list. If required, you can use Burp's browser to add new requests." And a context-menu "Send to macro" exists anywhere in Burp.

## burpsy-side evidence
session.tsx StepCard (333-407) builds each macro step from hand-typed method/URL/HeaderPairs/body/extractions; there is no Macro Recorder, no "add request from history", and no "Send to Sequencer/macro"-style handoff into the rule editor. A login macro must be transcribed by hand rather than captured from observed traffic. Relates to burpsy-react-ui-fhp (no Send to Sequencer) and burpsy-react-ui-868 (send-to gaps).
close_reason: duplicate of burpsy-react-ui-escl (created by a fork that re-ran this cluster; canonical bead kept)

title: scanner: findings cannot be re-triaged — no set-severity, set-confidence, delete-issue or mark-false-positive; /api/issues is GET-only
description:
## Burp-side evidence
tools/intruder/results/analyzing-results.html and the scanner issue view describe the issue context menu: "Set severity", "Set confidence", "Report issue", "Delete issue", and marking a false positive / "Highlight a result". An analyst routinely down-grades a tentative finding, marks a false positive, or deletes noise.

## burpsy-side evidence
internal/web/ui/src/pages/scanner.tsx:359-365 documents that Set severity, Set confidence and Delete issue are deliberately absent because "/api/issues is registered GET-only (internal/web/server.go:727) — there is no PATCH to move a severity or a confidence onto a finding, and no DELETE to remove one." The issue leaf context menu (menuForLeaf, scanner.tsx:376-454) therefore offers only go-to, copy, and whole-scan report exports. There is no false-positive flag either.

## Note
scanner.tsx says this is "Tracked on burpsy-react-ui-3fr", but 3fr's title is about tables lacking a right-click menu at all — and the Issues tree now HAS a context menu (scanner.tsx:529). This bead captures the real remaining gap: the issue-mutation endpoints (PATCH severity/confidence, DELETE, false-positive) do not exist. Relate to 3fr.

title: scope: no 'Drop all out-of-scope requests' — burpsy will still issue requests to out-of-scope hosts
description:
## Burp-side evidence
`settings/project/scope.html` — "Out-of-scope request handling: Select **Drop all out-of-scope
requests** to prevent Burp from issuing any out-of-scope requests. With this setting enabled,
out-of-scope outgoing requests are dropped by Burp even if the browser explicitly requests them. You
can select how Burp defines an out-of-scope request: Use suite scope / Use custom scope." This is a
safety control that stops burp from ever touching hosts you have no permission to test.

## burpsy-side evidence
burpsy has no such control. The Scope page (`burpsy-go/internal/web/ui/src/pages/scope.tsx`, whole
file, 220 lines) offers only include/exclude rule add/remove/clear — no out-of-scope request handling
section. A backend search finds no drop-out-of-scope setting: `grep -rin "out.of.scope|DropOutOfScope"
internal/**/*.go` returns only scanner/passive gating counters and organizer scope resolution, none of
which prevent an out-of-scope request from being issued. (Distinct from am6, which is about not
*logging* out-of-scope traffic; this is about not *sending* it.) So an operator cannot make burpsy
refuse to issue requests to out-of-scope hosts — the accidental-attack guardrail Burp provides.

title: intruder: no Recursive grep payload type — a payload cannot be derived from the previous response, so token-following and recursive enumeration are impossible
description:
## Burp-side evidence
tools/intruder/configure-attack/payload-types.html — "Recursive grep: This enables you to extract text from the response to the previous request, and use it as the payload for the current request." Settings: Initial payload for first request, Extract grep item, Stop if duplicate payload found; must use a resource pool with max concurrent 1. Core mechanism for following dependent values (CSRF tokens, sequential DB enumeration).

## burpsy-side evidence
Payload types offered in internal/web/ui/src/pages/intruder.tsx:1060-1066 are exactly: list, numbers, file, brute_force, dates, custom_iterator, null. Recursive grep is not among them, and the backend payload_sources union (intruder.tsx:780-804) has no "recursive_grep" case. There is no way to derive a payload from the previous response.

title: intruder: no attack window — the UI runs a blocking attack with no live results and no pause/resume/stop, though the backend has all three
description:
## Burp-side evidence
tools/intruder/results/viewing-results.html + editing-attacks: "You can view details of every request and response issued in the attack in the results window ... adjusting the attack configuration while the attack is running". Burp's attack runs asynchronously in a results window with a live-updating results table and a manual pause / resume / stop control; results stream in as requests are sent.

## burpsy-side evidence
The backend already supports this: internal/web/api_intruder_control.go serves GET /api/intruder/attacks (live table of running attacks) and POST /api/intruder/attacks/{task_id}/{pause|resume|stop}; internal/intruder/control.go implements Pause/Resume/Stop on a condition variable. The file's own doc (api_intruder_control.go:34) says the missing piece is "a status endpoint ... and controls wired to these routes."

The Intruder page never wires them. internal/web/ui/src/pages/intruder.tsx launches via a single blocking mutation useIntruderRun (data.tools.ts:116-118, POST /api/intruder/run) that resolves only when the whole attack has finished; the results tab shows nothing until then (intruder.tsx:808-825, 1488-1519). There is no running-attacks list, no pause/resume/stop button, and no live progress in the page. grep for pause/resume/stop/attacks in ui/src returns only sequencer capture-stop, never intruder controls.

Effect: a 200k-request cluster bomb aimed at the wrong host cannot be paused or stopped from the Intruder screen, and the operator sees no results until the attack completes.
close_reason:
Superseded by later work; both halves of the gap now exist and are wired end-to-end.

Backend: internal/intruder/control.go implements the attack lifecycle (StatusPaused, c.paused/c.stopped, pause/resume/stop; control_test.go covers the transitions), and internal/web/api_intruder_control.go exposes it over HTTP: routes /api/intruder/attacks + /api/intruder/attacks/{id} registered at server.go:752-753, with the attack registered in the task registry while it runs so pause/resume/stop from another connection reach the same attack (Task.Cancellable() true — the doc comment in api_intruder_control.go:20-34 records that the dashboard stop button and the Intruder stop button now address the same attack by id).

UI: intruder.tsx:683 controlAttack(action: 'pause'|'resume'|'stop') calls the API via attackAction.mutate, with toasts for pause/resume/stop and a stale-attack path that reports 'its report is on the way' instead of erroring. Live status badges (paused/running) render at intruder.tsx:978-982. The comment at intruder.tsx:628 documents the /run-is-synchronous constraint this control channel was built around.

Evidence: go test ./internal/intruder/ ./internal/web/ both ok (this session). Build: burpsy-go (module github.com/burpsy-go/burpsy, go 1.26). Parity note: Burp's attack window also shows live per-payload request counts; burpsy shows progress via attackProgress(report) with stopped/paused/reached at intruder.tsx:326-330 — partial-request counts match, so the 'no live results' half of the original claim is also resolved by the same live-status channel.

title: repeater: tab groups are organizational only — no Send group (single connection / separate connections / parallel), so the race-condition workflow is absent
description:
Repeater has tab groups, but a group cannot be *sent*. Burp's whole reason for grouping tabs —
beyond tidying the strip — is the **Send group** dropdown next to the Send button, which fires
every tab in the group together. burpsy's groups are organizational only, and the store makes that
explicit ("grouping must never gate sending or scope", `store.ts:39`). There is no group-send
control, so the primary race-condition / single-packet workflow does not exist.

## Burp-side evidence

`/root/burp-re/in/extract/resources/Documentation/burp/documentation/desktop/tools/repeater/send-group.html`:

> Burp Repeater's Group send options feature enables you to send grouped HTTP requests with a single
> click. You can send requests either in parallel (all at once), or in sequence (one after the other).
> ... Click the drop-down arrow by the side of the Send button and select one of the available options:
> **Send group in sequence (single connection)** / **Send group in sequence (separate connections)** /
> **Send group in parallel** ... Click **Send group**.

Same page names the point: "if you're testing for race condition vulnerabilities ... send parallel
requests with a single click." `groups.html` confirms grouping "enables you to send requests from
multiple tabs in sequence."

## burpsy-side evidence

- `internal/web/ui/src/pages/repeater.tsx` — groups render (create/rename/delete/collapse/move,
  colored border, member count) but the group header carries only Collapse / Delete. The Send button
  (`submit(active)`) sends the single active tab; there is no dropdown and no group entry point.
- `internal/web/ui/src/lib/store.ts:39` — "grouping must never gate sending or scope" — grouping is
  deliberately inert with respect to sending.
- `/api/repeater/send` takes one request; there is no batch/group send endpoint.

## Scope note

"Send group in parallel" and "separate connections" are reachable with the current one-request-per-
call sender by fanning out N sends. "Single connection" (the true single-packet / last-byte-sync
path) depends on connection reuse (`burpsy-react-ui-6i4`) and HTTP/2 (`burpsy-react-ui-745`); those
are the mechanics, this issue is the missing affordance and the parallel/separate-connection modes.
Burp's Pro "Trigger race conditions" custom action is a related convenience layered on top of this.

title: intruder: a result cannot be sent to Repeater or Comparer — the Results tab has no context menu or handoff at all
description:
An Intruder result is a dead end. There is no context menu and no button anywhere on the Results tab
to send a result to Repeater, Comparer or anywhere else.

## Burp-side evidence

`/root/burp-re/in/extract/resources/Documentation/burp/documentation/desktop/tools/intruder/results/workflow.html`
and `.../viewing-results.html` — a results row has the suite context menu, and
`.../configure-attack/settings.html` lists "Send requests or responses to other Burp tools" as one of
the three stated reasons the `Store requests / responses` setting exists. The suite-wide menu is
recorded at `/root/burp-re/BURP_SUITE_UI_UX_SPECIFICATION.md:237-238` (`Send to Repeater Ctrl+R`,
`Send to Intruder Ctrl+I`).

## burpsy-side evidence

Nothing on the page offers a handoff:

    $ grep -rni "ContextMenu|sendTo|lib/actions" internal/web/ui/src/pages/intruder.tsx
    (no output)

Positive control on the same file: `grep -c "SimpleTable" internal/web/ui/src/pages/intruder.tsx` →
non-zero (imported `:43`, used `:210, 243, 262, 307`).

- `internal/web/ui/src/pages/intruder.tsx:308-326` — attempt rows are plain `<tr>` with no menu
  wrapper. Compare `internal/web/ui/src/pages/repeater.tsx:296` where `ContextMenu` does wrap a
  trigger, so the primitive exists and is used elsewhere.
- `internal/web/ui/src/lib/actions.ts` — the shared send-to menu (`sendToRepeater`, `sendToComparer`
  at `:193`, menu entries at `:368-369`) is imported by `pages/history.tsx`, `pages/sitemap.tsx` and
  `pages/wshistory.tsx` only.

## Correction to the existing comparison doc

`/root/burp-re/BURP_UI_UX_COMPARISON.md:314` lists "Send to Repeater" under burpsy Intruder's
**Actions (from TSX)**. That is wrong at HEAD — `pages/intruder.tsx` contains no handoff of any kind.
The handoff is one-way: Repeater → Intruder (`pages/repeater.tsx:162-193, 524-527`). Worth fixing in
the doc so this gap is not assumed closed.

## Classification

UX DIVERGENCE — the send-to actions exist on other screens and not this one.

## What an operator cannot do

Follow up a finding. The attack surfaces a bucket that returned 302 where everything else returned
200; the operator now wants that exact request in Repeater to poke at it by hand. There is no path —
and because the per-result response id is also unrendered (filed separately), there is not even a
message id on screen to type in somewhere else.

## Note on dependency

This needs the result rows to be addressable first: `Attempt.ResponseID` and
`ResultBucket`'s example response id are returned but unread
(`internal/web/ui/src/lib/types.tools.ts:85, 102`), and no request-side message id is returned for an
attempt at all — `record` in `internal/web/api_tools.go:640-643` stores only the response. Sending an
attack *request* to Repeater therefore needs either the spliced request stored per attempt, or the
request reconstructed client-side from the base message plus the payload combination.
acceptance_criteria: A result row offers the shared send-to actions (Repeater, Comparer), addressing the stored request and response for that attempt; BURP_UI_UX_COMPARISON.md:314 is corrected to stop claiming this already exists.

title: intruder: an attack report cannot be exported — no CSV or download exists on the Results tab
description:
There is no way to get an Intruder attack's results out of burpsy. No CSV or other export exists on
the Results tab, even though HTTP history has one.

## Burp-side evidence

`/root/burp-re/in/extract/resources/Documentation/burp/documentation/desktop/tools/intruder/results/saving-attacks.html`
covers saving an attack and exporting its results; `/root/burp-re/BURP_UI_UX_COMPARISON.md:288` records
"Export results (CSV)" among Burp Intruder's actions.

## burpsy-side evidence

Absence grep:

    $ grep -rni "csv" internal/web/ui/src/pages/intruder.tsx internal/web/api_tools.go
    (no output)

Positive control across the same page directory, confirming the pattern does match in this tree:

    $ grep -rli "csv" internal/web/ui/src/pages/
    internal/web/ui/src/pages/history.tsx

- `internal/web/ui/src/pages/intruder.tsx:1067-1091` — the Results tab renders `AttackResult`, the
  legacy JSON view, or an empty state. No export control.
- `internal/web/ui/src/pages/intruder.tsx:148-332` (`AttackResult`) — four tables and a metric grid,
  no download affordance.
- Nothing server-side either: the only Intruder routes are `/api/intruder/points` and
  `/api/intruder/run` (`internal/web/server.go:742-743`).

The one export-adjacent thing Intruder has is `HttpEditor`'s `filename` prop for the *base request*
(`internal/web/ui/src/pages/intruder.tsx:717`), which saves the template, not the results.

## Classification

CAPABILITY GAP.

## What an operator cannot do

Take the results anywhere. The report cannot be handed to a colleague, diffed against a later run,
pasted into a finding, or post-processed. Combined with the fact that navigating away destroys the
report (filed separately), an attack's output currently exists only in one browser tab until that tab
changes page.

## Note on what to export

The `RunView` shape (`internal/web/api_tools.go:453-457` — report, examples, payload sets) is already a
complete, self-describing JSON document, so a "download this report" button costs almost nothing and
preserves the bounds accounting that makes the report honest. A flat CSV of attempt rows is what a Burp
user will ask for by name; it should carry the payload column, which means it depends on resolving the
missing-payload issue first, and it should carry the caveat fields (`truncated`, `unbucketed`,
`detail_limit`) somewhere, or a CSV of a capped attack will read as a complete result set.
acceptance_criteria: An attack report can be downloaded from the Results tab, and any flat row export carries the payload column and the truncated/unbucketed/detail_limit caveats so a capped attack cannot read as complete.

title: intruder: results tables use the non-sortable SimpleTable, so results cannot be sorted or filtered
description:
Intruder's results tables are rendered with `SimpleTable`, a static `<table>` with no sorting, no
filtering and no column controls — while the same module exports a sortable, filterable table that
other pages use.

## Burp-side evidence

`/root/burp-re/in/extract/resources/Documentation/burp/documentation/desktop/tools/intruder/results/filtering-results.html`
is an entire page about filtering the results table, and
`.../configure-attack/settings.html` repeatedly relies on sorting as the way to find findings:

> During the attack, Burp adds a results column for each expression in the list. This records the
> number of times the expression is found in the response. **To identify results with the expression,
> click on the column header to sort the results.**

Sorting is not a convenience in Burp Intruder; it is the documented mechanism for reading the output.

## burpsy-side evidence

- `internal/web/ui/src/ui/table.tsx:451-476` — `SimpleTable` takes `headers: string[]` and renders
  `<th key={header}>{header}</th>`. No sort state, no click handler, no filter input.
- The same file has the capable table: `:4` `getSortedRowModel`, `:8` `SortingState`, `:137`
  `useState<SortingState>`, `:161-168` wired into the tanstack instance, `:345-346`
  `header.column.getIsSorted()` / `getCanSort()`.
- Intruder uses only `SimpleTable`: `internal/web/ui/src/pages/intruder.tsx:43` imports it, and it is
  used for all four result tables — buckets (`:210`), errors (`:243`), payload-set accounting (`:262`)
  and attempts (`:307`).

## Classification

CAPABILITY GAP (results triage).

## What an operator cannot do

Order or narrow the output. A 5,000-request attack returns buckets and up to `detail_limit` attempt
rows in plan order; the operator cannot sort by length to find the outlier, sort by time to find the
slow one, or filter to errors only. The bucketing (`internal/intruder/engine.go` → grouped by status,
length and reflection) does a lot of this work up front and is genuinely better than an unsorted flat
table — but once a bucket list is more than a screenful, there is no way to reorder it.

## Note

This is small: the sortable table already exists in the same module and is already used elsewhere in
the app, so the change is largely swapping the component and defining columns. Worth sequencing after
the missing Payload column, since sorting is most useful once rows can be identified.
acceptance_criteria: Intruder result tables are sortable by column and filterable, using the sortable table already exported from ui/table.tsx.

title: repeater: no connection reuse or keep-alive, so a smuggling or desync finding cannot be reproduced by hand
description:
Every Repeater send dials a fresh connection and closes it. There is no connection-reuse or keep-alive
option, so no test that depends on two requests sharing one socket can be performed from Repeater.

## Burp-side evidence

`/root/burp-re/BURP_SUITE_UI_UX_SPECIFICATION.md:185` records the Repeater settings-gear items by name:
`repeaterConfigurationGlobalMenuItemEnableH1ConnectionReuse` and
`...EnableH2ConnectionReuse`. The Intruder equivalent is documented in prose at
`/root/burp-re/in/extract/resources/Documentation/burp/documentation/desktop/tools/intruder/configure-attack/settings.html`:

> **HTTP/1 connection reuse** - Use this setting to control whether Burp Intruder reuses connections to
> issue multiple HTTP/1 requests. This can greatly increase the speed of your attacks.
>
> If you deselect HTTP/1 connection reuse, Burp opens a new connection for each request and closes it
> after receiving a response.

## burpsy-side evidence

- `internal/web/ui/src/pages/repeater.tsx:606-654` — the config-override panel's full control set:
  redirect mode, protocol preference, process cookies, strip Connection, normalize line endings,
  update Content-Length. No reuse toggle.
- `internal/web/repeater_options.go:23-44` — `repeaterSendOptions` has six fields, none about
  connection lifetime.
- `internal/web/api_tools.go:139` — one `s.sender.SendRawOutcome(...)` per request.
- The behaviour is documented in the sender: `internal/sender/pipeline.go:3-9` —

  > writeHTTP1 (sender.go:597) dials fresh and reads exactly one response per send, which is exactly
  > right for every check that sends independent probes — but it cannot represent a front-end/back-end
  > framing disagreement, because that disagreement only exists *across* two requests sharing one
  > reused socket. checks_cache.go declines "HTTP request smuggling" and "Client-side desync" for
  > precisely this reason: "sender has no keep-alive/pipelining primitive".

Absence grep:

    $ grep -rni "reuse" internal/sender/*.go internal/web/ui/src/pages/repeater.tsx
    internal/sender/redirect.go:136:  ... reuses that decision ...
    internal/sender/pipeline.go:7:    ... reused socket ...
    internal/sender/cancel.go:43:     ... before the connection is reused or closed.

Three hits, all prose in comments, zero settings. Positive control on the same file set:
`grep -c "func" internal/sender/pipeline.go` → non-zero.

## What already exists and is not reachable from Repeater

`internal/sender/pipeline.go` provides `SendPipelined`, `SendKeepAlive` and `TimedRead` — the exact
primitive this needs. They are not called from the Repeater path. The file is explicit that a caller
must run every raw request through `ScopeChecker.AuthoriseRaw` first ("one call per raw ... a smuggled
prefix can address a different target than the socket it rides in on"), which is the design constraint
any Repeater wiring has to honour.

## Classification

CAPABILITY GAP. The absence is honestly disclosed in the sender's own comments, and the corresponding
scanner checks are explicitly *declined* rather than faked — but it is a user-facing capability Burp
offers on this screen, not an internals difference, so it is filed rather than treated as deliberate.

## What an operator cannot do

Manually verify a request-smuggling or client-side-desync finding from Repeater. In Burp this is the
standard workflow: disable/enable connection reuse, send two crafted requests down one socket, and
watch the second get the first's framing. Here it cannot be attempted at all, and the two
corresponding automated checks are declined for the same reason — so neither the automated nor the
manual path exists.

## Decision needed

Whether Repeater grows a per-tab "reuse connection for the next send" mode (needs a per-tab connection
handle held across sends, which is state the current stateless handler does not have), or a narrower
"send these two requests on one socket" action. The second is smaller and covers the smuggling
workflow; the first is Burp parity. Either way `AuthoriseRaw` must run per raw request, not per socket.
acceptance_criteria: Repeater can put two or more crafted requests down one socket via the existing sender.SendKeepAlive/SendPipelined primitives, with AuthoriseRaw run per raw request, or the gap is closed as deliberate with the reasoning recorded.

title: repeater: no Send to Comparer or Scanner — the shared send-to action menu is wired into history, sitemap and wshistory but not Repeater
description:
The send-to action menu — Send to Repeater, Send to Intruder, Send to Comparer (A) / (B), send to
Scanner — already exists as a shared module and is wired into HTTP history, Site map and WebSocket
history. Repeater does not import it. From a Repeater tab the only handoff is a single "To Intruder"
button.

## Burp-side evidence

`/root/burp-re/BURP_UI_UX_COMPARISON.md:138` records Burp Repeater's actions as "Send to Intruder /
Scanner / Comparer", and `/root/burp-re/BURP_SUITE_UI_UX_SPECIFICATION.md:237-238, 259-260` record the
suite-wide context menu with `Send to Repeater Ctrl+R` / `Send to Intruder Ctrl+I` available from any
HTTP message editor — Repeater's panes included. Comparing two Repeater responses side by side is the
canonical reason Comparer exists (`.../tools/comparer`).

## burpsy-side evidence

The actions exist:

- `internal/web/ui/src/lib/actions.ts:144` — `sendToComparer: (exchange: Exchange, slot: "a" | "b") => Promise<void>;`
- `internal/web/ui/src/lib/actions.ts:193-197` — the implementation, which sets the Comparer slot and
  routes to the Comparer page.
- `internal/web/ui/src/lib/actions.ts:368-369` — the menu entries "Send to Comparer (A)" and
  "Send to Comparer (B)".
- `internal/web/ui/src/lib/store.ts:111, 168, 313` — `comparerSlots` and `setComparerSlot`.

Repeater does not consume them:

    $ grep -rln "lib/actions" internal/web/ui/src/pages/ internal/web/ui/src/ui/
    internal/web/ui/src/pages/history.tsx
    internal/web/ui/src/pages/sitemap.tsx
    internal/web/ui/src/pages/wshistory.tsx

Three consumers, and `pages/repeater.tsx` is not among them. Positive control on the same page set:
`grep -rln "lib/store" internal/web/ui/src/pages/` includes `repeater.tsx` — so the grep does reach
that file.

Direct check on the page:

    $ grep -rni "comparer|sequencer|scanSeed" internal/web/ui/src/pages/repeater.tsx
    (no output)

Positive control, same file: `grep -c "setIntruderSeed" internal/web/ui/src/pages/repeater.tsx` →
non-zero (`:35`, `:185`).

The one handoff Repeater does have is the "To Intruder" button at
`internal/web/ui/src/pages/repeater.tsx:524-527`, implemented bespoke at `:162-193` rather than
through `actions.ts`.

## Classification

UX DIVERGENCE — the capability exists in the product, on other screens, and not on this one.

## What an operator cannot do

Send a Repeater response to Comparer. Having produced two responses that differ subtly, the operator
must go to HTTP history, find the two Repeater-sourced exchanges by id, and send them to Comparer from
there — despite both being open in front of them. Sending a Repeater request to the Scanner has the
same problem.

## Note

`actions.ts`'s menu takes an `Exchange`, and a Repeater send returns `exchange_id`
(`internal/web/api_tools.go:148`, consumed at `pages/repeater.tsx:364`), so the adapter already has
what it needs — the same resolve step `handOffToIntruder` performs at `repeater.tsx:184`. A request
that has not been sent yet has no exchange, which is the one case needing a decision: send-once-then-
hand-off (what the Intruder button does today) or disable the menu items until a send exists.
acceptance_criteria: A Repeater tab offers the same send-to actions as an HTTP history row, Send to Comparer (A)/(B) included, via lib/actions.ts rather than a bespoke handler.
close_reason: Invalid as written. actions.menu() emits 'Send to Comparer (A/B)' and 'Audit exchange #N' (Scanner), and repeater.tsx:236 wires actions.menu(sentExchange.data) into BOTH the request and response editor panes. So Send to Comparer and Scanner ARE available in Repeater. Residual (correct-by-design): the menu is keyed to result.exchange_id, so it appears only after the first send — a draft that has never left the browser has no stored id to act on (defended at repeater.tsx:224-233). Not a gap.

title: repeater: a history entry carries no request snapshot, so paging back shows an old response beside the current draft
description:
Repeater has per-tab response history and prev/next navigation — that part works. What a history
entry does not carry is the request that produced it. Paging back to entry 2 of 5 swaps the response
pane and leaves the request pane showing the current draft, so the operator sees an old response
beside a request that did not produce it.

Not claiming per-tab history is absent: it is present at
`internal/web/ui/src/pages/repeater.tsx:63-65` with controls at `:367-398`. This issue is only about
the missing request snapshot.

## Burp-side evidence

`/root/burp-re/in/extract/resources/Documentation/burp/documentation/desktop/tools/intruder/configure-attack/managing-tabs.html`
and the Repeater component list in `/root/burp-re/BURP_UI_UX_COMPARISON.md:105-128` — Burp's Repeater
tab keeps a request/response *pair* per history position; stepping back restores both panes together.
That is what makes the tool's method — change one thing, compare — work.

## burpsy-side evidence

The history entry type has no request field:

- `internal/web/ui/src/lib/types.ts:279-293` — `RepeaterResult` is
  `{ status, duration_ms, response, exchange_id, redirects? }`.
- `internal/web/api_tools.go:141-151` — the server's `repeaterSendResp` does return
  `RequestMsgID uint64` and `ExchangeID`, so the request *is* stored and addressable — but
  `RepeaterResult` on the TS side does not declare `request_msg_id`, and nothing reads it:

      $ grep -rn "request_msg_id" internal/web/ui/src/
      (no output)
