CAPABILITY GAP. Distinct from the "rebinding does nothing" defect: this row has no binding at all, so it is an advertised shortcut that has never fired.

## What an operator cannot do
Use Ctrl+O to file a row into Organizer, despite the shortcut list telling them they can.
acceptance_criteria: With a row selected, the send.organizer chord from the keymap registry files that exchange into Organizer; the row's presence in the shortcut table matches an installed binding.
close_reason: 63e101b8164900cbcd08697a60c61cda3dcab2d5. send.organizer is installed in useSendShortcuts (lib/actions.ts) alongside send.repeater and send.intruder, from the keymap registry, and that hook is called on History, Site map and WebSockets history. The advertised row in the modal and the Settings table now matches an installed binding. Guarded by src/lib/keymap-installed.test.ts, which fails if any rebindable id has no useChord call.

title: organizer: items have no user-applied workflow status (New / In progress / Postponed / Done / Ignored)
description:
## Claim
Organizer items have no workflow status, so there is no way to mark a saved exchange as tested, in progress, postponed or ignored.

## Burp-side evidence
`tools/organizer/annotate.html`, "Statuses in Organizer":
> "Statuses enable you to quickly see which saved requests still need attention and which ones you have already tested. Combined with filtering, this helps you focus on active work and easily return to items later.
> The following statuses are available: New / In progress / Postponed / Done / Ignored"

`tools/organizer/index.html` lists **Status** as a table column ("The status applied to the message") — distinct from **Status code** ("The HTTP status code of the response"), which is also a column. `tools/organizer/filter.html` then offers "Filter by status - Show or hide messages with different user-applied statuses."

The pairing is the point: status plus filter is how the operator returns to unfinished work.

## burpsy-side evidence
`internal/organizer/organizer.go:8-14` — the item carries `{ID, Exchange, Title, Note, Highlight}`; no status field. `Update` (`organizer.go:49`) takes exactly `title, note, highlight`.

Absence-grep with same-file positive control:
```
$ grep -n "status\|Status" internal/organizer/organizer.go
(no output)
$ grep -c "Item" internal/organizer/organizer.go
9
```

The page's edit surface is Title / Highlight / Note only — `internal/web/ui/src/pages/organizer.tsx:487-527`, with the wire payload `OrganizerEdit` built at `:203-208` from those three fields.

## Not the same as the existing status filter
`burpsy-react-ui-k4r` (closed) added an in-scope / status-class / MIME filter to this page. That filter's "Status" is the HTTP status class — `STATUS_CLASSES` at `internal/web/ui/src/pages/organizer.tsx:55-64` is `2xx / 3xx / 4xx / 5xx / No response`, and `matchesStatusClass` (`:68-74`) reads `item.status`, the response code resolved from the traffic store. That is Burp's *Status code* column. The user-applied workflow status is a different field and does not exist.

Worth noting because the two share a word and the page already has one of them, which is exactly how this gets mistaken for done.

## Classification
CAPABILITY GAP.

## What an operator cannot do
Tell, on returning to the Organizer, which of thirty saved requests they have already worked through. Highlight colours are the only marker available and carry no agreed meaning.
acceptance_criteria: An item can be set to one of the five statuses and the status is shown as its own column, distinct from the HTTP status-code column. The existing filter toolbar can filter on it. Round-trips through the save endpoint.

title: proxy settings: 3 of Burp's 8 response modification rules are absent — enable disabled fields, remove input length limits, remove cookie Secure flag
description:
VERIFIED against HEAD by AuditProxy (Proxy-screen parity audit, 2026-08-27).

burpsy implements 5 of Burp's 8 response modification rules. Three rules and one
sub-option have no counterpart.

## Burp-side evidence

BurpClass9083.java -- configPanelProxyModificationRules (:58), title "Response
modification rules" (:63). The eight controls plus one sub-option:

  :112  "Unhide hidden form fields"              -> burpsy HAS
  :182  "Prominently highlight unhidden fields"  -> MISSING (sub-option of above)
  :121  "Enable disabled form fields"            -> MISSING
  :129  "Remove input field length limits"       -> MISSING
  :137  "Remove JavaScript form validation"      -> burpsy HAS
  :145  "Remove all JavaScript"                  -> burpsy HAS
  :153  "Remove <object> tags"                   -> burpsy HAS
  :161  "Convert HTTPS links to HTTP"            -> burpsy HAS
  :169  "Remove secure flag from cookies"        -> MISSING

## burpsy-side evidence

internal/proxy/options.go:43-62 is the COMPLETE OptionKeys enumeration -- six
keys, and the file comment at :65 states it is "every editable option, in the
order the panel renders them":

  :45  unhide_hidden_form_fields
  :47  remove_object_tags
  :50  remove_javascript_form_validation
  :53  remove_all_javascript
  :56  convert_https_links_to_http
  :62  strip_accept_encoding          (burpsy's own, not a Burp rule)

pages/proxysettings.tsx:20-51 mirrors those six exactly, so the panel is honest
about what it has -- this is a missing capability, not a missing control for an
existing one.

This is an enumeration rather than an absence-grep: the authority lists
everything that exists, so the four omissions are proven by the presence of the
full list.

## Classification

CAPABILITY GAP (three rules plus one sub-option).

## What an operator cannot do

* Re-enable a greyed-out form control, or lift a maxlength to submit an
  over-long value, from the browser -- both routine client-side-control tests
  that today require hand-editing each response in Intercept.
* Downgrade a Secure session cookie so it is transmitted over plaintext HTTP and
  can be captured.

## Note

All four are the same shape as the five that exist -- regex rewrites over an
HTML response body, applied at the same point in applyResponseRules -- so this
is additive within the existing option set and route, with no new plumbing. The
"Prominently highlight unhidden fields" sub-option needs a decision on what
marker to inject, since burpsy has no equivalent of Burp's injected styling.
acceptance_criteria: Enable disabled form fields, Remove input field length limits and Remove secure flag from cookies are present in proxy.OptionKeys, switchable from Proxy settings, applied live by the relay, and counted by the existing outcome counters.

title: organizer: no collections — saved exchanges are one flat list with no grouping
description:
## Claim
The Organizer has no collections: saved exchanges live in one flat list with no way to group them.

## Burp-side evidence
`BURP_SUITE_UI_UX_SPECIFICATION.md` §4.11 names the four recovered menu items:
> "Context Actions: New Collection (`setName(\"organiserCollectionNewMenuItem\")`), Rename (`setName(\"organiserCollectionRenameMenuItem\")`), Copy Link (`setName(\"organiserCollectionCopyLinkMenuItem\")`), Unlink (`setName(\"organiserCollectionUnlinkMenuItem\")`)."

`tools/organizer/collections.html`:
> "Collections provide a way to group HTTP messages in a way that suits your testing workflow. […] To create a new collection, click New."
> "To move messages: In Organizer, select one or more messages. Right-click and select Move to… Select the collection you want to move the messages to."
> "You can rename, duplicate, and delete a collection by right-clicking it […] You can also add notes to a collection using the About tab."

`tools/organizer/index.html` frames the flat list as the *inbox*, i.e. the untriaged state, with collections as where work goes: "Messages appear in the Organizer inbox […] As your testing progresses, you may want to organize messages into collections."

## burpsy-side evidence
The stored model has no grouping field — `internal/organizer/organizer.go:8-14`:
```go
type Item struct {
    ID        int    `json:"id"`
    Exchange  int    `json:"exchange"`
    Title     string `json:"title"`
    Note      string `json:"note"`
    Highlight string `json:"highlight"`
}
```
`Store` is a single `items []Item` slice (`organizer.go:18-22`); `Add` appends to it (`:30`).

Absence-grep with same-file positive control:
```
$ grep -n "collection\|Collection" internal/organizer/organizer.go
(no output)
$ grep -c "Item" internal/organizer/organizer.go
9
```
The file is greppable, so the zero is real.

The page renders one `SimpleTable` over one list — `internal/web/ui/src/pages/organizer.tsx:358-446`. There is no collection selector, and no multi-select: rows carry a single-item `onClick` select (`:363`) and the add path takes one exchange id (`:180-196`).

## Classification
CAPABILITY GAP.

## Scope note
Burp's Pro-only sharing half of this feature — Share collection / Unshare / Copy Link / Import, which encrypt and upload to PortSwigger servers (`tools/organizer/collections.html`) — is a hosted-service dependency and is deliberately not part of this claim. What is claimed is local grouping: create, rename, duplicate, delete, move-to, copy-to, and collection-level notes.

## What an operator cannot do
Separate saved requests by test area. On a target of any size the Organizer becomes one undifferentiated list, which is the state Burp calls the inbox and expects you to empty.
acceptance_criteria: An operator can create, rename, duplicate and delete a collection, move or copy selected items between collections and the inbox, and attach a note to a collection. Deleting a collection that holds items asks whether to move them back to the inbox or delete them with it.

title: extender: plugin-registered context-menu items and editor tabs never appear in the context menu or the editor tab strip
description:
## Claim
A plugin's registered context-menu item never appears in any context menu, and a registered editor tab never appears in the message editor's view strip. Both can only be triggered from a Run button on the Extender -> Extensions page, with no selected exchange as context.

## Burp-side evidence
- Spec section 6.4: `ContextMenuItemsProvider` — *"Injects extension custom action menu items into Burp's right-click context menu."*
- Spec section 6.2: `HttpRequestEditorProvider` / `HttpResponseEditorProvider` — *"Allows extensions to inject custom tabbed views into the Request/Response viewer (e.g. Protocol Buffers, JWT decoders)."*
- `tools/message-editor/index.html` (bundled docs) confirms the editor tab strip is the extension surface: *"you can remove or reorder the tabs, and add some extra ones from the settings menu."*

## burpsy-side evidence
This is NOT the documented Swing exclusion. burpsy's own disclosure puts these three points explicitly IN scope — `lib/reference.ts:341`: *"Of userInterface()'s registration points, the ten Swing ones are out of scope for lack of an honest web analogue. The three declarative ones — context-menu items, message-editor tabs, menu actions — are in scope."*

The server side is real: `internal/extension/protocol.go:89-91` defines `KindContextMenu` as *"the analogue of registerContextMenuItemsProvider: an action against a selected [request]"*; `internal/extension/host.go:529-530` dispatches `contextMenu.invoke`; `internal/extension/views.go:157,163` label it.

The UI never surfaces it. The only consumer of the registration list in the entire UI tree is the Extender page's own table:
- `grep -rn 'registration' --include=*.ts --include=*.tsx lib/ ui/ pages/` (excluding reference.ts) -> hits only in `lib/types.extensions.ts`, `lib/data.extensions.ts`, `pages/extensions.tsx`.
- `pages/extensions.tsx:139-180` renders a Registrations table with a per-row Run button (`run(registration)` -> `POST` via `lib/data.extensions.ts:75-90`).
- `lib/actions.ts:782-834` `menu()` never reads the registration list.
- `ui/editor.tsx:264-274` builds `available` from a closed literal union (`MessageView` at `:177`) with no extension point.
- `app.tsx:414-571` `MENUS` is a static array, so `KindMenu` is unsurfaced too.

## Classification
CAPABILITY GAP, contradicting the project's own stated scope.

## What an operator cannot do
Right-click a request and run a plugin action on it. The plugin's action is invocable only by navigating to Extender -> Extensions -> select the plugin -> Run, which does not carry the exchange the operator wanted to act on — so a context-menu plugin cannot do the one thing its kind name means.
acceptance_criteria: A loaded plugin's context-menu registrations appear as menu entries in the exchange row and editor context menus and are invoked with the selected exchange; its editor-tab registrations appear as views in the message editor tab strip.

title: ui: Issues, Organizer, Content discovery and Dashboard tables have no right-click menu (Sequencer: not a gap)
description:
## Claim
Five data tables offer no right-click menu at all, because they are built on `SimpleTable`, which has no menu support. The worst affected is Target -> Issues, where Burp's entire issue-triage menu (Set severity, Set confidence, Report issue, Go to issue, Delete issue) lives.

## Burp-side evidence
- `tools/context-menu.html` (Burp bundled docs): *"The context menu provides quick access to a variety of tools and functions throughout Burp Suite. To view the context menu, right-click an item or group of items. **Most Burp Suite tools support this functionality.**"*
- Issue-specific entries in that same list: **Set severity** *"Sets or changes the severity level of an issue"*; **Set confidence**; **Report issue** *"Creates a report from the selected items"*; **Go to issue** *"Opens the relevant issue in the Issues tab"*; **Delete issue**.
- Spec section 4.11 documents the Organiser context actions (New Collection / Rename / Copy Link / Unlink).

## burpsy-side evidence
Surfaces that DO have a row menu (all pass `VirtualTable`'s `menuGroups`): `pages/history.tsx:1012`, `pages/sitemap.tsx:548`, `pages/logger.tsx:354`, `pages/intercept.tsx:728`, `pages/wshistory.tsx:213`. Plus `pages/repeater.tsx:296` on tab headers.

Surfaces that do NOT — all use `SimpleTable`, which takes no `menuGroups` prop (`ui/table.tsx:448-478`, signature is `{headers, children, className, density}` only, and it renders a bare `<tbody>{children}</tbody>` with no `ContextMenu` wrapper; contrast `ui/table.tsx:446-447` in `TableRow`, where `VirtualTable` does wrap):
- Target -> Issues: `pages/scanner.tsx:190` (`grep -c ContextMenu pages/scanner.tsx` -> 0; positive control `grep -c import` -> 16)
- Organizer: `pages/organizer.tsx:358` (ContextMenu -> 0, import -> 9)
- Sequencer: `pages/sequencer.tsx` (ContextMenu -> 0, import -> 10)
- Content discovery: `pages/contentdiscovery.tsx` (ContextMenu -> 0, import -> 8)
- Dashboard: `pages/dashboard.tsx` (ContextMenu -> 0, import -> 14)

## Classification
CAPABILITY GAP.

## What an operator cannot do
On Target -> Issues, right-click a finding to set its severity or confidence, report it, or jump to it in the site map — the whole Scanner triage loop. On Organizer, right-click a stored item to rename or act on it. The `ContextMenu` component already exists and `VirtualTable` already wires it; the gap is that these five tables are on the non-menu table primitive.

## Decision needed
Whether to add a `menuGroups` prop to `SimpleTable` (small, keeps both primitives) or migrate these tables to `VirtualTable` (fewer primitives, but Issues/Organizer are short lists where a scroll viewport is wrong — the reason `SimpleTable` exists per its own doc comment at `ui/table.tsx:447`).
acceptance_criteria: DONE in 63e101b: Organizer, Content discovery and both Dashboard tables have row menus; Target -> Issues has a menu on its finding leaf carrying go-to-issue, report exports, copies and the full cross-tool matrix on the finding's exchange. REMAINS: the Issues menu cannot carry Set severity, Set confidence or Delete issue — /api/issues is registered GET-only (internal/web/server.go:727), so this needs PATCH and DELETE endpoints first (a .go change). Sequencer is REMOVED from scope: its three tables are analysis output (FIPS bit-test results, per-position entropy, capture-miss reasons), not item rows, and Burp puts no row menu on its own Sequencer analysis panels either. Also corrected: pages/scanner.tsx:190 is the Passive check coverage counter table, not the Issues list; Issues is the role=tree around scanner.tsx:500-560.

comments.author: FixMenusHotkeys
comments.text:
PARTIALLY FIXED in 63e101b8164900cbcd08697a60c61cda3dcab2d5 — deliberately NOT closed. Four of the five surfaces now have a menu; the Issues menu cannot carry severity or confidence, which the acceptance criteria require.

MECHANISM. ui/table.tsx gains MenuRow, and it is a component rather than a menuGroups prop on SimpleTable for the reason the decision note asks about. SimpleTable takes its rows as children, so it never sees a row object to hand a factory. MenuRow IS the mapped element, so the React key goes on it and the tr it renders is the Radix trigger via asChild — no wrapper element, table markup stays valid, and the keyless-list trap that was tried and reverted here is structurally impossible. SimpleTable is unchanged, so the short-list-without-a-scroll-viewport reason it exists (its own doc comment) still holds. ui/menu.tsx also gains submenu support, because Burp's colour and severity pickers are submenus.

DONE:
- Organizer (pages/organizer.tsx): rename (prompt), Highlight submenu with the ten HIGHLIGHTS colours plus clear, show/copy exchange id, copy note, remove (routed through the existing delete confirmation, since the note is the only unrecoverable thing here). Writes go through patchItem, which reads title/note off the ROW and never off the open draft — sending the selected row's note under another row's id would overwrite a note the operator wrote.
- Content discovery (pages/contentdiscovery.tsx): Send to Repeater (built from the URL via templateRequest, with a toast that says the sweep captured no request bytes rather than implying it did), open in browser, copy URL/path/redirect target, filter history by the path.
- Dashboard (pages/dashboard.tsx), BOTH tables: tasks get cancel plus copy target and copy status line; recent activity gets show-in-history by host and by path plus copy request line and copy URL (as logged).
- Target -> Issues (pages/scanner.tsx): Burp's 'Go to issue' in both directions (the finding's exchange in HTTP history, and the host filtered), the three report exports as 'Report issue', copy issue name / location / detail, and — when the finding's exchange is inside the loaded 1000-row window — the FULL cross-tool matrix on that exchange, so retesting a finding by sending its request to Repeater is one gesture. The exchange is resolved per leaf, not reused from the selection.

BLOCKED, and why. Set severity, Set confidence and Delete issue are absent. /api/issues is registered GET-only (internal/web/server.go:727); there is no PATCH to move a severity or confidence onto a finding and no DELETE to remove one. A menu entry that opened a severity picker and dropped the choice is the exact class of defect this audit exists to find, so they are omitted with the reason in the code comment. Needs a .go change (FixBackendTruth's territory).

Organizer collections are also absent: Burp's New collection / Rename collection / Unlink are collection operations and /api/tools/organizer is one flat list with no collection concept. Rename of an ITEM is implemented; there is no collection to unlink from.

TWO AUDIT CORRECTIONS.

1. The Issues table is NOT a SimpleTable. pages/scanner.tsx:190 is the 'Passive check coverage' table (Check / Ran / Findings / Errored / State) — a read-only per-check statistics strip, not the issue list. Target -> Issues is a role=tree of host -> path -> finding leaves (the treePane, around pages/scanner.tsx:500-560). The menu was added to the leaf, which is where an operator right-clicks a finding. The coverage table still has no menu and should not have one: its rows are aggregate counters, not items.

2. Sequencer has NO menu and I did not add one, rather than adding filler. Its three SimpleTables are analysis output, not item rows: the FIPS 140-2 bit-test results (Test / Result / Observed / Requirement / Blocks), the per-character-position entropy strip (# / Entropy / Distinct / Samples / Distribution / Flag), and the capture-miss reasons (Attempt / Why no token). None of them is a thing that can be sent, annotated or opened elsewhere, and Burp does not put a row context menu on its Sequencer analysis panels either. The Sequencer DID gain something from this commit: its HttpEditor panes now carry the Convert-selection codec menu (see pf9), which is a real win on a pane holding a token list. If the audit still wants a Sequencer row menu, it needs to say which action on which row.

TO CLOSE THIS: PATCH and DELETE on /api/issues for severity, confidence and deletion. Or re-scope: the four shipped surfaces are done, and the Issues severity/confidence gap belongs on its own backend issue.

comments.author: FixMenusHotkeys
comments.text:
SCOPE ANSWER: FIVE DIFFERENT PROBLEMS WEARING ONE TITLE. This is the clearest answer I have for the inventory, and the issue as written will produce a bad estimate.

The title's premise is that these five tables share a cause — 'they are built on SimpleTable, which has no menu support' — and therefore share a fix. That premise is false for two of the five, and the remaining three differ in what a menu can contain, not in how to attach one. Attaching a menu turned out to be the trivial part (one 12-line `MenuRow` in ui/table.tsx, reused unchanged by three pages). Deciding what goes IN each menu was the entire cost.

Breaking it up, in the order I would put them in a plan:

1. ORGANIZER — real, valuable, done. Genuinely a SimpleTable row menu. Rename + Highlight submenu + copies + remove. The one non-obvious hazard is that /api/tools/organizer's save takes the whole OrganizerEdit, so a menu changing only the colour must still send title and note — read off the ROW, never the open draft, or the selected row's note gets written under another row's id. Blocked remainder: Burp's collections (New collection / Unlink) have no API concept to map to.

2. CONTENT DISCOVERY — real, done, but note the shape. A discovered path is NOT an exchange; the sweep is an external tool reporting a URL exists. Send to Repeater has to SYNTHESISE a request (templateRequest) and say so in the toast. 'Add to site map' is unimplementable — the site map is built from captured traffic and has no injection endpoint.

3. TARGET -> ISSUES — the highest-value one, and the issue MISIDENTIFIES IT. pages/scanner.tsx:190 is the 'Passive check coverage' table (Check / Ran / Findings / Errored / State), a read-only per-check counter strip that should NOT have a menu. Target -> Issues is a role="tree" of host -> path -> finding leaves, around pages/scanner.tsx:500-560. I put the menu on the leaf. Delivered: Go-to-issue both directions, Report (the three /api/report exports), copies, and the full cross-tool matrix on the finding's exchange when it is inside the loaded 1000-row window. BLOCKED and the reason this issue cannot close: Set severity, Set confidence and Delete issue need PATCH and DELETE on /api/issues, which is registered GET-only at internal/web/server.go:727. That is a .go change and it is the single most valuable item left in this issue.

4. DASHBOARD — real but thin, done. Two tables, not one. Tasks get cancel + copies. Recent activity (ActivityRow) has the same missing-ids problem as Logger, so it gets jump-to-history and copies only, never a send-to. Low value; would not have justified its own issue.

5. SEQUENCER — NOT A GAP. I added nothing and recommend nothing. Its three SimpleTables are analysis output, not item rows: FIPS 140-2 bit-test results (Test / Result / Observed / Requirement / Blocks), the per-character-position entropy strip, and the capture-miss reasons (Attempt / Why no token). None is a thing that can be sent, annotated or opened elsewhere, and Burp puts no row context menu on its own Sequencer analysis panels. The Sequencer DID gain something real from this commit, just not from this issue: its HttpEditor token pane now carries the Convert-selection codec menu (see pf9), which is the actually-useful thing on a pane holding a token list.

RECOMMENDED SPLIT for the inventory:
  - one CLOSED-as-done bucket: Organizer, Content discovery, Dashboard (all landed in 63e101b)
  - one BACKEND issue, P2, real value: PATCH/DELETE on /api/issues for severity, confidence, deletion — then the Issues leaf menu gains three entries and this closes
  - one INVALID: Sequencer. Please do not carry it into a plan; there is no action to put on those rows.

If you keep it as one issue, the estimate should be read as 'four surfaces of very different value plus one that should not be built', not 'five tables, one fix'.

title: history: original message bytes are not retained, so a Match & Replace rewrite or an intercept edit cannot be compared against what the client sent
description:
VERIFIED against HEAD by AuditProxy (Proxy-screen parity audit, 2026-08-27).

burpsy stores one version of each proxied message. When a Match & Replace rule
or a manual intercept edit changes a message, the bytes the client actually sent
are gone -- only a counter records that something changed.

## Burp-side evidence

BurpClass9062.java -- configPanelProxyMessageDisplay (:49):
  :57  title "Default Proxy history message display"
  :62  "...whether the Proxy history message editor displays auto-modified,
        manually edited, or original messages by default"
  three radio groups -- HTTP requests (:117), HTTP responses (:124),
  WebSocket messages (:132) -- each offering three values:
  :141 "Original"      configPanelProxyMessageDisplayOriginalReq
  :150 "Edited"        configPanelProxyMessageDisplayEditedReq
  :159 "Auto-modified" configPanelProxyMessageDisplayModifiedReq
  and the same triple for Res (:169-188) and Ws (:197-215).

The history editor then offers those views per message, which is why Burp's
history table also carries an "Edited" column.

## burpsy-side evidence

No original bytes are retained:
`grep -rniE "original(Req|Res|Bytes|Raw|Request|Response)" --include=*.go
internal/core internal/proxy internal/store` returns ZERO.
Positive control, same directory and same tool:
`grep -rc "odified" internal/proxy/proxy.go` -> 3.

No view surface: pages/history.tsx has no tab component at all --
`grep -cE "Tabs"` on that file -> 0, and the import block at history.tsx:1-18
confirms it (SplitPane and HttpEditor, no Tabs).
Positive control, same file: `grep -c "highlight"` -> 13.

The design is stated deliberately at internal/proxy/proxy.go:1660-1663:
  "Unrecorded, hence the counter: nothing here is stored, so the rewrite is real
   but invisible in history, and Counters.ModifiedUnrecorded is what makes it
   accountable."
-- so the counter is an accountability substitute for the bytes, not a view of
them.

Also absent for the same reason: Burp's "Edited" history column. burpsy's
columns are #, Method, Host, Path, Status, Type, Ext, Query, TLS, Comment,
Length, Time, Age (history.tsx:657-763) -- 13 columns, none of them Edited.

## Classification

CAPABILITY GAP.

## What an operator cannot do

See what a Match & Replace rule actually did to real traffic. After a rule
rewrites a request, the operator cannot compare what the client sent against
what reached the origin -- in Burp that comparison is one radio button. The same
applies to their own intercept edits: the edited bytes overwrite the originals.

## Not a duplicate of burpsy-react-ui-ruw

ruw asks for a per-rule preview on the Match & Replace PAGE. This issue is about
RETAINING the original bytes of captured traffic so history can show them. See
my note on ruw: the preview it asks for already exists (matchreplace.tsx:399-452,
"Sample input" / "Transformed output" with a changed/no-change badge), so these
are different claims and only this one is outstanding.

## Shape of the work -- storage decision first

Retaining originals doubles the stored bytes for every modified message. The
decision to record on this issue before building: store the original only when a
rule or an edit actually changed the message (the modified/unchanged verdict is
already computed -- proxy/options.go Counters), or store both unconditionally.
The former is far cheaper and is what the counters already distinguish.
acceptance_criteria: A history entry whose message was auto-modified or manually edited can be viewed as Original as well as the version that went on the wire; the storage policy (retain-on-change vs retain-always) is recorded as a decision on this issue; an entry that was never modified gains no extra stored bytes.

title: sequencer: FIPS tests run over the flattened bit stream, not per bit position, and the page does not say so
description:
## Claim
The FIPS tests run over the concatenated bit stream in 20,000-bit blocks rather than at each bit position across tokens, so the report cannot name which bit positions failed — and unlike the page's other statistical caveats, this one is not disclosed.

## Burp-side evidence
`tools/sequencer/results/tests.html`, "Bit-level analysis":
> "each token is converted into a set of bits. This enables Burp to perform powerful bit-level tests **at each bit position**."

Per test, the same framing, repeatedly: monobit — "analyzes the distribution of ones and zeroes at each bit position"; poker — "At each position, the test calculates the probability…"; runs — "divides the bit sequence at each position into runs"; long runs — "measures the longest run of bits with the same value at each bit position".

And the reported output is per-position: "FIPS result - For FIPS tests, a FIPS pass or fail result. **Any bits that failed the test are identified.**" (`tools/sequencer/results/index.html`, "Individual tests").

## burpsy-side evidence
`internal/sequencer/fips.go:11-20`, the package's own description of the shape:
> "Because every interval is a function of the 20,000-bit sample size, the stream is cut into whole 20,000-bit blocks, each is tested exactly as specified, and the leftover bits are reported as untested rather than folded in."

Implementation: `BitsOf(tokens, encoding)` (`internal/sequencer/fips.go:183`) flattens every token into one `[]byte` bit stream; `AnalyseFipsBits(bits)` (`fips.go:465`) walks it in `BlockBits`-sized slices; `testBlock(block)` (`fips.go:453`) treats its slice as an undifferentiated sequence. Nothing carries a bit *index within a token*.

The reported unit is consequently a block, not a position — `FipsTest.BlocksPassed` / `BlocksFailed` (`fips.go:313-314`), rendered as a "Blocks" column at `internal/web/ui/src/pages/sequencer.tsx:96-98`.

## Why this is filed as its own claim
The statistics are correct for what they measure, and the FIPS thresholds genuinely are defined on a 20,000-bit sample — the block-cutting is a defensible reading. The gap is that a Burp user reads the bit-level tab to learn *which bits* are weak (a fixed prefix, a low-entropy counter field), and that answer is unavailable here in principle, not by sample size.

The undisclosed part is what makes it actionable rather than a preference. The page is scrupulous about its other statistical limits:
- positional independence: `pages/sequencer.tsx:216-222` ("an upper estimate, not a measurement")
- FIPS not run below one block: `pages/sequencer.tsx:82-85`
- bit view vs. encoding: `internal/sequencer/fips.go:62-70`, surfaced as a warning at `report.go:207-212`

Nothing anywhere says the FIPS verdict is a whole-stream verdict rather than a per-position one. An operator who knows Burp will read the "FIPS 140-2 bit-level tests" heading (`pages/sequencer.tsx:80`) as the per-position battery they know.

## Decision needed before code
1. Re-shape the FIPS battery to run per bit position, as Burp does. Requires deciding what to do about thresholds: Burp "adjusts the FIPS pass criteria to work with random sample sizes" (`tests.html`) and notes that formal compliance needs 20,000 tokens. That adjustment is exactly the confidently-wrong-number risk `fips.go:11-20` was written to avoid, so it needs a stated method, not a fudge.
2. Keep the block model and disclose it — one sentence under the FIPS heading saying the verdict describes the stream, not individual bit positions.

(2) is small and should happen regardless of whether (1) is scheduled.

## Classification
UX DIVERGENCE in the statistics, plus a missing disclosure.

## What an operator cannot do
Say which bit positions of a token are non-random — so they cannot distinguish a token with a fixed prefix from one that is uniformly weak, which is the finding Burp's bit-level tab exists to produce.
acceptance_criteria: The FIPS section either reports per-bit-position results naming the failing bits, or states in the UI that its verdict describes the whole bit stream rather than individual bit positions. The disclosure half lands even if the per-position work is deferred.

title: auditqueue: no base request/response viewer for a queue item
description:
## Claim

The Audit queue shows no request or response for a queue item. An operator can see what the audit
decided about an exchange but not the exchange it decided it about.

## burpsy side

`pages/auditqueue.tsx` renders one `SimpleTable` with headers
`["Seq", "Request", "State", "Attempts", "Note", ""]` (`:64`). The "Request" cell is a text line —
`{item.method} {item.tls ? "https" : "http"}://{item.host}...{item.path}` (`:70-78`). There is no
`HttpEditor` import (`:1-14`) and no message pane anywhere on the page.

Compare the two pages that do this properly: `pages/sitemap.tsx:456-471` and `pages/scanner.tsx:585,
602` both mount `HttpEditor` for the selected row's bytes.

Positive control on the same file: `grep -n "Audit again" pages/auditqueue.tsx` -> `:97`.

## Burp side

`map_root.tsv` class `burp.Zr_7` — `auditItemsTable` alongside `Base request`, `Base response`,
`auditItemsTableRequestResponseViewer`, `auditItemsTableRequestMessageAnalyzer` and
`auditItemsTableResponseMessageAnalyzer`. Burp's Audit items view is a table over a message viewer,
the same shape as its history and site map views.

## Classification

CAPABILITY GAP.

## What an operator cannot do

Tell why an item was bounded, skipped or failed. The `note` column gives the engine's reason; the base
request is what makes that reason legible — a 500 on the base response, or a session cookie that
expired, is invisible today.

## Note

The exchange id is already on the row (`item.exchange_id`, used by the Audit-again call at `:91`), and
`useMessage` already fetches bytes by message id elsewhere. The missing piece is resolving
`exchange_id` -> request/response message ids on this page the way `pages/scanner.tsx:290, 323-329`
does it.
acceptance_criteria: Selecting an audit-queue item shows its base request and response bytes on the page.

title: scope: an existing rule cannot be edited — only removed and retyped
description:
## Claim

An existing scope rule cannot be edited. The only way to change one is to remove it and retype the
whole tuple.

This is distinct from burpsy-react-ui-c09 (advanced scope control / save-to-library): that issue is
about rule *expressiveness*, this one is about editing a rule that already exists at all.

## burpsy side

`pages/scope.tsx` has exactly three mutating controls:

- `addRule()` (`:43-68`), driven by the form at `:163-194`
- `removeSelected()` (`:70-84`), the "Remove rule" button at `:202-206`
- Clear scope (`:141-152`)

Row selection sets `selected` (`:213-214`) and is used only by `removeSelected`. There is no edit
affordance and no `PUT`-shaped action — `useUpdateScope` takes `action: "include" | "exclude" |
"remove" | "clear"` only (`lib/data.policy.ts`, per the call sites at `:56`, `:75`, `:147`).

Absence grep on the file: `grep -riE "edit|paste|load from|import" pages/scope.tsx` returns only the
`import` statements at `:1-7`. Positive control on the same file: `grep -n "Add rule" pages/scope.tsx`
-> `:192`.

## Burp side

`map_root.tsv` class `burp.Zry2` (`configPanelTargetScope`) — `Add a new item`,
**`Edit the selected item`**, `Remove the selected item`. Edit is a first-class button next to Add and
Remove in both the include and exclude tables.

## Classification

CAPABILITY GAP (small, high-frequency).

## What an operator cannot do

Fix a typo, or narrow `*.example.com` to `api.example.com`, without deleting the rule and re-entering
host, port, path and protocol from scratch. On a five-arm rule that is five fields retyped to change
one.
acceptance_criteria: Selecting a scope rule allows editing its arms in place and saving, with the edit replacing exactly that tuple.

title: intercept: the held-message context menu has no Send to Repeater and no send-to matrix, unlike every other HTTP table
description:
VERIFIED against HEAD by AuditProxy (Proxy-screen parity audit, 2026-08-27).

Right-clicking a held message offers Forward and Drop only. Every other burpsy
table with HTTP rows offers the full send-to matrix; Intercept is the one that
does not.

## Burp-side evidence

BurpClass11441.java -- proxyInterceptTablePopup (:64) carries Forward and Drop
AND the send-to entries:
  :96-98    "Drop"    (proxyInterceptTablePopupDropMenuItem)
  :103-105  "Forward" (proxyInterceptTablePopupForwardMenuItem)
  :139      "Send to Repeater"
  :123-124  "Send to Comparer (requests)" / "Send to Comparer (responses)"
  :142      "Send to Comparer"
  :177-178  "Send to Comparer (request)" / "Send to Comparer (response)"
  :185-187  "Request in browser" -> "In original session" / "In current session"

The same matrix is section 5.1 of
/root/burp-re/BURP_SUITE_UI_UX_SPECIFICATION.md, which states it is invoked
"on any HTTP Message editor or History table row".

## burpsy-side evidence

pages/intercept.tsx:728-754 -- menuGroups is a single group, id "intercept",
containing exactly two actions: `forward` (:736) and `drop` (:747). Nothing else.

The page never imports the shared action factory. Contrast the two pages that do
and therefore get the whole matrix:
  pages/history.tsx:5     import { useExchangeActions, exchangeUrl } ...
  pages/wshistory.tsx:8   import { useExchangeActions } ...
  pages/wshistory.tsx:174 return actions.menu(exchangeDetail.data)

So the mechanism already exists and is wired on two sibling pages; Intercept is
not using it.

## Classification

CAPABILITY GAP.

## What an operator cannot do

Fork a copy of a held request to Repeater while KEEPING the original held. Today
the message must be forwarded or dropped first, so the operator loses the hold
-- and forking to Repeater from an intercepted request is the single most common
action taken from Burp's Intercept tab.

## Note

A held message is not yet an Exchange (it has no response and no history id), so
`actions.menu` cannot be passed a HeldMessageDetail unchanged. Deciding what a
send-to does with a message that has no recorded exchange is the one design
question here: sending the raw bytes to Repeater needs no exchange id, whereas
"Show in HTTP history" has nothing to point at until the message is forwarded.
acceptance_criteria: A held message can be sent to Repeater (and the other send-to targets that make sense without a recorded exchange) from its context menu while remaining held; actions that require an exchange id are either omitted or disabled with a stated reason rather than failing.
close_reason: 63e101b8164900cbcd08697a60c61cda3dcab2d5. pages/intercept.tsx now builds heldMenu(row: HeldMessageDetail) and passes it as the VirtualTable menuGroups and as the held-bytes editor's menuGroups. Four groups: send (Repeater, Comparer A, Comparer B, Decoder), 'Resolve the hold' (Forward, Drop - unchanged semantics, still row.raw and still fixContentLength, per 3g5), copy (URL, curl, request to file) and scope (add host to scope, open in browser). Send to Repeater copies the bytes into a new tab and leaves the hold intact, which was the point of the issue - the toast says so explicitly. Per the acceptance criteria's second clause, the one action needing an exchange id is OMITTED with the reason stated in the code: Send to Intruder splices payloads into a stored message id, which a held message does not have; the docstring points the operator at Repeater's own hand-off (which sends once to create the stored message) or at HTTP history after forwarding. 'Show in HTTP history' is likewise absent - it has nothing to point at. tsc --noEmit clean.

title: ui: Ctrl+R reloads the browser on every table page, including HTTP history — not just outside it
description:
## Claim
Ctrl+R and Ctrl+I only work on the HTTP history page. On a selected Site map, Logger or WebSockets history row, Ctrl+R falls through to the browser and reloads the console.

## Burp-side evidence
- Spec `BURP_SUITE_UI_UX_SPECIFICATION.md` section 5.2 scopes both bindings to *"HTTP Message / Table Row"* — not to one tool.
- `tools/organizer/index.html` (bundled docs) states the same pattern for the sibling binding: *"You can send HTTP messages to Burp Organizer from other Burp tools by right-clicking one or more selected messages and selecting Send to Organizer. Alternatively, you can use the default hotkey Ctrl + O"*.

## burpsy-side evidence
- Installed only in `pages/history.tsx:614-633` (`"mod+r"` and `"mod+i"`, both `event.preventDefault()` on a `selected` row).
- `grep -c useHotkeys` -> **0** in each of `pages/sitemap.tsx`, `pages/logger.tsx`, `pages/wshistory.tsx`, `pages/scanner.tsx`. Positive control on the same files: they import and render `VirtualTable` and pass `menuGroups` (`pages/sitemap.tsx:548`, `pages/logger.tsx:354`, `pages/wshistory.tsx:213`), so row selection state exists on each — only the binding is missing.
- Because nothing calls `preventDefault` on those pages, Ctrl+R reaches the browser: the console reloads and the operator loses their filter and selection.

## Classification
CAPABILITY GAP.

## What an operator cannot do
Send a Site map row to Repeater from the keyboard — the normal way to work a site map in Burp. Pressing the key they have used for years actively destroys their page state instead.

## Related
Fix alongside the keymap defect (rebinding these does nothing) rather than duplicating the literals onto three more pages.
acceptance_criteria: Three holes, all of which let Ctrl+R reach the browser. (1) DONE in 63e101b: with a row selected on Site map and WebSockets history the chord sends to Repeater and calls preventDefault; the chords come from the keymap registry, not literals. (2) OPEN: with NO row selected, preventDefault is never reached on any table page including HTTP history, so the first Ctrl+R after a page load reloads the console — preventDefault must move above the selection guard, with a toast so the swallowed key is not merely dead. (3) OPEN: with focus in a form field the bindings do not fire at all (enableOnFormTags: false), so Ctrl+R in the DSL query box or a column filter reloads the console — needs enableOnFormTags: true, as intercept.tsx already uses. Requires a product decision on whether burpsy may swallow the browser's reload unconditionally. Logger is out of scope: ToolLogRow carries no message or exchange id, so it has nothing to send; needs a backend change first.

comments.author: FixMenusHotkeys
comments.text:
PARTIALLY FIXED in 63e101b8164900cbcd08697a60c61cda3dcab2d5 — deliberately NOT closed, because the acceptance criteria name Logger and Logger is not satisfied.

DONE. lib/actions.ts gains useSendShortcuts(exchange), which installs send.repeater, send.intruder and send.organizer from the keymap registry (not literals — that was the 9td half, now closed). Called on pages/history.tsx, pages/sitemap.tsx and pages/wshistory.tsx. On those three pages a selected row's ctrl+R sends to Repeater and calls preventDefault, so the browser reload — the urgent half — is gone. preventDefault fires only when a row is actually in hand, matching the previous history.tsx semantics: with nothing selected there is no send to make, so the key is left to the browser rather than swallowed into a no-op.

NOT DONE, and it is not a matter of adding a call. Logger cannot send anything to Repeater or Intruder. Its rows are ToolLogRow (lib/types.workbench.ts:271) — {id, tool, host, port, method, path, status, response_len, started_ms, duration_ms, error}. There is no request message id, no response message id and no exchange id, and the page's own menu already says so: 'Copy as curl (request line only)' with the toast 'the log stores no headers or body' (pages/logger.tsx:369-375). Binding ctrl+R there would either fabricate a request or swallow the browser's reload for a no-op; neither is worth doing.

AUDIT CORRECTION. The issue's evidence says the three pages 'import and render VirtualTable and pass menuGroups ... so row selection state exists on each — only the binding is missing.' That is true of Site map and WebSockets history. It is not true of Logger: selection state exists, but the thing to send does not. This is a backend gap, not a UI one.

TO CLOSE THIS: the tool log needs to record the request (and response) message ids it already has server-side, or an exchange id, so a logged row can resolve to an Exchange. That is a .go change and is outside this unit's ownership. Suggest re-scoping this issue to Site map + WebSockets history and opening a separate backend issue for the Logger row shape.

title: ui: Highlight and Add comment are missing from the row context menu, and absent entirely outside HTTP history
description:
## Claim
Highlight and Add comment are not in any row context menu. They exist only as fields in the HTTP history detail pane, so annotating is a per-row round trip through that pane, and rows on Site map, Logger and WebSockets history cannot be annotated at all.

## Burp-side evidence
- `tools/context-menu.html` (Burp bundled docs) lists as universal menu options: **Add comment** — *"Enables you to add text comments to the selected items"*; **Add notes** — *"Enables you to record text notes for the selected items"*; **Highlight** — *"Marks the selected items with a color label for easy identification"*. All apply to a selection, i.e. multiple rows at once.
- `tools/proxy/http-history/filter-settings.html` has a dedicated *"Filter by annotation - This enables you to only show items with notes or highlights"*, so annotate-then-filter is a first-class triage loop in Burp.

## burpsy-side evidence
- The backend supports it: `internal/web/api_capture.go:145-183` `PATCH /api/exchange/{id}` with `notes` and `highlight`; `lib/data.ts:357-361` `useAnnotateExchange`. Both are queryable DSL fields (`lib/reference.ts:99-101,157-159`).
- `HighlightPicker` is defined at `pages/history.tsx:252` and rendered **once**, at `pages/history.tsx:813` — inside the detail pane, not the row menu. (`grep -n HighlightPicker pages/history.tsx` -> 2 hits: the definition and that one usage.)
- The note field is likewise a detail-pane textarea (`pages/history.tsx:640-650` `saveNote`).
- `lib/actions.ts:782-834` `menu()` — the shared row menu used by History, Site map, Logger and WebSockets history — contains groups `send`, `request-edits`, `copy`, `organise`, `scope-scan`, `engage`. No highlight group and no comment group.
- Consequence: `pages/sitemap.tsx:548`, `pages/logger.tsx:354` and `pages/wshistory.tsx:213` pass `actions.menu(row)` and so offer no annotation path of any kind.

## Classification
UX DIVERGENCE on History (present but relocated); CAPABILITY GAP on Site map, Logger and WebSockets history (absent).

## What an operator cannot do
Triage by colour. In Burp: select rows, right-click, Highlight red. Here: select one row, look down to the detail pane, click a swatch, select the next row, repeat — and outside HTTP history there is no way to mark a row at all, even though `highlight = "red"` is a queryable filter.
acceptance_criteria: DONE in 63e101b: the shared row menu from lib/actions.ts menu() carries a Highlight submenu (all ten HIGHLIGHTS colours including the clear sentinel, each with a colour chip drawn from the same --highlight-* properties as the detail pane's picker) and an Add comment / Edit comment action, landing on HTTP history, Site map, WebSockets history and the Scanner issue leaf at once. REMAINS: Logger. Its rows are ToolLogRow (lib/types.workbench.ts:271) with no exchange id and no message ids, and PATCH /api/exchange/{id} needs an exchange id, so there is nothing to annotate. The Dashboard's recent-activity table (ActivityRow) has the identical shape and limitation. Both need the tool log to carry an exchange id — the same backend change that closes the Logger remainder of burpsy-react-ui-bc2. Note one deliberate divergence in what shipped: Add comment uses window.prompt rather than a modal, because menu() is a plain function called from six pages and a dialog would mean each owning open/target/draft state for a single-line string; the detail pane's textarea stays for multi-line notes.

comments.author: FixMenusHotkeys
comments.text:
PARTIALLY FIXED in 63e101b8164900cbcd08697a60c61cda3dcab2d5 — deliberately NOT closed, because the acceptance criteria name Logger and Logger is not satisfied.

DONE. lib/actions.ts's menu() gains an 'annotate' group, placed directly above 'organise':
- Highlight, as a real submenu (ui/menu.tsx gained submenu support for it, since Burp's colour picker is one), carrying all ten HIGHLIGHTS values including the 'none' clear sentinel. Each row shows an actual colour chip, built from the same --highlight-* custom properties the detail pane's HighlightPicker uses, so the two swatch sets cannot drift (ui/highlight-icons.tsx). The currently-set colour renders disabled rather than hidden, so 'which one is set' is answerable from the menu. Fires useAnnotateExchange straight off — one PATCH, visible in the row immediately, and picking another colour is the undo.
- Add comment / Edit comment (the label follows whether the row already has a note), seeded with the row's existing note.

Because the four surfaces that call actions.menu() share that factory, this lands on HTTP history, Site map, WebSockets history (the connection list) and the Scanner issue leaf's exchange section at once. History no longer needs the select-row / look-down / click-swatch / select-next round trip, and Site map and WebSockets history can be marked at all — which matters exactly as the issue argues, since highlight and notes are queryable DSL fields, so a row that cannot be marked cannot be found again.

ONE DELIBERATE DIVERGENCE, stated here because it is a real trade and not an oversight. Add comment uses window.prompt, not a modal. menu() is a plain function called on every right-click from six pages; a dialog would mean each of those pages owning open/target/draft state for a single-line string. The detail pane's textarea deliberately stays — that is where multi-line prose belongs. Cancel is left alone; clearing the box to empty is sent as null, which is the PATCH endpoint's 'unset'.

NOT DONE. Logger. Its rows are ToolLogRow (lib/types.workbench.ts:271) with no exchange id and no message ids — the log records that one of burpsy's own tools sent a request, not the request. PATCH /api/exchange/{id} needs an exchange id, so there is nothing to annotate. The Dashboard's recent-activity table (ActivityRow) has the same shape and the same limitation, noted in its own code comment.

AUDIT CORRECTION. The issue's classification reads 'CAPABILITY GAP on Site map, Logger and WebSockets history (absent)'. For Site map and WebSockets history that was right and is now fixed. For Logger it is a backend data-shape gap, not a menu gap: the annotation route exists and works, the row has no id to aim it at.

TO CLOSE THIS: the tool log rows need an exchange id (or their own annotation storage). Same blocker as burpsy-react-ui-bc2, same suggested split — one backend issue for the ToolLogRow shape closes both remainders.

comments.author: FixMenusHotkeys
comments.text:
SCOPE NOTE for the inventory. This issue is two-thirds a shared fix and one-third a backend blocker, and the split is clean.

The shared part cost almost nothing once ui/menu.tsx had submenu support: menu() is the single factory behind History, Site map, WebSockets history and the Scanner leaf, so adding one 'annotate' group lit up four surfaces at once. The submenu support itself (Radix Sub/SubTrigger/SubContent threaded through a MenuParts bundle, so context menus and dropdowns cannot diverge) is the reusable asset and is what Burp's severity and confidence pickers will need when /api/issues gains PATCH — see burpsy-react-ui-3fr.

The blocker is the same one as burpsy-react-ui-bc2's Logger remainder: tool-log rows carry no exchange id. ONE backend change — putting the exchange id (or the request/response message ids) on ToolLogRow — closes the Logger half of both issues at once. Worth pairing them in the plan rather than estimating them separately.

VALIDITY: valid, and the 'UX DIVERGENCE on History / CAPABILITY GAP elsewhere' classification was exactly right. Nothing in the issue's evidence was wrong except the implication that Logger was a menu problem.

title: sequencer: character transition, spectral, correlation and compression tests are all absent from the randomness battery
description:
## Claim
Four of the eight randomness tests Burp Sequencer runs are absent: character transition analysis, the spectral test, the correlation test, and the compression test.

## Burp-side evidence
`tools/sequencer/results/tests.html` enumerates the battery in full. Character-level ("Two different character-level tests are performed at each character position"):
1. **Character count analysis** — distribution of characters at each position.
2. **Character transition analysis** — "analyzes the transitions between successive tokens in the sample. If the sample is randomly generated, a character appearing at a given position is equally likely to be followed in the next token by any one of the characters that is used at that position."

Bit-level:
3. FIPS monobit test
4. FIPS poker test
5. FIPS runs test
6. FIPS long runs test
7. **Spectral tests** — "treats each series of consecutive numbers as coordinates in a multi-dimensional space […] repeated for multiple sizes of number (between 1 and 8 bits) and for multiple numbers of dimensions (between 2 and 6). This test can identify evidence of non-randomness in some samples that pass the other statistical tests."
8. **Correlation test** — "tests for any statistically significant relationships between the values at different bit positions within the tokens. […] This test enables you to assess the amount of randomness in the token as a whole. This is important as each of the bit-level tests operates only on individual bit positions."
9. **Compression test** — "attempts to compress the bit sequence at each position using standard ZLIB compression. The results indicate the proportional reduction in the size of the bit sequence when it is compressed."

(Nine named tests; four FIPS members are one family, hence "eight" as an operator counts them.)

`BURP_SUITE_UI_UX_SPECIFICATION.md` §4.8 lists "FIPS poker" and "Spectral" among the recovered Sequencer config strings, confirming both are per-test toggles in the shipped product.

## burpsy-side evidence
The whole implemented set is in `internal/sequencer/`:
- Character count: `internal/sequencer/report.go:290` `AnalyseChars` — per-position counts and entropy.
- FIPS monobit: `internal/sequencer/fips.go:420`
- FIPS poker: `internal/sequencer/fips.go:440`
- FIPS runs: `internal/sequencer/fips.go:387` with `runIntervals` at `fips.go:53-60`
- FIPS long runs: `internal/sequencer/fips.go:391`

`testBlock` (`internal/sequencer/fips.go:453`) computes exactly the four FIPS statistics and nothing else; `blockResult` (`fips.go:371-377`) has exactly four fields. `FipsTest.ID` is documented as `"monobit" | "poker" | "runs" | "long_runs"` (`fips.go:301`).

Absent: no transition, spectral, correlation, or compression computation anywhere in the package. The rendered report is the FIPS four plus per-position character stats — `internal/web/ui/src/pages/sequencer.tsx:87-101` (the FIPS table) and `:152-180` (the positions table).

Separately implemented but **not reachable from the web report**: `ChiSquare` (`internal/sequencer/sequencer.go:137`), `SerialCorrelation` (`:156`), `MonteCarloPi` (`:180`), `DetectPatterns` (`:209`). Their only non-test caller is the CLI, `cmd/burpsy/cli_tools.go:361-370`. `SerialCorrelation` is not Burp's correlation test (it correlates successive character codes, not values at different bit positions), so it is not a substitute — but it does mean the web Sequencer reports less than burpsy's own CLI.

## Classification
CAPABILITY GAP — one capability (the randomness battery), four named members missing.

## What an operator cannot do
Reach the verdict Burp's docs single out the spectral test for: catching non-randomness in a sample that passes every other test. The correlation test's absence is the one with a stated consequence in Burp's own documentation — without it, a token whose bit positions are individually random but mutually dependent scores as high-entropy.
acceptance_criteria: The analysis report names and reports a result for character transition analysis, the spectral test, the correlation test and the compression test alongside the existing FIPS four, each with the observed statistic rather than a bare pass/fail. Any test that cannot run on the supplied sample reports "not tested" with the reason, matching the existing FIPS-below-one-block behaviour.

title: dashboard: New scan takes one seed URL though the engine and the site-map launcher take many
description:
## Claim

The Dashboard's "New scan" dialog accepts a single seed URL, while the crawl engine and a second
launcher in the same codebase both accept many.

## burpsy side

`pages/dashboard.tsx:259-261` — one `Input`:

    <Field label="Seed URL">
      {(id) => <Input id={id} value={seed} ... placeholder="https://demo.local/" />}

and the submit at `:222-236` sends `seeds: [seed.trim()]` — a one-element array.

The multi-seed form already exists: `ui/crawl.tsx:56-70`, `label="Seed URLs"`, hint "One per line, or
comma separated", splitting on `/[\s,]+/` at `:28-31`. It is rendered from the **Site map** header
(`pages/sitemap.tsx:636` `<CrawlLauncher />`), not from the Dashboard.

So the engine, the wire and a working UI all support N seeds; only the dialog a Burp user reaches for
does not.

Positive control on the same file: `grep -n "Seed URL" pages/dashboard.tsx` -> `:259`.

## Burp side

Burp's Scan details page is a multi-line "URLs to scan" box, described in `map_root.tsv` class
`burp.Zhwl`: *"Define the URLs to scan. Burp will begin crawling from these URLs, and by default will
include everything beneath the specified URLs' folders."*

## Classification

UX DIVERGENCE — the capability exists, the Dashboard dialog just cannot express it.

## What an operator cannot do

Start one scan across the three hosts of an application from the Dashboard. They must either run three
scans or go find the other launcher on a different tab.

## Note

Smallest honest fix is to have the New scan dialog reuse `CrawlLauncher`'s seed field rather than grow
a second parser — two split-and-trim implementations of the same input is how they come to disagree.
acceptance_criteria: The Dashboard's New scan dialog accepts multiple seed URLs, parsed by the same code path as ui/crawl.tsx, and starts one task covering all of them.

title: intercept: the target host/port/TLS of a held request cannot be edited before forwarding
description:
VERIFIED against HEAD by AuditProxy (Proxy-screen parity audit, 2026-08-27).

A held request's destination is display-only in burpsy. Burp lets the operator
click the target and change it before forwarding.

## Burp-side evidence

BurpClass9694.java -- the intercept header bar:
  :197  setName("proxyInterceptTargetLabel")
  :206  setName("proxyInterceptEditTargetButton")
  :66   the pencil action, labelled "Edit target"
  :109  setToolTipText(var2 ? "Click to modify" : null)
  :195  setText("https://ginandjuice.shop")   -- the label shows the authority

## burpsy-side evidence

The authority is rendered twice, read-only both times:
  pages/intercept.tsx:485-490   the "Host" column, accessorFn returning
                                `${row.host}:${row.port}${row.tls ? " (tls)" : ""}`
  pages/intercept.tsx:512-516   the detail head, static text

The wire carries no destination field. The forward request body is exactly three
keys:
  internal/web/api_intercept.go:333
    struct { Raw *string; FixContentLength bool `json:"fix_content_length"` }
    keyed by id
and the engine signature matches:
  internal/intercept/intercept.go:670
    func (e *Engine) Forward(id uint64, edited *string, fixContentLength bool) error

There is no host, port or TLS parameter on either, so the capability is absent
end to end and not merely unrendered.

## Classification

CAPABILITY GAP.

## What an operator cannot do

Redirect a held request to a different host, port or scheme before releasing it
-- Burp's standard move for replaying a production request against a staging
origin, or for steering a request at an internal host reached through the proxy.
Today the only route is Drop, then hand-edit in Repeater, which loses the
client's waiting connection.

## Note on scope

Editing the target changes where bytes go, so the held message's recorded
authority and the history row it produces must reflect the destination actually
used, not the one the client asked for -- internal/proxy/ws.go:166 already sets
the precedent for annotating a request that was altered before forwarding.
acceptance_criteria: A held request's destination host, port and TLS flag can be changed from the Intercept detail pane before forwarding; the relay dials the edited destination; the recorded history row states the destination actually used.

title: sequencer: no "Send to Sequencer" action exists, so every capture starts by hand-copying a request
description:
## Claim
There is no "Send to Sequencer" action anywhere in the UI, so a live capture requires the operator to transcribe a request that is already in history.

## Burp-side evidence
`tools/sequencer/sample/index.html` ("Configuring a live capture of tokens"):
> "Locate a request that returns a token that you want to analyze. Right-click the request and choose **Send to Sequencer** from the context menu. You can send a request from anywhere in Burp. Select the token in the Token location within response panel. Click Start live capture."

`tools/sequencer/getting-started.html` makes it step 3 of 8 of the canonical workflow, and step 4 notes the sent entry "is automatically selected in the Select live capture request panel."

`BURP_SUITE_UI_UX_SPECIFICATION.md` §4.8 lists "Select Request source (from History/Repeater)" as a Sequencer view.

## burpsy-side evidence
Absence-grep across the whole UI tree, excluding the Sequencer's own three files:
```
$ cd internal/web/ui/src && grep -rn "equencer" --include=*.ts --include=*.tsx . \
    | grep -v "^./pages/sequencer.tsx\|^./lib/data.workbench.ts\|^./lib/types.workbench.ts"
nav.ts:38:import { SequencerPage } from "./pages/sequencer";
nav.ts:157:    id: "sequencer",
nav.ts:158:    label: "Sequencer",
nav.ts:162:      { id: "sequencer", label: "Sequencer", description: "Token randomness analysis", page: SequencerPage },
ui/hex-editor.tsx:63:  /** Absent means read-only — a captured response, a sequencer token. */
```
Routing and one comment. No action, no menu entry, no store hand-off.

Positive control on the same files the action would live in — `grep -rn "Send to\|sendTo"` over the same tree returns the full existing matrix, so those files are readable:
`internal/web/ui/src/lib/actions.ts:366-371` is the complete context menu send group — Repeater, Intruder, Comparer (A), Comparer (B), Decoder. `lib/actions.ts:142-151` declares the matching action types. Sequencer is in neither.

What the operator does instead, on `internal/web/ui/src/pages/sequencer.tsx`:
- pastes raw request bytes into the "Request to repeat" editor (`:428-436`)
- types the target URL (`:438-447`)
- types a cookie name, header name, or RE2 body pattern (`:448-479`)

## Classification
CAPABILITY GAP.

## What an operator cannot do
Start a Sequencer capture from a request they already have. Every capture begins by hand-copying a request out of HTTP history and retyping the authority.

## Note
The related gap — that the token location is typed rather than picked from a dropdown of cookies actually present in the response, and that Burp's **Form field** location has no counterpart — is filed separately. The declared-not-guessed design is deliberate and disclosed at `pages/sequencer.tsx:422-425`; the missing hand-off is not.
acceptance_criteria: The row context menu and the detail-pane action bar in HTTP history and Site map offer "Send to Sequencer", and it lands the exchange's request bytes and authority in the Sequencer's live-capture tab without the operator typing either.

title: site map: nothing can be deleted from the map — /api/sitemap is read-only
description:
## Claim

Nothing can be removed from the site map. `/api/sitemap` is registered as a read-only handler, so a map
polluted by a mistargeted crawl stays polluted for the life of the process.

## burpsy side

`internal/web/server.go:818`

    s.mux.HandleFunc("/api/sitemap", s.handleSitemap)

and the handler, `internal/web/api_toolkit.go:82-90`, documents itself as
`GET /api/sitemap?host=&path=&depth=`. It is the only sitemap route.

Absence grep: `grep -rniE "delete host|delete branch|remove.*from.*site ?map"` over
`internal/web/ui/src`, `internal/sitemap/` and `internal/web/*.go` returns nothing but unrelated
backup-pruning hits in `api_backup.go` and `settings.tsx`. Positive control on the same file set:
`grep -n "sitemap" internal/web/server.go` -> `:25`, `:58`, `:189`, `:210-212`, `:647-648`, `:818`.

`pages/sitemap.tsx` has no delete control on the tree, the contents table, or the header.

## Burp side

`map_root.tsv` class `burp.Zxut` — `Delete host`, `Delete branch`, `Delete item`,
`Delete selected items`. Burp also ships a bulk variant, `burp.Zraa`:
`Remove out-of-scope items (based on current suite scope)`.

## Classification

CAPABILITY GAP.

## What an operator cannot do

Clean up. A crawl that wandered onto a CDN or a staging host leaves those hosts in the tree
permanently, inflating every node count and every subsequent "scan this branch" target.

## Note before coding

The site map is a projection: `internal/web/server.go:212` wires `s.sitemap.Follow(store)`, so the tree
is derived from the exchange store. Deleting a branch therefore needs a decision — does it delete the
underlying exchanges (which HTTP history and findings both reference), or does the site map grow a
suppression set that `Follow` respects? The second is almost certainly right and is the smaller change,
but it should be chosen explicitly rather than discovered mid-implementation.
acceptance_criteria: A host, branch or item can be removed from the site map; the decision on whether removal suppresses or deletes underlying exchanges is recorded, and node counts reflect the removal.

title: intercept: no 'Forward all', though 'Drop all' exists — the destructive half of Burp's pair shipped without the safe half
description:
VERIFIED against HEAD by AuditProxy (Proxy-screen parity audit, 2026-08-27).

burpsy has "Drop all" but not "Forward all". In Burp the two are a symmetric
pair on the same toolbar, built from the same dropdown pattern. burpsy shipped
the destructive half and not the safe half.

## Burp-side evidence

The Forward button carries a dropdown (proxyForwardOptionsButton) offering both
entries, and the button itself relabels:

  BurpClass11143.java:35   new BurpClass11151(ZF, "Forward")
  BurpClass11143.java:43   setName("proxyForwardRequestButton")
  BurpClass11143.java:48   setName("proxyForwardOptionsButton")
  BurpClass11143.java:91   new BurpClass10899("Forward")
  BurpClass11143.java:93   new BurpClass10899("Forward all")
  BurpClass11143.java:145  setText("Forward all")

Its exact mirror for Drop is BurpClass11154.java:70-72 ("Drop" / "Drop all").

## burpsy-side evidence

`grep -rni "forward.all\|forwardAll"` across --include=*.go --include=*.tsx
--include=*.ts returns ZERO matches.

Positive control, same files and same directories: DropAll IS found --
  internal/intercept/intercept.go:724   func (e *Engine) DropAll(reason string) int
  internal/web/api_intercept.go:172     handleInterceptDropAll
  internal/web/api_intercept.go:184     s.intercept.DropAll(req.Reason)
  internal/web/server.go:810            /api/intercept/drop-all

So the absence is real, not a grep artefact.

The toolbar at pages/intercept.tsx:587-608 has exactly three buttons: Forward
(:587), Drop (:591), Drop all (:600). Drop all was added by
burpsy-react-ui-t6f; Forward all was not part of it.

## Classification

CAPABILITY GAP.

## What an operator cannot do

Release a queue in one action. An operator who wrote too broad an interception
rule and is now holding 40 messages can discard them all with one click but must
forward them one at a time, re-selecting a row between each.

## Note on the engine

Engine.Forward is per-id and takes an edit buffer
(internal/intercept/intercept.go:670, `Forward(id uint64, edited *string,
fixContentLength bool)`), so a bulk forward needs a decision about the edit
buffer: forward-all should send each held message's ORIGINAL bytes, never the
selected row's buffer -- that confusion is exactly what burpsy-react-ui-3g5
fixed for the row context menu, and the same trap is open here.
acceptance_criteria: The Intercept toolbar can forward every held message in one action; each message is forwarded with its own original bytes, not the selected row's edit buffer; the count actually forwarded is reported the way Drop all reports its count.
close_reason: Forward all shipped: engine ForwardAll (mirrors DropAll once-only gate + single signal, forwards held bytes unmodified — nil would wake the client to an empty message), POST /api/intercept/forward-all answering the honest count, toolbar button between Forward and Drop all with the queue-moved toast, no confirmation needed for the safe direction. Verified manually in agent-browser: 3 held -> one click -> queue empty, clients unblocked with own bytes, history rows present. Engine test TestEngine_ForwardAllForwardsEveryHeldMessageUnmodifiedAndCountsOnlyItsOwn, web tests, route manifest, UI unit 157/0 green. Commits: see forward-all commit on ui-react-comparison.

title: ui: the Render view does not render image responses, only HTML
description:
## Claim
The Render view is offered only for HTML responses. Burp's Render tab also renders image responses, so a captured image in burpsy can only be read as raw bytes or a hex dump.

## Burp-side evidence
- `tools/message-editor/index.html` (bundled docs), Render tab: *"This tab applies to HTTP responses containing HTML **or image** content. It attempts to render the contents of the message body in the form it would appear when displayed in a browser."*

## burpsy-side evidence
- `burpsy-go/internal/web/ui/src/ui/editor.tsx:250` — `const renderable = useMemo(() => response && /html/i.test(contentTypeOf(value)), [response, value]);`
- `:269` gates the tab on that flag; `:347-355` renders through `<iframe sandbox="" srcDoc={bodyOf(value)} />`, which is an HTML-only mechanism.
- An `image/png` or `image/jpeg` response therefore has `available = ["raw","hex"]` and no Render tab.

## Classification
CAPABILITY GAP.

## What an operator cannot do
Look at a captured image — a CAPTCHA, a QR code, an IDOR'd avatar, an exposed document scan or a chart that leaks data. These are ordinary findings and the evidence is in the response body burpsy already stored.
acceptance_criteria: Selecting a response whose Content-Type is an image type offers a Render view that displays the decoded image; the existing HTML path is unchanged.

title: ui: the message editor cannot display non-printing characters (no newline/CR/NUL toggle)
description:
## Claim
The message editor has no control to reveal non-printing characters. Burp has a `\n` toggle above every message, documented specifically for request smuggling, header injection and null-byte work.

## Burp-side evidence
- `tools/message-editor/text-editor.html` (bundled docs), Non-printing characters: *"By default, non-printing characters in HTTP requests and responses are hidden. To display them, click [\n]. This is supported for any bytes with a hexadecimal code point lower than 20, which includes tabs, line feeds, carriage returns, and null bytes. Characters with code points from 7F to FF are also supported."* Listed uses: *"Spot subtle differences between byte values in responses. Experiment with HTTP request smuggling vulnerabilities. Study line endings to identify potential HTTP header injection vulnerabilities. Observe how null-byte injections are handled by the server."*
- `tools/message-editor/index.html`, Raw tab: *"You can use the \n button to toggle whether non-printing characters are displayed."*

## burpsy-side evidence
Absence grep over the whole UI tree:
`grep -rli 'non-print|nonprint|unprintable|control char' --include=*.tsx --include=*.ts burpsy-go/internal/web/ui/src/` -> **no files**.
Same-tree positive control: `grep -rli 'Copy URL' --include=*.tsx --include=*.ts .` -> `pages/logger.tsx lib/actions.ts` (2 files), so the grep is reaching the tree.
The editor toolbar's full control set is `ui/editor.tsx:323-344`: Wrap, Copy, Save. No such toggle in `ui/hex-editor.tsx` either (it is a hex view, not a text-with-glyphs view).

## Classification
CAPABILITY GAP.

## What an operator cannot do
See whether a header line ends `\r\n` or bare `\n` while reading the message. The Hex view carries the same bytes but not the same reading task — a smuggling operator has to switch views and count offsets to answer a question Burp answers with one toggle in place.
acceptance_criteria: A toggle above each request/response renders bytes below 0x20 and 0x7F-0xFF as visible glyphs in the Pretty and Raw views, off by default, without changing the underlying bytes.
close_reason: Implemented in abdcb10. Pilcrow toggle above each request/response (Pretty/Raw only), off by default. Verified live in browser against real proxied traffic: toggle ON renders ␍␊ end-of-line markers (4 markers on a CRLF request), lines keep breaking, toggle ON→OFF leaves the document byte-identical (DOM text compared). Meets acceptance: bytes <0x20 as control pictures, 0x7F as ␡, 0x80-0xFF in marked spans with U+XXXX tooltips, underlying bytes untouched (pure CM decorations).

title: dashboard: no Issue activity feed — findings appear only as aggregate counts
description:
## Claim

The Dashboard has no Issue activity feed. Findings are shown only as aggregate severity counts, so
nothing tells an operator *which* issue was just raised.

## burpsy side

`pages/dashboard.tsx` renders five cards — Coverage (`:415`), Requests sent by burpsy (`:431`), Tool
events (`:436`), Tasks (`:456`), Traffic sources (`:476`) — plus the severity tile row at `:382-412`.

The tiles are counts pulled from `useIssues()`: `issues.data!.counts?.[severity]` (`:390`). They tell
you five went from 4 to 5; they do not tell you what the fifth was, and there is no link through.

"Tool events" is not this feed — it is `data.events` (`:440`), documented in its own subtitle as
"State changes that are not requests."

Absence grep: `grep -rniE "issue activity" internal/web/ui/src internal/dash` -> no match.
Positive control on the same tree: `grep -rn "Tool events" internal/web/ui/src` ->
`pages/dashboard.tsx:437`.

## Burp side

Issue activity is one of Burp's three Dashboard panels and one of the three tabs in every task's
detail window. `map_root.tsv` classes `burp.Zi96`, `burp.Zr_d`, `burp.Zr_f` and `burp.Zr_y` each carry
the same triple of labels: `Audit items`, `Issue activity`, `Event log`. The backing tree is
`siteMapIssueActivityTree` (`burp.Zhlv`), which is also what Burp hangs the per-issue context menu off.

## Classification

CAPABILITY GAP.

## What an operator cannot do

Watch findings arrive during a scan. The only signal today is a tile number changing between
refreshes, which gives no name, no host and no way in.

## Note

Cheap version first: the feed is a reverse-chronological list of findings with severity, name and host,
linking to the advisory. The finding store already has everything it needs — this is a view, not new
collection.
acceptance_criteria: The Dashboard carries a reverse-chronological feed of findings as they are raised, each naming severity, issue and host, and each opening its advisory.

title: ui: requests cannot be edited in the Pretty view — editing is refused outside Raw and Hex
description:
## Claim
Burp prettifies editable bodies as you type and lets you edit in the Pretty tab. burpsy refuses to accept edits on Pretty, so editing a minified JSON body in Repeater or Intercept has to be done on one unwrapped line in Raw.

## Burp-side evidence
- `tools/message-editor/index.html` (bundled docs), Pretty tab: *"In this tab, you can access all the same functionality as in the Raw tab. ... In editable messages, supported text formats are dynamically prettified as you type wherever possible. Otherwise, the text is prettified when you send the request."*
- `tools/message-editor/text-editor.html`: *"In editable messages, such as in Burp Repeater, supported text formats are dynamically prettified as you type."*

## burpsy-side evidence
- `burpsy-go/internal/web/ui/src/ui/editor.tsx:387` `onChange={active === "raw" ? onChange : undefined}`
- `:388-389` `editable={editable && active === "raw"}` / `readOnly={!(editable && active === "raw")}`
- `:415-417` renders the note *"Editing happens on the Raw and Hex views, which are the exact bytes."*
- Stated rationale at `:196-201`: *"Editing never happens on a derived view: a reformatted body is not the bytes that were sent, and silently sending the reformatted version would be a lie."*

## Classification
CAPABILITY GAP. The rationale is sound but Burp solves the same problem by reformatting on send rather than by refusing the edit, so this is a behaviour choice, not a constraint.

## What an operator cannot do
Edit a JSON body with any structure visible. In Repeater, changing one value in a 4KB minified body means finding it inside a single wrapped line in Raw.

## Decision needed
Whether to adopt Burp's model (accept edits on Pretty, re-derive the raw bytes on send / on blur, and show the operator what will actually be sent) or keep the current refusal. This needs a call before code: option (a) edit-on-Pretty with a normalise-on-send step; option (b) keep Raw-only but add a "Prettify in place" action that rewrites the actual bytes once, so the operator opts into the reformat explicitly.
acceptance_criteria: A decision is recorded, and either edits on the Pretty view are accepted and normalised into the sent bytes, or a explicit prettify-in-place action rewrites the message so subsequent Raw editing is on formatted bytes.
