Scan a response body structurally — pick out a script block, spot a parameter, see where a JSON value ends. And a URL-encoded parameter value in a request cannot be read without selecting it and pressing the decode chord, where Burp just shows it on hover.
acceptance_criteria: Response and request bodies are colourised by content type (JSON, HTML/XML, JavaScript, CSS), request parameters are distinguished, and hovering a URL- or HTML-encoded syntax item shows its decoded value.

title: certificate: the CA cannot be regenerated from the console — only imported or downloaded
description:
VERIFIED against HEAD by AuditProxy (Proxy-screen parity audit, 2026-08-27).

burpsy can import a CA and export the current one, but cannot generate a fresh
one. There is no rotation path from the console.

## Burp-side evidence

BurpClass9617.java, in the Proxy listeners panel:
  :149  setText("Regenerate CA certificate")
  :198  confirm text: "Are you sure you want to regenerate Burp's CA
        certificate?\nTo take effect, you will need to restart Burp, and then
        install the new certificate in your browser."
  :141  the sibling "Import / export CA certificate" button
  :132  the panel's explanation of why both exist

## burpsy-side evidence

Import EXISTS:
  internal/web/api_ca.go:89        handleCAImport
  internal/web/server.go:722       /api/proxy/ca/import
  lib/data.policy.ts:110-113       useImportCaCert
  pages/settings.tsx:1533-1619     CaImportSection ("Use your own CA")
Export EXISTS:
  /ca.crt, with pages/settings.tsx:1621-1663 CertificateSection and the sidebar
  download at app.tsx:453-457.

Regenerate does NOT:
`grep -rniE "regenerat" --include=*.go --include=*.tsx internal/` returns 6 hits,
none of them a CA action -- internal/crawler/destructive.go:128 (a word list),
internal/intruder/engine.go:17,217 and payload.go:148 (payload replay),
internal/scanner/catalog.go:9 (codegen), and internal/proxy/proxy.go:288, which
is a doc comment reading "A regenerated CA would invalidate any trust-store..."
with no caller. Per the count rule: that is one comment and zero implementations.

Positive control, same grep style and same directories: the import path above is
found by `grep -rn "ImportCaCert\|ca/import"` across the same trees.

## Classification

CAPABILITY GAP.

## What an operator cannot do

Rotate the CA. A CA whose private key may have been exposed, or one that was
installed into a client's trust store during an engagement that has now ended,
cannot be replaced from the console. The nearest workaround is to generate a CA
pair out-of-band with openssl and import it -- which works (CaImportSection
validates the pair and discards previously issued per-host certificates,
settings.tsx:1611-1615) but requires leaving the tool.

## Note

The import path already does everything the hard part of this needs -- validate,
swap, invalidate the per-host cache, keep /ca.crt serving whichever CA is in
force (server.go:125). Regenerate is that same swap with a self-generated pair
instead of a pasted one, so it is small. It must reuse the import path's
invalidation rather than adding a second one.
acceptance_criteria: A new CA can be generated from the console; it reuses the import path's validation and per-host certificate invalidation; /ca.crt then serves the new CA and the UI states that clients must re-trust it.

title: wshistory: the empty state says to 'clear the selection to see every frame' but no control clears the connection selection
description:
VERIFIED against HEAD by AuditProxy (Proxy-screen parity audit, 2026-08-27).

The WebSocket frame table's empty state tells the operator to clear the
connection selection. There is no control that clears it. Once a connection is
selected, the all-frames view is unreachable without reloading the page.

## burpsy-side evidence

The instruction, in the frame table's empty state:
  pages/wshistory.tsx:253-258
    title={selectedExchange === null ? "No WebSocket traffic captured yet"
                                    : "No frames on this connection"}
    detail={... : "Select another connection, or clear the selection to see
                   every frame."}

The selection setter has no clear path -- it only ever assigns:
  pages/wshistory.tsx:209-212
    onSelect={() => {
      setSelectedExchange(conn.exchange);
      setSelectedFrameId(null);
    }}

ConnectionRow (wshistory.tsx:31-57) renders a plain <button> whose onClick is
that setter; there is no toggle-off branch, no "All connections" row in the list
(the list is a bare `conns.map`, wholly at wshistory.tsx:203-216), and no clear
button anywhere in the connections column. The only Clear controls on the page
are for the FRAME selection, not the connection: wshistory.tsx:279 ("Clear frame
selection") and the frame-level X.

`selectedExchange` is initialised to null (wshistory.tsx:109) and after any click
can never return to null for the rest of the page's life.

## Classification

UX DIVERGENCE with a dead affordance -- the screen names an action the operator
cannot perform. Not a Burp-parity gap: this one is burpsy's own copy promising
its own missing control.

## What an operator cannot do

Get back to the cross-connection frame view after clicking any connection, and
they are explicitly told to do it. On a capture with several sockets this is the
view that answers "what happened across all of them, in order".

## Note

Two honest fixes, and the choice is a small design decision:
either add an "All connections" entry at the top of the connections list (makes
the all-frames view a first-class, re-selectable state), or make ConnectionRow
toggle -- clicking the selected connection deselects it. The first is clearer,
because the current all-frames state is otherwise invisible and undiscoverable.
Whichever is chosen, the empty-state copy at :257 must match it.
acceptance_criteria: The cross-connection all-frames view is reachable after a connection has been selected, via a control that exists on screen; the frame table's empty-state copy names that actual control.
close_reason: Fixed in e8a8396: two affordances keep the empty-state promise — (a) clicking the already-selected connection deselects it (ConnectionRow toggle with aria-pressed), (b) a 'Clear connection selection' X button in the detail head whenever a connection is selected but no frame is. Proven interactively: relayed two real WebSocket upgrades through the proxy to a local origin, selected a connection (frames filtered), clicked clear (all 4 frames visible again), clicked the same connection twice (deselects). bun run check 163/0.

title: ui: 'Change body encoding' only toggles chunked framing — no form-urlencoded / multipart / JSON conversion
description:
## Claim
The row menu's "Change body encoding" only toggles chunked transfer framing. Burp's item of that name converts a request body between form URL-encoding, multipart encoding and JSON — a different operation under the same label.

## Burp-side evidence
- `tools/context-menu.html` (bundled docs): **Change body encoding** — *"Change the encoding of any request body between **form URL-encoding, multipart encoding, and JSON**. You can also select Toggle body encoding to switch between the two most recently used encodings in the current Repeater tab."*

## burpsy-side evidence
- Menu entry: `lib/actions.ts:799` — `{ id: "body-encoding", label: "Change body encoding (chunked)", onSelect: () => void changeBodyEncoding(exchange) }`.
- Implementation is chunked framing only: `lib/actions.ts:729-749` `changeBodyEncoding` calls `isChunked(raw) ? dechunkBody(raw) : chunkBody(raw)`; `chunkBody` (`:539-549`) swaps `Content-Length` for `Transfer-Encoding: chunked`, `dechunkBody` (`:520-536`) reverses it.
- No form/multipart/JSON conversion exists: `grep -rn 'multipart' --include=*.ts lib/` -> no conversion helper (positive control: `grep -rn 'x-www-form-urlencoded' lib/message.ts` -> `:260`, which is a parameter-form *detector* used by the Inspector, not a body converter).

## Classification
CAPABILITY GAP for the conversion; the label is separately misleading since it already carries the Burp name for a different operation. The parenthetical `(chunked)` mitigates but does not remove the collision.

## What an operator cannot do
Re-encode a JSON body as form-urlencoded (or as multipart) to test whether the server accepts both — a routine content-type confusion / parser-differential probe. Chunked framing is a useful capability and should stay, under its own name.
acceptance_criteria: The row menu converts a request body between form URL-encoding, multipart and JSON (adjusting Content-Type and Content-Length), and the existing chunked-framing toggle is offered under its own distinct label.

title: ui: no 'paste URL as request' — a new Repeater tab always starts from a fixed example.com template
description:
## Claim
There is no way to turn a host or URL into a request. Burp's "Paste host / URL as request" builds a request from a copied URL; in burpsy a new Repeater tab always starts from a fixed example.com template that must be hand-edited.

## Burp-side evidence
- `tools/context-menu.html` (bundled docs), universal menu options: **Paste host / URL as request** — *"Creates an HTTP request from a copied host or URL. For example, ginandjuice.shop or https://ginandjuice.shop"*.

## burpsy-side evidence
- Absence grep over the whole UI tree: `grep -rli 'Paste host' --include=*.tsx --include=*.ts burpsy-go/internal/web/ui/src/` -> **no files**; `grep -rli 'as request'` -> **no files**. Same-tree positive control: `grep -rli 'Copy URL' --include=*.tsx --include=*.ts .` -> `pages/logger.tsx lib/actions.ts`.
- The only new-tab path is a fixed template: `app.tsx:472-485` Repeater -> "New request tab" calls `openRepeaterTab({ name: ..., target: "https://example.com:443", protocol: "https", request: templateRequest("example.com") })`.
- `lib/actions.ts:561-577`'s action surface has no URL-to-request entry.

## Classification
CAPABILITY GAP.

## What an operator cannot do
Paste a URL from a ticket, a report or a browser bar and get a working request. They open a template pointed at example.com and hand-edit the target field, the request line and the Host header — four edits for what is one paste in Burp.
acceptance_criteria: Pasting or entering a host or URL creates a Repeater tab whose target, request line and Host header are derived from it, reachable from the Repeater menu and the new-tab affordance.

title: settings: no font-size or UI-scaling control — editor text is hardcoded at 12px
description:
## Claim
There is no font-size or UI-scaling control. Burp offers separate font adjustment for the UI and for the message editor; burpsy's only appearance controls are Theme and Table density, and the editor font size is a hardcoded 12px.

## Burp-side evidence
- `tools/message-editor/text-editor.html` (bundled docs), Syntax analysis: *"You can configure this behavior, and **adjust the font**, in the message display settings."*
- Spec section 2.2 defines two independent scales: a System UI hierarchy (16/13/12/11pt) and a separate `Code / Monospace` scale (12pt, JetBrains Mono / Consolas / Menlo) for *"HTTP Request/Response headers & bodies"* — two knobs, deliberately separate.

## burpsy-side evidence
- Appearance section offers Theme and Table density only: `pages/settings.tsx:1301-1335` (`THEMES` at `:40`, `DENSITIES` at `:46`). `grep -in 'font|scal|zoom' pages/settings.tsx` -> one hit, `:1421`, an inline `fontSize: "var(--fs-sm)"` style on unrelated helper text.
- UI sizes are viewport-fluid clamps with no user input: `tokens/primitives.css:46-48` e.g. `--fs-sm: clamp(12px, 0.68vw, 14px)`.
- Editor font size is hardcoded: `ui/editor.tsx:86` `"&": { ..., fontSize: "12px" }` and `:93-94` gutters at `11px`.

## Classification
CAPABILITY GAP.

## What an operator cannot do
Enlarge the HTTP message text without enlarging the tables. Browser zoom is the only lever and it scales everything together — which is precisely why Burp ships the two knobs separately. On a 4K display this is a per-session irritation.
acceptance_criteria: Settings -> Appearance offers a UI text-size control and a separate message-editor font-size control, both persisted, with the editor size driving ui/editor.tsx's theme instead of a literal.

title: settings: no search across settings and no category tree — 20 sections and ~87 fields in one flat scroll
description:
## Claim
Settings is one flat 20-section scrolling page with no search and no category tree. Burp's Settings is a searchable tree, and the search box is how a Burp user finds any setting they do not already know the location of.

## Burp-side evidence
- `settings/ui/hotkeys.html` (bundled docs) navigates by path — *"Go to **Settings > User interface > Hotkeys**"* — and the whole docs tree under `desktop/settings/` mirrors Burp's category hierarchy (`settings/ui/`, `settings/network/`, `settings/tools/`, ...), i.e. a two-level tree is the addressing scheme.
- Same page also records the project/user split, which burpsy has no analogue for: *"The Hotkeys settings are **user settings**. They apply to all installations of Burp on your machine."*
- Spec section 4.12 and the tool sections consistently reference a Settings *dialog* reached from each tool's own gear.

## burpsy-side evidence
- `pages/settings.tsx:1967-1994` `SettingsPage` renders 20 sections in sequence with nothing but a `PageHeader` above them; the file is 2,627 lines with 87 `Field`s (`grep -c Field pages/settings.tsx` -> 87).
- The only search in the whole file is hotkeys-local: `grep -in search pages/settings.tsx` -> 2 hits, `:1271` *"Search hotkeys"* and `:1284` *"No matching hotkey"*. Nothing searches across sections.
- No anchor nav, no tree, no section index component is rendered by `SettingsPage`.
- No project/user distinction: config export/import is a single undifferentiated bundle (`app.tsx:279-323`, `internal/web/api_config.go`).

## Classification
UX DIVERGENCE.

## What an operator cannot do
Type "redirect" or "response modification" and land on the setting. They scroll 20 sections instead, past ~87 fields.

## Decision needed
Scope call before code: (a) add a filter box that hides non-matching sections/fields (cheap, gets 80% of the value); (b) add a left category tree plus deep-linkable section routes; (c) also introduce a project-vs-user settings distinction, which is a data-model decision about what travels with a capture and touches `api_config.go`. (a) and (b) are independent of (c).
acceptance_criteria: Settings offers a search that filters to matching sections and fields across the whole page, and sections are reachable by name (tree or deep-linkable anchors) rather than only by scrolling.

title: scan launch: no pre-scan filter step to drop duplicates, static assets or unparameterized items
description:
## Claim

There is no pre-scan filter step. A scan launched from the site map goes straight to the engine, so
static assets and duplicate items consume the request budget.

## burpsy side

`lib/actions.ts:404-405` — "Actively scan this branch (crawl)" / "this host (crawl)" call
`crawlFrom(exchange, "branch"|"host")` directly; there is no intermediate dialog.
`pages/dashboard.tsx:222-236` — `submit()` calls `startCrawl.mutate` and `close()` immediately.

Absence grep: `grep -rniE "remove duplicate|no parameters|remove items with" internal/web/ui/src` -> no
match. Positive control on the same tree: `grep -rn "Actively scan this branch" internal/web/ui/src` ->
`lib/actions.ts:404`.

Note what *does* exist and is not this: the crawl form's bounds — max requests, max depth, rps
(`ui/crawl.tsx:72-83`) — cap the total cost but cannot express "spend it on the parameterized pages,
not the sprite sheets".

## Burp side

`map_root.tsv` class `burp.Zraa` is the wizard step, with the prompt *"You have selected N items to
scan. Before continuing, you can use the filters below to remove certain categories of items, to make
your scanning more targeted and efficient."* and four filters:

- `Remove duplicate items (same URL and parameters)`
- `Remove items with no parameters`
- `Remove out-of-scope items (based on current suite scope)`
- `Remove items with the following extensions` — shipped default
  `js,gif,jpg,png,ico,css,woff,woff2,ttf,svg`

Each renders a live count (the `[calculating...]` variants are in the same class).

## Classification

CAPABILITY GAP.

## What an operator cannot do

Aim a bounded scan. With a 200-request budget on a site whose map is 60% static assets, most of the
budget goes to files that cannot carry a finding — and nothing on screen says so.

## Note

The extension filter is the one worth building first; it is a client-side predicate over the same tree
the site map already holds, and Burp's default list is a reasonable starting value to copy.
acceptance_criteria: Launching a scan from a site-map selection offers filters to exclude items by extension, items with no parameters, and duplicates, each showing how many items it removes.

title: site map: no way to copy the URLs under a host or branch
description:
## Claim

There is no way to copy the URLs under a site-map host or branch.

## burpsy side

Absence grep: `grep -rniE "copy urls|copy links" internal/web/ui/src` -> no match.

Positive control on the same file, showing the copy family that *does* exist:
`grep -n "label:" internal/web/ui/src/lib/actions.ts` -> `:385` `Copy URL`, `:386` `Copy as curl`,
`:387` `Copy exchange id`, `:388` `Copy request to file`. All four are single-exchange; none is
subtree-scoped, and `actions.menu()` is only mounted on the contents table
(`pages/sitemap.tsx:548`), never on a tree node.

## Burp side

`map_root.tsv` class `burp.Zxut` — `Copy URLs in this host`, `Copy URLs in this branch`,
`Copy selected URLs`, `Copy links in this host`, `Copy links in this branch`,
`Copy links in selected items`. ("URLs" is what was requested; "links" is what was found in the
responses — two separate menu items in Burp.)

## Classification

CAPABILITY GAP (polish).

## What an operator cannot do

Get the URL list for a host out of burpsy and into anything else — ffuf, a spreadsheet, a colleague's
message — without clicking each row and copying one at a time.

## Depends on

burpsy-react-ui-dpk (tree rows have no context menu) is where this action would live.
acceptance_criteria: A site-map host or branch offers copy-URLs-in-this-branch, putting one URL per line on the clipboard.
close_reason: Implemented in 1e6883d, verified live in browser (proof in the commit message).

title: scope: no Paste URL and no load-from-file for bulk scope entry
description:
## Claim

Scope rules can only be entered one at a time through the form. There is no paste-a-URL shortcut and no
load-from-file, so scoping a 40-host engagement is 40 manual entries.

## burpsy side

`pages/scope.tsx:163-194` — one `Toolbar` of five `Field`s (kind, host pattern, port, path prefix,
protocol) and an "Add rule" button. `addRule()` (`:43-68`) reads those five pieces of state and clears
them; it parses nothing URL-shaped.

Absence grep on the file: `grep -riE "edit|paste|load from|import" pages/scope.tsx` returns only the
`import` statements at `:1-7`. Positive control on the same file: `grep -n "Add rule" pages/scope.tsx`
-> `:192`.

## Burp side

`map_root.tsv` class `burp.Zry2` (`configPanelTargetScope`) — `Add a new item by pasting a URL`,
`Paste URL`, and `Load ...`. The same pair appears on the other scope-entry surfaces: `burp.Zh5w`,
`burp.Zrda`, `burp.Zhw_` all carry `Paste URL` + `Load ...`.

## Classification

CAPABILITY GAP (polish).

## What an operator cannot do

Turn a scope list they were handed — a text file of URLs, or a URL on the clipboard — into scope rules
without decomposing each one into host / port / path / protocol by hand.

## Note

Paste URL is the higher-value half and is nearly free: it is a URL parse feeding the five fields the
form already has. Load-from-file needs a decision on format (one URL per line? the JSON the API
speaks?) and can wait.
acceptance_criteria: A URL can be pasted and decomposed into a scope rule's arms; bulk entry from a file or multi-line paste is available or explicitly declined with a reason.

title: ui: no hide-headers toggle in the message editor (and Settings' 'Uninteresting headers' is a different feature that hides nothing)
description:
## Claim
There is no way to hide uninteresting HTTP headers while reading a message. Burp has an eye button above each message driven by editable Hide request headers / Hide response headers lists. burpsy's similarly-named "Uninteresting headers" setting is a Comparer diffing weight and hides nothing — its own copy says so.

## Burp-side evidence
- `tools/message-editor/text-editor.html` (bundled docs), Hide headers: *"In the Pretty tab, you have the option to hide HTTP headers that typically don't offer much insight into the target application's behavior... Toggle whether these HTTP headers are visible using the eye button above each message. Burp hides the headers specified in the Hide request headers or Hide response headers list. You can edit these lists in the Settings dialog, under **User interface > Message editor**."*

## burpsy-side evidence
- No such control in the editor: the full toolbar is `ui/editor.tsx:323-344` (Wrap, Copy, Save). `grep -rn 'EyeOff\|<Eye' --include=*.tsx src/` -> no hits in `ui/editor.tsx`; the only "eye" string in the tree is an unrelated comment at `ui/inspector.tsx:144`. Positive control on editor.tsx: `grep -c import ui/editor.tsx` -> 14.
- The name collision is the trap: `pages/settings.tsx:1467-1530` "Uninteresting headers" is explicitly not this feature. Its section detail reads *"Differences in these headers are dimmed in: ..."* (`:1470-1472`) and its footnote states *"**Nothing is hidden.** A difference inside one of these headers is still reported and still rendered — dimmed, and counted separately"* (`:1524-1530`). It feeds Comparer, not the editor.

## Classification
CAPABILITY GAP. Flagging the naming separately: a migrating user reading the Settings tree will conclude the feature is present.

## What an operator cannot do
Reduce a 30-header response to the five that matter while reading it. Also worth a rename or a cross-reference note so "Uninteresting headers" is not mistaken for Burp's hide-headers lists.
acceptance_criteria: A toggle above each message hides the headers named in an editable request/response hide-list, and the existing Comparer 'Uninteresting headers' section is named or cross-referenced so the two are not confused.

title: ui: no request/response layout switcher — split orientation is hardcoded per page and there is no combined view
description:
## Claim
There is no way to switch how a request and response are arranged. Burp offers three layouts (side-by-side, stacked, and a combined single-pane view with tabs) from icons in the editor's top-right corner; in burpsy the orientation is fixed per page in source.

## Burp-side evidence
- `tools/message-editor/index.html` (bundled docs): *"In the upper-right corner of the message editor, there are three icons that adjust the screen layout. You can choose from the following options: **Horizontal layout** - The request and response are arranged side-by-side. **Vertical layout** - The request and response are stacked one on top of the other. **Combined view** - Either the request or response fills the message editor pane. You can use the tabs to alternate between the two."*

## burpsy-side evidence
- Orientation is a hardcoded prop per page: `pages/history.tsx:1001` `orientation="vertical"`, `pages/intercept.tsx:717` `"vertical"`, `pages/sitemap.tsx:526` `"vertical"`, `pages/logger.tsx:341` `"vertical"`, `pages/sitemap.tsx:646` `"horizontal"`, `pages/scanner.tsx:674` `"horizontal"`, `pages/advisories.tsx:258` `"horizontal"`.
- `ui/layout.tsx:77-120` `SplitPane` accepts `orientation` as a prop and persists only the divider position (`useDefaultLayout` keyed `burpsy.split.${storageId}`, `:96-100`). There is no control anywhere that changes `orientation` at runtime, and no combined/tabbed mode exists in the component at all.

## Classification
UX DIVERGENCE.

## What an operator cannot do
Give a long response the full pane and switch back to the request with a tab — the standard laptop workflow in Burp. The only lever here is dragging the splitter to the edge and dragging it back.
acceptance_criteria: Each request/response pane offers horizontal, vertical and combined (single pane with request/response tabs) layouts from a control in the editor area, persisted per surface.

title: scope: a rule cannot be disabled without deleting it
description:
## Claim

A scope rule cannot be disabled. The only way to stop a rule applying is to delete it.

## burpsy side

`internal/core/scope.go` — `ScopeRule` has `Kind`, `Regex`, `Port`, `PathPrefix`, `Protocol` (per the
constructors at `:67-80` and the matcher at `:83-105`) and no enabled/disabled field.
`MatchesRequest` (`:91`) consults no such flag.

`pages/scope.tsx:98-130` — the table's five columns are `Kind`, `Host`, `Port`, `Protocol`,
`Path prefix`. No checkbox column, and `ScopeRow` (`:10-16`) carries no enabled field.

Positive control that `enabled` exists elsewhere on the wire (so this is a scope-specific gap, not a
missing convention): `grep -n "enabled" internal/web/ui/src/lib/types.policy.ts` -> `:57`, `:119`,
`:230`, all on match/replace and session rules.

## Burp side

Burp's scope tables have a per-row Enabled checkbox — `map_root.tsv` `burp.Zb4l` and `burp.Zbwj` carry
the `Enabled` column label, alongside `configPanelTargetScope`'s Add / Edit / Remove controls
(`burp.Zry2`).

## Classification

CAPABILITY GAP (polish).

## What an operator cannot do

Temporarily widen scope — lift an exclusion for one test and put it back — without retyping the rule.
Combined with the absence of rule editing (burpsy-react-ui-k5l), every scope change is destructive.
acceptance_criteria: A scope rule can be toggled inactive and back, the state persists, and an inactive rule is ignored by ScopeRule matching.

title: site map: contents table has no Comment column or highlight, though history does
description:
## Claim

The site map's contents table has no Comment column and no highlight, though HTTP history has both over
the same exchanges.

## burpsy side

`pages/sitemap.tsx:307-367` — the columns are `#`, `Method`, `URL`, `Params`, `Status`, `Length`,
`MIME`, `Time`, `Age`. Nine columns, no annotation.

`pages/history.tsx:657-763` — the same table plus `TLS` (`:735`), **`Comment`** (`:741`), `Ext`
(`:716`) and `Query` (`:725`), and a highlight swatch picker at `:247-266`.

The data is on the exchange, not on the history page: `internal/core/store.go:384-389` documents
`Exchange.Highlight` — *"the operator's colour tag for this row"* — with the shared vocabulary at
`:809` (`ValidHighlights`).

Absence grep on the file: `grep -c "highlight\|comment" pages/sitemap.tsx` -> `0`. Positive control on
the same file: `grep -c "accessorKey" pages/sitemap.tsx` -> non-zero (the column defs at `:309-364`).

## Burp side

Burp's site map contents table carries the annotation columns, and its filter bar has a group that
depends on them: `map_root.tsv` class `burp.Zh5v` — `Filter by annotation`,
`Show only highlighted items`, `Show only items with notes`, keys
`target.filter.by_annotation.show_only_highlighted_items` and `.show_only_commented_items`.

## Classification

UX DIVERGENCE — the fields exist and are editable in HTTP history; the site map just does not render
them.

## What an operator cannot do

See, in the site map, that they already flagged a request as interesting — so a colour set while
triaging history is invisible the moment they move to the map. Related: burpsy-react-ui-36d covers the
filter that would consume these columns.
acceptance_criteria: The site-map contents table shows each exchange's highlight and comment, using the same vocabulary and editing affordance as HTTP history.
close_reason: Implemented in 1e6883d, verified live in browser (proof in the commit message).

title: issues: report export cannot be filtered — always the whole finding store
description:
## Claim

Report export is always the entire finding store. There is no way to export a subset — by severity, by
host, or by selection.

## burpsy side

`internal/web/api_report.go:18-35` — `handleReport` reads nothing off the request but the path suffix:

    format := strings.TrimPrefix(r.URL.Path, "/api/report/")

then dispatches to `reportJSON` / `reportSARIF` / `reportHTML`. No `r.URL.Query()` call anywhere in the
file. `reportRows()` (`:40-67`) begins `findings := s.findings.All()` and iterates all of them.

`pages/scanner.tsx:641-646` renders three unconditional download links built from `REPORT_FORMATS`
(`:47-51`) — `/api/report/html`, `/api/report/json`, `/api/report/sarif`. They ignore the page's own
severity and confidence filters, which are applied only to `rows` for display (`:292-303`).

Positive control on the same file: `grep -n "api/report" internal/web/api_report.go` -> `:12`, `:23`.

## Burp side

`map_root.tsv` class `burp.Zeem` — `Report issues`; class `burp.Zuv8` — `Report `, `selected issues`,
`the "%s" issues`. Burp reports from a selection.

## Classification

CAPABILITY GAP (polish).

## What an operator cannot do

Hand over "the High and Critical findings on this host" — the export is everything or nothing, so the
filtering has to happen in whatever tool receives the file.

## Note

Worth noting the mismatch is visible on screen: the operator filters the Issues tree to 3 findings,
clicks HTML, and gets 200. Making the export honour the active filters would be the least surprising
behaviour and needs no new controls.
acceptance_criteria: Report export honours a severity/host filter or the active Issues-tree filter, and the UI states which findings the file will contain.

title: dashboard: event feed has no clear action and is capped at 12 rows
description:
## Claim

The Dashboard's event feed has no clear action and is hard-capped at 12 rows with no way to see more.

## burpsy side

`pages/dashboard.tsx:436-454` — the "Tool events" card renders
`data.events.slice(0, 12)` (`:440`). The 12 is a literal; there is no paging, no "show all", and no
link to a fuller view.

Absence grep: `grep -rniE "clear.*event log|events/clear" internal/web/*.go internal/dash/*.go
internal/web/ui/src/` -> no match. Positive control on the same tree:
`grep -rn "Tool events" internal/web/ui/src/` -> `pages/dashboard.tsx:437`.

## Burp side

`map_root.tsv` class `burp.Zbuz` — `Clear event log`, and `burp.Zr_h` — `No event log items to show`,
`dashboardEventLogEmptyState`, plus the empty-state copy *"The event log shows key task events, such as
start times, alerts, and progress updates."* Burp's is a scrollable table with a clear action, not a
fixed-height digest.

## Classification

CAPABILITY GAP (polish).

## What an operator cannot do

Read the 13th event, or reset the feed after resolving a burst of errors so that the next one is
visible.
acceptance_criteria: The Dashboard event feed is scrollable or paged past 12 entries and offers a clear action.

title: advisories: 183 of Burp's 366 issue definitions — decide whether the catalogue tracks checks or Burp
description:
burpsy bundles **183** issue definitions (`internal/advisory/definitions/*.json`). Burp ships **366**
(`resources/KnowledgeBase/Issues/`). That is **50%**.

Re-derived: 366 confirmed from `/root/burp-re/in/extract/resources/KnowledgeBase/Issues`. Note W0
described these as top-level `KnowledgeBase` files; they are in an `Issues/` subdirectory, which is
why a naive `ls KnowledgeBase | wc -l` returns 1. The 366 figure itself is right.

## What the gap actually costs

An advisory is what turns a finding into something reportable: description, remediation, CWE/CAPEC
classifications, references. burpsy's catalogue is honest about misses — a finding that resolves to no
catalogue entry carries `advisory_note` explaining why rather than an empty advisory — so this
degrades reporting quality rather than producing wrong output.

The 183 present are not a random half: they cover the check families burpsy actually implements (22
check descriptors). So the practical shortfall is smaller than 50% suggests — most of the missing 183
describe issues burpsy has no check for, and an advisory with no check to raise it is inert.

## The real question this issue exists to force

**Is the catalogue meant to be complete, or to match the checks?** Those are different products:

- Match the checks: the gap is near zero today, and every new check must arrive with its advisory.
  A test could enforce that — every check descriptor resolves to a catalogue entry — which is the
  version I would build.
- Complete: 183 definitions to transcribe, most describing checks that do not exist, and the same
  licensing question as the payload wordlists (this is PortSwigger's prose).

Answer that before transcribing anything.

## Concrete sub-task worth doing either way

Assert that every one of the 22 check descriptors resolves to a bundled advisory, and that every
bundled advisory is either reachable from a check or explicitly marked as catalogue-only (the
`ExtensionGeneratedIssue` / `ManuallyGeneratedIssue` / `BCheckGeneratedIssue` / `BambdaGeneratedIssue`
entries exist for exactly that reason). That closes the honest half of this gap and is testable.
acceptance_criteria: The catalogue's intended scope is recorded; a test asserts every check descriptor resolves to a bundled advisory and every bundled advisory is reachable or marked catalogue-only.
close_reason: INVALID — I filed this, and the arithmetic was mine and wrong. Burp does not ship 366 issue definitions; it ships 183, as 366 FILES (one .html and one .json per issue). Proof: stripping the extension from resources/KnowledgeBase/Issues and de-duplicating gives 183. burpsy bundles 183 definitions with 183 distinct type_index prefixes, and comm against Burp's prefix set shows NO difference — the index sets are identical. So the catalogue is at full parity, not 50%. Two things went wrong and both are worth recording: W0-burp-denominators.md counted files where the unit is issues, and I propagated it into an issue and into a verbal assessment without checking whether the unit matched. The tell was available and I walked past it — the company's own Security Research role definition states the target as 'Burp's 183-issue catalog', which contradicted my 366 denominator, and I only noticed when importing that role file. The sub-task in the body is still worth doing on its own merits and should be re-filed if anyone wants it: assert that every one of the 22 check descriptors resolves to a bundled advisory, and that every bundled advisory is either reachable from a check or explicitly marked catalogue-only (the ExtensionGenerated/ManuallyGenerated/BCheckGenerated/BambdaGenerated entries exist for that). That is a real guard against drift; it is not a parity gap.

title: ui: HTTP history has no auto-scroll-to-new toggle
description: Audit gap #41 (PlumOtter parity audit 2026-08-27). history.tsx auto-loads rows but offers no 'auto-scroll to newest' toggle (Burp's history auto-pins to the bottom as traffic arrives). Verified absent: grep auto-scroll|autoScroll in history.tsx returns no matches. NOTE: highlighted/commented filters (#39/#40) are present (history.tsx:1132-1133) — those audit entries were false and intentionally not added.
close_reason: Implemented in 954b0b9. Auto-scroll FilterToggle in the history toolbar (off by default), wired to a new opt-in followNewRows prop on VirtualTable that pins to the last row on row growth only. Verified live in browser: ON pinned the viewport to bottom across 30 seeded rows (scrollTop at max), OFF held scrollTop 0 across 10 more rows.

title: ui: Dashboard telemetry (task throughput / bytes / requests) absent
description: Audit gap #34 (PlumOtter parity audit 2026-08-27). dashboard.tsx has a live task-progress bar and task table but no telemetry view (requests/sec, bytes transferred, task throughput over time) that Burp's dashboard shows. Verified absent: grep telemetry|listener in dashboard.tsx returns no matches.

title: ui: Repeater status label, follow-redirects, explore, streaming, validation warnings, search, WS-tab absent
description: Audit Repeater gaps #56-#62 (PlumOtter parity audit 2026-08-27). repeater.tsx lacks: a per-tab status label, a follow-redirects toggle, an AI 'explore' action, streaming-response config, validation warnings, a search-within-responses control, and a WebSocket-tab option. Verified absent: grep status label|follow redirect|explore|streaming|validation warning|search|ws tab|websocket tab in repeater.tsx returns no matches. NOTE: Cancel button (#25) was filed as burpsy-react-ui-0c2 and closed (9db42d8).
close_reason: INVALID as filed: it bundles seven unrelated claims and at least one is demonstrably false, which makes it unclosable in either direction. 'Follow-redirects absent' — repeater.tsx line 609 is a 'Follow redirections' Field, RepeaterRedirects is a wire type, and line 536 renders a RedirectChain of the hops taken. The comment at line 594 even explains which redirect-related checkboxes are deliberately NOT offered and why (a raw-byte send cannot honour them, and hops do not replay cookies), so the page has both the feature and a recorded decision about its edges. A single issue asserting seven absences cannot be verified, scheduled or closed honestly: whoever closes it either overstates (marking six unverified claims done) or leaves it open forever on the strength of the weakest one. Re-file the remaining six — status label, explore, streaming, validation warnings, search, WS tab — as separate issues, each with the thing an operator cannot currently do.

title: ui: Extender Ruby/Python/Java language config absent
description: Audit Extender gap #55 (PlumOtter parity audit 2026-08-27). extensions.tsx has no per-extension language/engine selector (Ruby/Python/Java/own config). Verified absent: grep Ruby|Python|Java config in extensions.tsx returns no matches.
close_reason: INVALID — a language selector is a control with nothing to control, for the same reason edv's store controls were. Burp has Ruby/Python/Java config because it EMBEDS Jython and JRuby interpreters and must be told where they are. burpsy embeds nothing: internal/extension/session.go states the contract directly — a plugin is a local executable speaking newline-delimited JSON-RPC on stdin/stdout, and 'one that needs an interpreter should be an executable script with a shebang'. So the language is the operating system's business, already expressed in the file the operator names on the command line. There is no language concept anywhere in internal/extension to configure: grep for jython/jruby/interpreter/Language across the package returns only that one comment saying it is deliberately not our concern. Adding a selector would mean burpsy resolving interpreters, which is a strictly larger and unasked-for change (and one the no-store decision already argues against). Re-open only against a decision to embed interpreters.

title: ui: Extender bapp-store update and suppress-popup absent
description: Audit Extender gaps #53/#54 (PlumOtter parity audit 2026-08-27). extensions.tsx has no 'check for BApp updates' action and no 'suppress future popups' preference. Verified absent: grep bapp|update|suppress popup|suppressPopup in extensions.tsx returns no matches.
close_reason: INVALID — 'bapp-store update and suppress-popup absent' asks for controls over a store that deliberately does not exist. extensions.tsx states this at three points, including a whole section headed 'There is no store': 'Burp's store is a hosted catalogue; nothing in burpsy fetches, resolves or installs anything', and a plugin is a local executable the operator names on the command line. The API reports the absence explicitly rather than leaving it inferred from a missing field, so a caller can tell 'no store' from 'a store this build did not ask about'. An update button and a suppress-update-popup toggle for a catalogue with no fetch path are not a gap; they are controls with nothing to control. Re-open only against a decision to add a store, which is a strategic question and not a UI one.

title: ui: Extender JMenu items and hot-key handlers absent
description: Audit Extender gaps #51/#52 (PlumOtter parity audit 2026-08-27). extensions.tsx has load/unload/enable/invoke/console but no per-extension JMenu contribution and no registered hot-key handlers. Verified absent: grep JMenu|hotkey|hot key in extensions.tsx returns no matches. NOTE: Add/Edit/Remove (#362-364) were filed as burpsy-react-ui-2l5 and closed FALSE (the empty state is the absence, by design).
close_reason: INVALID — 'JMenu items and hot-key handlers' describes Burp's Swing implementation, not a capability. javax.swing.JMenu has no counterpart in a React console and its absence is not a gap; this is Burp internals leaking through a decompiled-source audit into a burpsy issue. The capability behind it — operator-rebindable keyboard shortcuts — already exists and is more complete than Burp's: lib/keymap.ts and lib/shortcuts.ts hold a registry, Settings has an editable binding table with duplicate detection, and three renderers read one keymap (shipped in a9e45d9, U21). useHotkeys is wired on history, repeater and intercept among others. If a specific binding is missing, file that binding.

title: ui: Comparer has no word-level diff mode
description: Audit gap #50 (PlumOtter parity audit 2026-08-27). comparer.tsx is byte-level aligned only (lines 268-277: 'There is no word-level mode, and none is offered rather than a control that silently did the same thing'). Burp's Comparer offers word-level. Verified: handler reads two flat strings, no granularity param.

title: ui: Proxy settings miscellaneous and web-interface sections absent
description: Audit gap #46/#47 (PlumOtter parity audit 2026-08-27). proxysettings.tsx covers bind/intercept/certificate/redirect/timeout but not Burp's 'Miscellaneous' settings (e.g. strip comments, remove unsupported encodings) or 'Web interface' (accessible via browser) section. Verified absent: grep miscellaneous|web interface|webInterface in proxysettings.tsx returns no matches. NOTE: TLS passthrough (#10) and resource pools (#11) were already filed as burpsy-react-ui-wyp and closed FALSE (they exist).

comments.author: AuditProxy
comments.text:
AuditProxy, Proxy-screen parity audit 2026-08-27 — the gap is real but this body misdescribes the page, which will mislead whoever picks it up.

The body says: "proxysettings.tsx covers bind/intercept/certificate/redirect/timeout but not Burp's 'Miscellaneous' settings".

It covers none of those five. pages/proxysettings.tsx is 140 lines end to end (I read all of it): six response-modification switches (:20-51 SWITCHES, rendered :76-99), an outcome-counters card (:102-119), and a transport-adjustments table (:121-137). There is no bind control, no certificate control, no redirect control and no timeout control on that page — those are the subject of burpsy-react-ui-77m (listener config), which I filed separately at P1 because the whole Proxy listeners panel is absent, not merely its Miscellaneous neighbour.

The Miscellaneous half of this issue stands. For whoever builds it, Burp's actual panel is configPanelProxyMiscellaneous, BurpClass9621.java, keyword set at :45-69 — the members are: use HTTP/1.0 in requests to server, use HTTP/1.1 in requests to server, set "Connection: close" on requests and on responses, strip Proxy-* headers in incoming requests, remove unsupported Accept-Encoding headers, strip Sec-WebSocket-Extensions headers, unpack gzip/deflate in requests and in responses, disable web interface at http://burp, suppress Burp error messages in browser, don't send items to Proxy history or live tasks if out of scope, don't send items to live tasks. Control names configPanelProxyMiscellaneousHttp1KeepAlive and configPanelProxyMiscellaneousDontLogOutOfScopeItems are in /root/burp-re/out/ui_report/setname_inventory.tsv.

Three of those members are NOT closable by building a switch panel and are filed separately with their own evidence:
- burpsy-react-ui-6rb (P1) — Sec-WebSocket-Extensions stripping: the behaviour exists but is builder-only (WithStripWsExtensions), and three shipped UI strings already tell the operator to toggle a control that exists nowhere.
- burpsy-react-ui-pi8 (P2) — unpack gzip/deflate: needs a decompressor on the HTTP path; there is none, per proxysettings.tsx:49.
- burpsy-react-ui-am6 (P2) — don't log out-of-scope items: needs a retention decision in the relay, not a display filter.

What remains uniquely here after those three: the HTTP/1.0-vs-1.1 forcing, Connection: close, strip Proxy-* headers, suppress error messages, and the web-interface section. Suggest re-scoping the body to those, since they are the ones that are genuinely just switches.

title: ui: Match & Replace original/auto-modified message preview absent
description: Audit gap #44/#45 (PlumOtter parity audit 2026-08-27). matchreplace.tsx has inline edit of match/replace/comment and move/duplicate/delete, but no side-by-side 'original message' vs 'auto-modified' preview per rule. Verified absent: grep preview|original message|auto-modified in matchreplace.tsx returns no matches.

comments.author: AuditProxy
comments.text:
AuditProxy, Proxy-screen parity audit 2026-08-27 — this issue's premise is false at HEAD, and its grep method is why.

The preview it asks for EXISTS: pages/matchreplace.tsx:399-452 is a "Draft test" card with side-by-side editors — "Sample input" (:433-443) and "Transformed output" (:444-450) — plus a changed/no-change badge at :408 and a "Test draft" button at :427 that applies the draft rules server-side via useTestMatchReplace (:77). That is an original-vs-auto-modified preview.

The body's verification reads: "grep preview|original message|auto-modified in matchreplace.tsx returns no matches." Correct, and misleading — the feature is labelled "Sample input" / "Transformed output" / "Draft test". This is the label-grep failure, not an absence: the capability was searched for by Burp's wording rather than by what it does.

Suggest closing as FALSE, or re-scoping to the one thing that genuinely differs: the test panel is per-RULE-SET (it runs the whole draft against one sample), whereas Burp previews per rule. If that per-rule distinction is what is wanted, the title should say so, because as written the issue invites someone to build a second preview beside the one that already ships.

Not to be confused with burpsy-react-ui-c05, which I filed for a different claim: history does not RETAIN original bytes for real captured traffic, so a rule's effect on live traffic cannot be reviewed after the fact. That one is outstanding.

title: wshistory: no filter surface at all — not just Bambda
description:
RE-TITLED, because the original framing named the one thing that was already decided against and understated the actual gap.

The Bambda half is NOT a gap: burpsy has its own typed query DSL and 8sa closed the Bambda question in burpsy's favour on the grounds that a second filter language would give two ways to say the same thing and stop the query box being the single statement of what is filtered. Filing 'no Bambda filter' invites someone to build the thing that decision refused.

THE REAL GAP, verified: wshistory.tsx contains ZERO matches for 'filter'. Not a DSL box, not a toolbar select, not a search field — nothing. History gained per-column filters composing into the DSL in 5ffe51b and the WS page got none of it, so an operator with a busy WebSocket connection has no way to narrow the frame list at all. That is worse than missing Bambda and is the thing to fix.

## Shape of the work

The DSL is the wrong tool as it stands: internal/query's fields are host/method/path/mime/status/body/length/duration/header/extension/params/highlight/comment — all HTTP-shaped. A frame has a direction, an opcode, a payload and a connection, and none of those are expressible. So this is either:

1. a plain toolbar filter over the frame list (direction, opcode, payload substring), which is small and honest; or
2. new DSL fields for frames, which means deciding what a Queryable is for a frame — the crawler's frontierRow precedent says an adapter that cannot answer a field must report absent rather than guess, and a frame cannot answer  or  at all.

Prefer (1) first. It is the operator-facing gap, and (2) is a grammar decision that should not be made to serve one page.
acceptance_criteria: The WebSocket history frame list can be narrowed by direction, opcode and payload substring; an empty result is distinguishable from an empty connection; the Bambda framing is not reintroduced.

title: ui: Scope advanced scope control and save-to-library absent
description: Audit gap #37/#38 (PlumOtter parity audit 2026-08-27). scope.tsx has no advanced scope-rule builder (protocol/host/port/file/param include-exclude expressions) and no 'save to scope library' action. Verified absent: grep advanced|library|save to in scope.tsx returns no matches.

comments.author: AuditDashTarget
comments.text:
Independent re-verification at HEAD (655a777), AuditDashTarget Dashboard/Target audit 2026-08-27.
**Part of this issue's premise is now wrong, and the accurate gap is narrower than stated.**

The description says scope.tsx "has no advanced scope-rule builder (protocol/host/port/file/param
include-exclude expressions)". Those arms DO exist: `pages/scope.tsx:163-194` has fields for Rule kind
(Include/Exclude), Host pattern, Port, Path prefix and Protocol, and the table renders all five
(`:98-130`). The wire carries them too (`:54-61`). As written, this issue would be closed by work that
has already shipped.

The absence grep quoted — "grep advanced|library|save to in scope.tsx returns no matches" — is true but
does not support the stated claim; it only shows the words are absent, not the capability. This is the
grep-hit-counting failure mode: the labels differ, the arms are there.

What is actually missing, verified in `internal/core/scope.go`:

1. **Rule arms are literal, not regex.** `NewScopeRule` compiles the host pattern as a glob — `*` and
   `?` translated, everything else `regexp.QuoteMeta`'d (`:55-63`) — and the path is
   `strings.HasPrefix(path, *r.PathPrefix)` at `:101`, a literal prefix. Burp specifies a **regular
   expression per URL component**: `map_root.tsv` class `burp.Zg5d`, *"Specify a regular expression to
   match each URL component, or leave blank to match any item."*
2. **No IP ranges.** Same Burp class: `Host or IP range:`, `Enter regex, IP range or leave blank`.
   `ScopeRule.Matches` (`:83-89`) only regex-matches the host string.
3. **No simple/advanced mode.** Burp ships both — `burp.Zry2`: `enable advanced scope control` /
   `disable advanced scope control` — where simple mode is a flat list of URL prefixes
   (`prefix for in-scope URLs`). burpsy is permanently in a middle state: more than prefixes, less
   than regex. The mode a Burp user meets first has no equivalent.

Suggest rewriting the title and body to "scope rule arms are literal globs and prefixes, not regex, and
IP ranges are unsupported", which is closable on evidence. The save-to-library half is a separate claim
and I have not verified it.

Three smaller scope gaps outside this issue's premise are filed separately, one claim each:
burpsy-react-ui-k5l (a rule cannot be edited), plus the disable-a-rule and Paste-URL/load-from-file
issues.

title: ui: Site map second-view switch (URL vs crawl-paths) and passive-scan controls absent
description: Audit gap #35/#36 (PlumOtter parity audit 2026-08-27). sitemap.tsx has no read-only/items/queued/processed indicators and no view switch. NOTE: crawl-paths VIEW (#16) and passive-scan branch controls (#17) were already filed as burpsy-react-ui-tix/p09 and closed. This issue tracks only the remaining sitemap read-only indicator + items/queued/processed counters, which are still absent (grep read.only indicator|items|queued in sitemap.tsx returns only the exchange inspector's readOnlyNote, no tree-level indicator).
close_reason: INVALID — its own title asserts what now exists. sitemap.tsx has the URL/Crawl-paths view switch (565c6c7, tix) and the 'Passive scan branch' control (655a777, p09), both in the page header. The body acknowledges this and narrows to 'read-only indicator + items/queued/processed counters', but a tracker is read by title, and a title claiming an absent feature that shipped an hour earlier will be acted on. The narrowed remainder does not survive either: the header already carries three badges — nodes, exchanges, and 'in flight' when non-zero — which are Burp's items/queued/processed under different names, and the grep behind the claim ('read.only indicator|items|queued') tested for Burp's vocabulary rather than for the capability. 'Read-only site map' is a Burp state burpsy has no equivalent of: nothing here makes the tree read-only, so there is no state to indicate. File something narrower if a specific counter is genuinely missing, with the number an operator cannot currently see.

title: ui: Dashboard pause/resume and listener-status controls absent
description: Audit gap #32/#33 (PlumOtter parity audit 2026-08-27). Dashboard.tsx has a live task-progress bar (line 117) but no pause/resume control for a running task and no listener up/down status indicator. Burp's dashboard exposes both. Verified absent: grep for pause|resume|listener status|telemetry in dashboard.tsx returns no matches.

comments.author: AuditDashTarget
comments.text:
Independent re-verification at HEAD (655a777), AuditDashTarget Dashboard/Target audit 2026-08-27.
Confirming the pause/resume half and adding evidence that argues this is a capability gap rather
than P3 polish.

Server-side, not just UI: `internal/web/server.go:819` registers
`s.mux.HandleFunc("/api/tasks/", s.handleTaskCancel)` as the ONLY task-mutation route, and
`internal/web/api_tasks_cancel.go:25` parses only the `/cancel` suffix. So pause/resume is absent from
the wire too — this is not a control missing from an existing capability, it is the capability.

Burp side, for the record: `dashboardPauseAllTasksButton`, `dashboardResumeAllTasksButton`
("Pause all tasks" / "Resume task processing"), `dashboardTasksPausedWarningBar`
("Task execution is paused") and per-task `taskListEntryResumeButton` — `map_root.tsv` classes
`burp.Zr_o` and `burp.Zr__`. Note Burp has both a suite-wide pause and a per-task one.

Suggest re-pricing to P2: an operator running a long crawl who needs to do manual testing through the
proxy has only "cancel and lose the crawl" available.

One scope correction to the description: it says "no pause/resume control ... and no listener up/down
status indicator", which bundles two claims. The pause/resume half is confirmed. I did not audit the
listener indicator (Proxy is not my screen set), so that half is still unverified here — worth
splitting so the issue can be closed on evidence.

The remainder of Burp's `taskListEntryOptionsMenu` — rename, delete task, scan again, settings, show
details — is filed separately as burpsy-react-ui-r6q to keep this one to a single claim.

title: ui: whitespace reformat of 5 files hides the substance of the ContextMenu change
description:
The uncommitted ContextMenu work re-indents five whole files from 2-space to 1-space, which buries
the substance and has already caused one outage-class corruption.

## Measurement

    git diff --stat      -> 2247 insertions, 2180 deletions
    git diff -w --stat   ->  124 insertions,   83 deletions

Files: `intercept.tsx`, `matchreplace.tsx`, `organizer.tsx`, `scope.tsx`, `session.tsx`.

So ~96% of the diff is whitespace. The three real defects filed alongside this issue
(burpsy-react-ui-3g5, -e64, -aih) all live in that remaining 4%, and none of them is findable by
reading the diff as presented.

## It has already broken a file

Earlier the same reformatting pass left `intercept.tsx` non-parsing: re-indented wholesale, a
`SplitPane` prop dropped, `TS1003` at line 609, 593 open braces against 565 closes on a 656-line
file. It was restored from HEAD. The current pass parses (`npx tsc --noEmit` exit 0), which is luck
rather than a property of the process.

## The gate that misses it

`bun run build` **succeeded** on the corrupted copy — esbuild strips types without checking them. Any
workflow that treats a green `bun run build` as verification will ship a file that cannot compile.
`npx tsc --noEmit` is the only gate that catches this and belongs in whatever runs before a UI commit.

## Ask

1. Land reformatting as its own commit, separate from behaviour, or not at all.
2. If the 1-space indentation is intentional as a house style, apply it once across the tree in a
   single mechanical commit that touches nothing else, and pin it in a formatter config so it stops
   arriving as a side effect of feature work.
3. Add `npx tsc --noEmit` ahead of `bun run build` in the UI pre-commit path.
acceptance_criteria: Reformatting is separated from behavioural change; tsc --noEmit runs before bun run build in the UI commit path.
close_reason: Done in ecfe2bd, by not landing the reformat at all. The behavioural change was reapplied onto HEAD's 2-space formatting rather than committed on top of the 2-space-to-1-space reindentation: git diff --stat and git diff -w --stat on intercept.tsx are now IDENTICAL at 63 lines, which is the measurable form of what this issue asked for. The other five files (scope, matchreplace, session, advisories, dashboard) had already been reverted to HEAD by their author. Worth recording as the reason this mattered rather than as a style preference: the fixContent_length regression was one character in the middle of six hundred reformatted lines, and that is why it survived a review request that claimed tsc was clean. Item 3 of the issue — running tsc before bun run build — is not enforced by a hook and remains a process matter; noted here rather than claimed.

description:

Proven interactively on the live console: ran Sequencer, Collaborator, Extender via the palette, re-opened — top three are Extender, Collaborator, Sequencer (most recent first). 4 unit tests pin the ledger contract (167 pass / 0 fail / 361 expect). This is useful if you want to step through items in the Proxy history, to look for a particular expression in the responses."

title: decoder: transforms apply to the whole input only — no per-selection transform and no colour-coding of the applied encoding

title: repeater: tab strip has no scrolling/wrapped view toggle, no drag-reorder, and individual (ungrouped) tabs cannot be colored
description:
Three small tab-strip affordances Burp's Repeater has and burpsy's does not. Grouped here because
each alone is cosmetic; together they are the difference between a strip that scales to the dozens
of tabs a real engagement accumulates and one that does not.

## Burp-side evidence

`/root/burp-re/in/extract/resources/Documentation/burp/documentation/desktop/tools/repeater/managing-tabs.html`:

> **Switch tab view** - Use the tab view toggle in the top-right corner to choose from two different
> views: **Scrolling view** - a single, scrollable row ... [or a] drop-down list of open tabs ...
> **Wrapped view** - wrap tabs onto multiple rows.

`groups.html`: "Select a group color. The group's tabs are highlighted with this color on the tab
bar." Burp also lets tabs be dragged to reorder and dragged between groups.

## burpsy-side evidence (`internal/web/ui/src/pages/repeater.tsx`)

1. **No scrolling/wrapped view toggle.** `ungrouped.map(renderTabTrigger)` renders one flat
   `tabs-list` row; with many tabs it overflows with no scroll affordance and no overflow dropdown.
2. **No drag to reorder / drag into a group.** Order is fixed to `state.repeaterTabs`; moving a tab
   into a group is menu-only (`setRepeaterTabGroup`). There is no `draggable`/`onDrag*` anywhere in
   the page or a `moveRepeaterTab` reorder action in `store.ts`.
3. **Individual tabs cannot be colored.** Color lives on the *group* (`group.color`, the colored
   border); an ungrouped tab has no color. Burp colors per group too, but exposes it as a tab-bar
   highlight; a single ungrouped tab still cannot be marked.

## Not in scope of this issue

Per-tab *settings* (Burp's blue settings icon + "Restore global default") are already at parity:
the Config trigger shows an override count `Config (N)` and offers "Reset overrides"
(`SendOptionsPanel`). Rename (double-click) and duplicate are also present.

title: ui: no 'Save items' — selected exchanges cannot be exported as request/response pairs, only the request alone
description:
## Claim
"Copy request to file" saves the request only. Burp's "Save items" saves the selected request/response pairs together in a structured format, which is what an operator hands to a colleague or attaches to a report.

## Burp-side evidence
- `tools/context-menu.html` (bundled docs), universal menu options: **Save items** — *"Saves the selected items in the specified format"*. Listed separately from **Copy to file** — *"Enables you to select a file and copy the contents of the current message to that file"* — so Burp has both, and they are different actions.

## burpsy-side evidence
- burpsy has the Copy-to-file half only: `lib/actions.ts:808` `{ id: "to-file", label: "Copy request to file", ... }` -> `lib/actions.ts:685-698` `copyRequestToFile`, which fetches `exchange.request` alone (`fetchRaw(exchange.request)`, `:687`) and downloads it as `.txt`. The response is never included.
- Absence grep: `grep -rli 'Save item' --include=*.tsx --include=*.ts burpsy-go/internal/web/ui/src/` -> **no files**. Positive control: `grep -rli 'Copy URL'` -> `pages/logger.tsx lib/actions.ts`.
- Report export exists but is a different object: `app.tsx:437-443` exports findings reports (HTML/JSON/SARIF), not selected exchanges.

## Classification
CAPABILITY GAP, low frequency.

## What an operator cannot do
Export one or more selected exchanges, request and response together, as a single artefact. Today: download the request, then separately copy the response bytes out of the editor.
acceptance_criteria: The row menu offers saving the selected exchange(s) with both request and response in one file in a documented format.
close_reason: Implemented in a1c8ada. 'Save request and response' in the shared copy group: one labelled file (REQUEST + RESPONSE sections), missing response saves labelled rather than refusing. Verified live by intercepting the download blob: 678 bytes with real request/response bytes under their markers, confirming toast.

title: ui: no 'Add to site map' action — the site map is populated only by observed traffic
description:
## Claim
There is no "Add to site map" action. Burp lets you push a selected item onto the site map; in burpsy the site map is populated only by observed proxy traffic and crawls.

## Burp-side evidence
- `tools/context-menu.html` (bundled docs), universal menu options: **Add to site map** — *"Adds the selected items to the project scope"* [sic — the table's description column; the option name and its effect are the site map].

## burpsy-side evidence
- Absence grep over the whole UI tree: `grep -rli 'Add to site map' --include=*.tsx --include=*.ts burpsy-go/internal/web/ui/src/` -> **no files**. Same-tree positive control: `grep -rli 'Copy URL'` -> `pages/logger.tsx lib/actions.ts`.
- The shared row menu's organise and scope groups (`lib/actions.ts:811-827`) offer Add to Organizer, Filter history by host, Open URL in browser, Add host to scope, Audit exchange, and two crawl scopes — no site-map insert.

## Classification
CAPABILITY GAP, low frequency.

## What an operator cannot do
Put a URL they know about onto the site map without sending traffic to it. Note this interacts with the documented append-only store property (`lib/reference.ts:349-351`: *"the site map adds and never removes. A host on the map was observed at some point — that is not evidence it is reachable now."*) — an operator-inserted node would break that invariant's current meaning.

## Decision needed
Whether an operator-added node is acceptable at all given the disclosure above. If yes, it needs to be distinguishable from an observed node on the map, or the disclosure needs rewording. Worth answering before implementing.
acceptance_criteria: A decision is recorded on whether operator-inserted site-map nodes are allowed; if allowed, the row menu offers 'Add to site map' and inserted nodes are visually distinguishable from observed ones.

title: ui: no 'Copy links' action to extract URLs from a selected response
description:
## Claim
There is no "Copy links" action. Burp parses the selected items for links and copies them, which is the standard way to harvest URLs out of a response for a wordlist or a crawl seed set.

## Burp-side evidence
- `tools/context-menu.html` (bundled docs), universal menu options: **Copy links** — *"Parses the selected items for links and copies them to the clipboard"*.

## burpsy-side evidence
- Absence grep over the whole UI tree: `grep -rli 'Copy links' --include=*.tsx --include=*.ts burpsy-go/internal/web/ui/src/` -> **no files**. Same-tree positive control: `grep -rli 'Copy URL'` -> `pages/logger.tsx lib/actions.ts`.
- The copy group in the shared row menu is `lib/actions.ts:802-810`: Copy URL, Copy as curl, Copy exchange id, Copy request to file. No links extraction.
- burpsy does parse links elsewhere — the crawler has a frontier — so the capability exists server-side but is not offered as a clipboard action on a response.

## Classification
CAPABILITY GAP, low frequency but cheap.

## What an operator cannot do
Pull every link out of a captured response in one action, to feed a content-discovery run or a manual review list.
acceptance_criteria: The row and editor menus offer 'Copy links', which extracts the links from the selected response body and copies them one per line.
close_reason: Implemented in 0415420. 'Copy links' in the shared row-menu copy group (all tools). extractLinks harvests quoted attrs + bare absolute URLs + CSS url(), deduped, order-preserving, as-found; javascript:/mailto:/data:/fragments/trailing punctuation excluded (5 unit tests). Verified live: real page harvest toasted 'Copied 3 links from #0'.

title: docs: the command-palette note says Burp has no default binding — Burp's own docs say Ctrl+K, which burpsy already matches
description:
## Claim
Two documents state that Burp's command palette has no default hotkey, or that it is Ctrl+Shift+P. Burp's own shipped documentation says the default is Ctrl+K — which is exactly what burpsy binds, so a correct parity claim is being recorded as a divergence.

## Burp-side evidence
`tools/command-palette.html` (Burp 2026.7.1 bundled docs, `/root/burp-re/in/extract/resources/Documentation/burp/documentation/desktop/`):
> *"**If** you have already assigned the `Ctrl+K` or `Cmd+K` hotkey to another command, the command palette isn't assigned a default hotkey. Set one manually in **Settings > User interface > Hotkeys**."*

Ctrl+K is the default; the no-default case is the conditional fallback when the operator has already taken that chord.

## burpsy-side evidence (the two wrong statements)
1. `lib/shortcuts.ts:82` — `{ id: "nav.palette", ..., defaultChord: "mod+k", ..., note: "Burp ships its palette with no default binding at all" }`. The binding is right; the note is wrong, and it is rendered to operators beside the row (`app.tsx:58`, `pages/settings.tsx:1266`).
2. `/root/burp-re/BURP_SUITE_UI_UX_SPECIFICATION.md` section 3.2 and section 5.2 both give the palette trigger as `Ctrl + Shift + P` / `Cmd + Shift + P`. The spec is wrong here and the bundled docs supersede it.

## Classification
Documentation defect. No code change to the binding — `mod+k` is exact parity.
